ar.name: جرة.
description: جرة كاملة ذات جسم منتفخ وعنق ضيق وشفة مقلوبة إلى الخارج، وقد تم تزجيج كامل الجرة، عدا حلقة القاعدة، وزخرفتها بطلاء ذي بريق معدني. تبدأ الزخرفة ذات البريق المعدني عند ثلث المسافة من القاعدة، وتنقسم إلى أطواق أفقية. يتضمن الطوق الأسفل أشرطة مجدولة ملونة بتحفظ، يعلوها شريط أعرض ذو زخارف قلبية الشكل، أما الطوق في الأعلى، فتظهر عليه خمس سمكات، حراشفها والتفاصيل الأخرى محززة ضمن الطلاء ذي البريق المعدني لتظهر باللون الأبيض. العنق مزخرف بطوق من المثلثات والنقاط. تذكر زخارف الجرة بالفن القبطي، إذ تعتبر الأسماك نموذجاً مسيحياً تقليدياً، وعادة ما يتم استخدام نماذج الأسماك والطيور في المنسوجات القبطية المبكرة.

مزهرية مزخرفة بالزخارف البرّاقة، تحتوي على شريط من الأسماك النافرة، التي تحيط بكتف الإناء. تُعتبر الأسماك الموجودة على هذا الإناء دليلاً على أنه صُنع ليتمَّ استخدامه من قبل المسيحيين الأقباط، الذين اشتهروا باستخدام الأسماك كأهم التصاميم التي يزخرفون بها منسوجاتهم.
keywords: زخرفة تصويرية؛ ماء.

en.name: Jar.
description: A virtually undamaged jar with a swelling body and a narrow neck with an everted rim. Except for the foot-ring the whole jar is glazed and decorated with lustre painting. The lustre decoration begins about a third of the way up from the foot and is divided into horizontal bands. The bottom band features interlaced ribbons painted in reserve; above them, a wider band has heart-shaped palmettes. At the top is a band which displays five fish, their scales and other details scratched through the lustre to appear in white. The neck is decorated with a band of triangles and dots. The jar’s decoration is reminiscent of Coptic art: fish are a traditionally Christian motif, and motifs using repeated fish (and birds) are found in early Coptic textiles.

A large vase with extensive decoration in lustre, including a band of prominent fish around the shoulder. The presence of the fish may indicate that the vase was made for use in the Coptic Christian community, as early Coptic textiles feature similar repetitions of fish-motifs.
keywords: figurative decoration; water; Christian themes

es.name: Jarrón.
description:
Intacto jarrón de cuerpo abultado y cuello estrecho con boca redondeada. Está totalmente vidriado y decorado en reflejo metálico, excepto en la base. La decoración está formada por bandas horizontales que ocupan los dos tercios superiores del cuerpo de la pieza. La banda inferior consiste en un entrelazo pintado en reserva; la banda intermedia, más ancha, presenta palmetas en forma de corazón; en la superior hay cinco peces cuyas escamas y demás detalles están esgrafiados en la capa de reflejo metálico para que aparezcan más claros. El cuello está adornado con una franja de triángulos y puntos.  
La decoración de este jarrón recuerda el arte copto: los peces son un tradicional motivo cristiano, y en los primeros tejidos coptos se encuentran peces o aves repetidos.

Jarrón con extensa decoración en reflejo metálico en la que destaca una banda de grandes peces alrededor del cuello. La presencia de este motivo indica que el jarrón perteneció a la comunidad copta, pues en los primeros tejidos coptos aparece la misma repetición de dibujos de peces.
keywords: decoración figurativa; agua

fr.name: Jarre.
description: Jarre pratiquement intacte à corps renflé et col étroit à bord retourné. À l'exception de l'anneau du pied, la totalité de l'objet est vernissée et décorée d'une peinture lustrée. Le décor lustré qui débute à un tiers environ de la hauteur est divisé en bandes horizontales. La bande inférieure présente des rubans entrelacés peints en réserve. Au-dessus, une bande plus large est ornée de palmettes en forme de cœur. La bande supérieure comporte cinq poissons dont les écailles et autres détails sont esgrafiés dans le lustre pour apparaître en blanc. Le col est décoré d'un bandeau de triangles et de points. Ce décor rappelle l'art copte : le poisson est par tradition un ornement chrétien et des motifs à poissons répétés (oiseaux également) se trouvent dans les plus anciens textiles coptes.

Grande jarre à complet décor lustré comprenant une bande supérieure ornée de poissons autour de l'épaule, ce qui indique sans doute que la jarre a été exécutée pour la communauté chrétienne copte, car les premiers textiles coptes présentent une semblable répétition de motifs de poissons.
keywords: Décoration figurative ; eau

ar.name: قارورة الضرس الزجاجية
description: يرتبط اسم هذه الحاوية الصغيرة المصنوعة من الزجاج المجروش بشكلها، الذي يشبه الضرس بأقدامها الأربعة التي تتخذ شكل الوتد. وحيث إن هذه القنينات مُزودة في الأساس بسدادة، فإنها على الأرجح كانت تستخدم لحفظ وتوصيل العطور والزيوت والخلاصات المستخدمة في مستحضرات التجميل الباهظة الثمن. وقد اعتاد المستهلكون الأثرياء اقتناء قنينات مصممة بنفس الشكل من العاج أو المعدن أو البلور الصخري (حجر المرو).
dates: القرن الثالث- الرابع الهجري/ القرن التاسع - العاشر الميلادي
keywords: تجميل

en.name: Molar glass flacon
description: This tiny cut-glass container owes its name to its shape, which resembles a molar tooth with its four wedge-shaped, pointed feet. Originally provided with a stopper, these bottles were used most probably to store and convey expensive perfumes, oils and cosmetic essences. Rich consumers had the shape copied in ivory, metal or even rock crystal.
keywords: Flacon; Abbasid; Glass; cosmetic; cut-glass decoration

en.name: Memorial Volume – Dedicatory and opening ceremonies of the Chicago World's Colombian Exposition – 1893
short_description: The World's Columbian Exposition or The Chicago World's Fair was a World's Fair held in Chicago in 1893 to celebrate the 400th anniversary of Christopher Columbus' arrival in the New World in 1492. The fair was an influential social and cultural event to which the Ottoman Empire had been invited. It displayed raw materials and agricultural products at the exposition, as well as handicraft products and plant products belonging to the palace revenue. The 1893 Chicago Exhibition was a big success for the Chamber of Commerce. The Head of the Chamber of Commerce, Azaryan Efendi, was assigned to the head of the commission, which was formed in Istanbul for the Chicago Exhibition.
keywords: International Exhibitions; exposition; fair

en.name: Pearl Trader’s Pearl Pouch
short_description: This colourful little bag would have contained a pearl merchant's most priced pearls. Many such bags could be found in a pearl merchant's chest, each one containing a particular grade of pearl, determined by their shape, colour and level of surface perfection.
holder: Sharjah Maritime Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
materials: Cotton fabric with multi-coloured, cotton embroidery threads

en.name: Asmalyk
description:
Turkmen organized in tribal groups, living nomadic and semi-nomadic lives in Central Asia. Their textiles, woven to be functional as well as decorative and ceremonial, were their most treasured possessions. Considering they travelled throughout the year with their herds, they used lightweight textiles for protection and transportation. A majority of their textiles were made by women on portable ground looms and were for their family’s consumption.  
  
Among the Turkmen, it was customary for a girl of marriageable age to have woven or made all of the ceremonial items required for the wedding and her new home. These included the textiles used to decorate the camel on which she would ride from her family’s tents to that of the groom. The decorations included a pair of large weavings used to cover the flanks of the camel, one on each side. During the ride, the bride was concealed within a covered litter (palanquin) carried by a camel decorated with her work. The palanquin was roofed over with curved wooden rods and covered with a white curtain decorated with tassels. The decorations outside included a pair of large weavings used to cover the flanks of the camel, one on each side. This camel trapping not only advertised the bride’s dexterity and ability as a textile artist, which was considered a crucial asset in marriage negotiations, but also symbolized the transition to a new life as a wife.
holder: The George Washington University Museum and The Textile Museum
keywords: Wool; Turkmen; Central Asia
materials: Wool; knotted pile rug; asymmetrical knot; open right
partner: The George Washington University Museum and The Textile Museum

cs.name: Kašna Parnas
description: “Umělecké památky” nemají jen své objednavatele a autory, ale i realizátory – výkonné umělce (kameníky, stavitele, řemeslníky) nebo také úředníky. Stavbu kašny spravoval brněnský senátor J. I. Dechau. Urgoval architekta, řídil řemeslníky a po dokončení stavby nechal vyrýt grafický list, v němž se hrdě uvádí dole pod obrazem. Je možná také oním mužem, vysvětlujícím obsah kašny šlechtické společnosti.

en.name: Parnassus Fountain
description: “Art monuments” have their clients and designers as well as those who build them, the stonemasons, builders and other craftsmen, and sometimes bureaucrats as well. The construction of the fountain was administered by the Senator of Brno, J. I. Dechau. He supervised the architect and managed the builders and, when it was completed, he had a print engraved in which he proudly stated his name under the picture. He may be the man depicted here explaining the fountain’s symbolism to a group of aristocrats.

ar.name: أربعة دنانير ذهبية تعود للعصر الأموي
description: يضم المتحف مجموعة مهمة من العملات المعدنية الخاصة بعصر صدر الإسلام، تشمل الدنانير الأموية على غرار هذه القطع. وفي عام 77 هجريًا/ 696 ميلاديًا، أمر الخليفة الحاكم عبد الملك بإصدار عملة إسلامية جديدة تمامًا، تحمل في الأساس كتابات قرآنية تدل على وحدانية الله وقدرته المطلقة وتؤكد على أن محمدًا هو رسول الله.
dates: أواخر القرن الأول- أوائل القرن الثاني الهجري/ أواخر القرن السابع- أوائل القرن الثامن الميلادي

en.name: Four Umayyad gold dinars
description: The Museum houses an important collection of early Islamic coins, including Umayyad dinars likes these ones.  In AH 77/ AD 696, the ruling caliph Abd al-Malik ordered the issue of a brand new, truly Islamic coinage, carrying mainly qur’anic inscriptions emphasizing the oneness and omnipotence of Allah and confirming Muhammad as the Prophet of God.
dates: Hegira late 1st – early 2nd century / AD late 7th – early 8th century
keywords: Dinar; Abd al-Malik; Gold, numismatics; coin; coinage; calligraphy; inscription; kufic

en.name: Jar
description:
This jar is a large glass cup, which was most possibly used for store liquids. This one is made of pale blue-green translucent glass by applying the free-blowing technique. It has a globular body, sloping shoulder; its rim is rounded and turned outwards; and its neck goes concave to the body. It is in an intact situation, but some soil-encrusted weathering, blowing striations, partly flaked off dulling are also seen on the surface. The jar is light green in colour, with a bluish tingle on some parts.  
After the free-blowing technique has been found, possibly around in the first quarter of the 1st century BC, the mould-blowing technique has developed and the desired glass forms and patterns were obtained by blowing into glass, terracotta, stone, metal or wood moulds. The melt at the end of the blowing rod is inflated in two or more pieces of the container until it covers the mould. The use of angular and patterned moulds has usually made it unnecessary to apply additional ornaments. With this technique, mass production of glasses with the same form, measurement, and decoration can be produced by using a single mould. In the form of quadrangular shaped moulds, the glass workshop's or the manufacturer's names were added by applying letters and symbols on the pedestal portion. Glassware that has been blown into a mould whose interior has a raised pattern so that the object shows the pattern with a concavity on the inside, underlying the convexity on the outside. Pattern moulds are not used to impart the final form to the object.
keywords: Glass in Asia Minor; Roman period; casting; blowing; mould-blowing

de.name: Magnuskapelle
description: Die als ovale Mausoleumsrotunde angelegte Grabkapelle des hl. Magnus soll legendär auf dessen Kirchengründung zurückgehen und ist somit Pilgerziel und Traditionsort der Abtei zugleich. Zur würdigen Marmorausstattung gehören Bildwerke des Verehrten sowie der Ordensheiligen Benedikt, Scholastika, Gallus und Columban.
dates:
1712 Bau  
1717 Altar einschließlich Sitzfigur des hl. Magnus

1751/52 Gewölbedekoration

en.name: Chapel of St. Magnus
description: Designed as an oval mausoleum rotunda, the Burial Chapel of St. Magnus legendarily goes back to his foundation of the church and is, therefore, a pilgrimage destination as well as a traditional site for the abbey itself. The dignified marble decorations include sculptures of Magnus of Füssen and saints of the Benedictine Order: St. Benedict, St. Scholastica, St. Gallus and St. Columbanus.
dates:
1712: construction  
1717: altar, including the sitting figure of St. Magnus  
1724: statues of saints  
1751/52: decoration of the vaults

en.name: Alessandro Manzoni
holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History

en.name: Dar Ben Abdallah
short_description: The curving hallway, richly decorated with faience pottery, marble and stucco, leads to an open-air courtyard, around which there are several apartments, today housing the museum's collection. The patio is surrounded by porticos with white marble columns. The walls are decorated with Neapolitan faience pottery, above a frieze of carved plaster. At the centre of the patio sits a fountain with three basins made of marble imported from Carrara. On the first floor, a circular gallery with wood railings adds to the palace's opulent style.
history: This princely palace in the Tunis medina was built in the style of 19th century Italian royal courts, and named after its original owners, who were rich silk weavers. During the French Protectorate era it was brought by a French painter, but was then reacquired by the Tunisian state after independence, at which point it became the Musée des Arts et Traditions Populaires of the 19th century Tunisian bourgeoisie.
keywords: Architecture; Italian style; Carrara marble
partner: Higher Institute for the Study of Contemporary History of Tunisia, University of Manouba

fr.name: Dar Ben-Abdallah
short_description: L’entrée en chicane, richement décorée de faïences, de marbre et de stucs, conduit vers une cour à ciel ouvert autour de laquelle se distribuent les appartements qui abritent aujourd’hui les salles de musée. Le patio est entouré de portiques pourvus de colonnes et de chapiteaux en marbre blanc. Les murs sont revêtus de faïence napolitaine que surmonte une frise de plâtre sculpté. Une fontaine à trois vasques en marbre de Carrare enrichit le patio. A l’étage, une galerie circulaire à balustrade de bois complète la somptuosité de l’ensemble.
history: Demeure princière de la médina de Tunis, rénovée dans un style italianisant au cours du XIXe siècle, le palais porte le nom de l’un de ses anciens propriétaires, un riche tisserand en soie. Acheté par un peintre français sous le protectorat, l’Etat tunisien le rachète après l’indépendance et en fait le Musée des Arts et Traditions populaires de la bourgeoisie tunisoise du XIXe siècle.
partner: Institut Supérieur d’histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie, Université de la Manouba

ar.name: قفل
description: إن القفل بشكل أسد واقف هو في وضعية جيدة نسبيا والشكل العام للأسد يتحدد عن طرق جسمه المتطاول والفخذين البارزين التي تملك تزيين زخرفي. ويبدي الأسد رقبة طويلة نسبيا والتي في نهايتها الرأس محني للخلف بشكل بوق. والمخالب والملامح الوجهية تظهر تقريبية وليست مفصلة. خاصة الوجه لا يبدو منحوتا بيد خبيرة والعينين مشار لهما بواسطة ثقوب وهذا يعتبر على تباين قوي مع التزيين الزخرفي على الفخذين والنقش على الجوانب المنفذ بدقة عالية. والكتابة بالخط النقشي على الطرف الأيسر تقول ""البركة لصاحبه"" وعلى الطرف الأيمن يقول "" عمل محمد"".
dates: ربما القرن الحادي عشر - الثالث عشر
keywords: قفل ، مشغولة معدنية ، أسد
materials: برونز أو خليطة نحاس ، قطع صب ، موصلة ومحفورة
tags: برونز أو خليطة نحاس ، قطع صب ، موصلة ومحفورة
partner: المتحف الجامعي للفن الإسلامي / مجموعة بوميلر

en.name: Padlock
description: This lion-shaped padlock is in a relatively good state of preservation. The general appearance of the lion is determined through its elongated body and the emphasized thighs with ornamental decoration. The lion shows a relatively long neck, at the end of which and the head is a backwardly bent horn. The claws and facial features appear rough and not very detailed. Especially the face does not seem to be carved by an experienced hand. The eyes are indicated through holes. This stands in stark contrast to the ornamental decoration on the thighs and the inscription on the flanks which are executed very carefully. The *naskhi*\-inscription on the left side it says *al-baraka li-sahibihi* which translates to: Blessing to its owner; and on the right side it says *amal Muhammad* which translates to: Work of Mohammed.
holder: University Museum of Islamic Art | The Bumiller Collection
keywords: Padlock; metalwork; lion
materials: Bronze or other copper alloy. Cast parts, joint and engraved
tags: Bronze or other copper alloy. Cast parts, joint and engraved
partner: University Museum of Islamic Art | The Bumiller Collection

ar.name: طغراء (توقيع سلطاني).
description: هذه القطعة هي الطغراء الخاصة بسليمان القانوني (حكم في الفترة 926 - 73/ 1520-66)، وقد تمت كتابتها بالحبر، وزخرفتها بالغواش. وقد استعملت الطغراء في الوثائق أو الفرمانات التي كان ديوان الدولة يصدرها. يحمل هذا النموذج اسم السلطان سليمان شاه واسم أبيه سليم وعبارة ' الظافر أبداً'. وضمن العقدة الأكبر في رسم الطغراء التي تشكلت من كلمة خان، هناك تصميم مزخرف صعب التحليل، فقد تم رسم حلزونات زهرية ناعمة بالأسود والذهبي على أرضية من الزخارف الدقيقة المتموجة، وملء العقدة الداخلية بأغصان نخيل مشطورة وزهيرات، ويوجد زخارف زهرية أخرى، بالإضافة إلى الزخارف المتموجة، تملأ الفراغ بين الأجزاء السفلية من الأحرف، ويظهر التصميم الحلزوني تحت التزجيج على الخزف. لقد تم وضع أسس زخرفة الطغراء من قبل السلطان بيازيد الثاني، المتوفى عام 917/ 1512، وخلال حكم سليمان، ازداد إتقانها. ومن غير المعروف موضوع الوثيقة التي حملت هذه الطغراء.
مخطوطة (أو طغراء) لسليمان الأكبر، كُتبت بالحبر الأسود، وبالخطّ المنحني، واحتوت أيضاّ على تصاميم نباتية، بأشكال لولبية، رُسمت بالأسود والذهب.
keywords: زخرفة كتابية.

en.name: *Tughra* (imperial monogram).
description: Written in pen and illuminated in gouache, this is the *tughra* (imperial monogram) of Suleyman the Magnificent (r. AH 926–73 / AD 1520–66). *Tughra*s were used on documents, or firmans (commands) which were issued by the Diwan (Council of State). This example bears the Sultan’s name, Suleyman Shah, and that of his father, Selim, and the phrase ‘the one who is always victorious’. Within the widest loop, formed by the Han (Title), is an intricate illuminated design. Painted in black and gold are fine floral spirals set against a ground of minute cloud-scrolls. The inner loop is filled with split-palmette scrolls and florets. Further floral- and cloud-scrolls fill the space between the ascending parts of the letters. The spiral design is also found on underglaze painted ceramics. The practice of illuminating the *tughra* was established by the ruler Bayazid II (d. AH 917/ AD 1512), under Suleyman they became ever more elaborate. The subject of the document to which this *tughra* was attached is not known.

This copy of the *tughra*, or imperial monogram, of Süleyman the Magnificent is written in black pen. Contained within the curves and lines of the letters are delicate illuminated designs of floral spirals in black and gold.
keywords: Calligraphy

es.name: *Tugra* (monograma imperial)
description:
Esta es la *tugra* (monograma imperial) de Suleimán el Magnífico (r. 926-973 / 1520-1566), aquí trazada a pluma e iluminada con aguada. Estos monogramas se utilizaban en los documentos y los *firmans* (órdenes) que salían del *Diwan* o Consejo de Estado.  
Esta *tugra* incluye el nombre del sultán y el de su padre, Selim, junto con apelativo “el siempre victorioso”. El espacio comprendido dentro del trazo mayor, correspondiente al *han* o título, presenta una intrincada iluminación consistente en una elegante espiral de flores negras y doradas sobre un fondo de pequeños roleos de nubes. El espacio delimitado por el lazo interno se ha rellenado con roleos de medias palmetas y florones. El espacio entre los trazos verticales de las letras está decorado con más roleos de flores y nubes. El motivo de la espiral decoraba también cerámicas pintadas bajo vidriado. Bayazid II estableció la práctica de la iluminación de la *tugra* en el año 917 / 1512 y, bajo el sultanato de Suleimán, la técnica se hizo más elaborada. Se desconoce el contenido del documento en el que se utilizó este monograma.

Esta copia de *tugra* o monograma imperial de Suleimán el Magnífico está trazada en tinta negra. Los espacios entre los trazos de las letras están delicadamente iluminados con espirales de flores pintadas en negro y oro.
dates: Hacia 956 de la Hégira / 1550 d. C.
keywords: caligrafía

fr.name: Tughra (monogramme impérial).
description: Dessiné à la plume et enluminé de gouache, ce *tughra* (monogramme impérial) est celui de Soliman le Magnifique (r. 926-973 H / 1520-1566 J.-C.). Les *tughras* étaient utilisés sur les documents, ou firmans, émis par le Divan (Conseil de l'État). Cet exemple porte le nom du sultan, Soliman Chah, et celui de son père Selim, ainsi que l'expression “celui qui est toujours victorieux.” La plus grande boucle, formée par le *han* (le titre), est occupée par un complexe fond enluminé. Des spirales de tiges de fleurs peintes en noir et or se détachent sur un fond de minuscules enroulements de nuages. La boucle interne est remplie de rinceaux, de demi-palmettes et de fleurons. D'autres enroulements floraux et nuageux comblent l'espace entre les parties ascendantes des lettres. Le motif de la spirale se trouve également sur diverses céramiques vernissées. La pratique d'enluminer les *tughras* fut lancée par Bayézid Ier (m. 917 H / 1512 J.-C.) et se sophistiqua de plus en plus sous Soliman. L'objet du document auquel était attaché ce *tughra* est inconnu.

Cette copie du *tughra* ou monogramme impérial du sultan Soliman le Magnifique est écrite à l'encre noire. Remplissant les courbes et les lignes des lettres, des spirales florales sont délicatement enluminées en noir et or.
keywords: calligraphie

en.name: Azurite
short_description: Two aggregates of azurite prismatic crystals with a radial distribution. Azurite is a copper carbonate mineral, of chemical formula Cu3(CO3)2(OH)2. Its name comes from the antiquity for its deep blue colour after the Arabian azure that came from the Persian lazhward. Azurite crystals conform to the monoclinic system of symmetry. In this sample they are prismatic, opaque and their faces present striations. The lustre is vitreous. Azurite was used as a blue pigment for centuries, providing a wide range of blues. It is also used as jewellery and as an ornamental stone. As a secondary mineral found in the oxidized portions of copper deposits, the presence of Azurite is a good surface indicator of the presence of copper ores. This sample was collected at the Touissit Mine, near Oudja, Morocco.
holder: National Museum of Natural History and Science (MUHNAC) / Museums of the University of Lisbon
keywords: Azurite; carbonate mineral; monoclinic system; copper; pigment; jewellery; National Museum of Natural History and Science; University of Lisbon
partner: National Museum of Natural History and Science (MUHNAC) / Museums of the University of Lisbon

en.name: Camel cover
description: Because of their comparatively low weight, their durability, multifunctionality and their versatility in design, flatweaves and pile weavings were of great importance for a nomadic or semi-nomadic lifestyle. Large tent bags, throws, or hangings were prominently displayed, especially on treks. This kilim belongs to a group of pieces that were used as camel covers. When thrown over a loaded animal, the large-patterned sections hang down on either side, while the solid red centre section envelops the humps and back. The surface design, coloration and patterning of the piece are characteristic of southwestern Anatolia and refer to the Fethiye region. A full description of how such pieces were used and their design was illustrated in detail by Harald Böhmer in 2004 (English edition 2008). The Dresden piece is in excellent condition. It shows a clear, skilful pattern and colour design and appealing, well-balanced details, such as the bright, lateral line pattern separating the zigzag of the red background and blue border.
holder: Museum für Völkerkunde Dresden (Ethnological Museum Dresden), Dresden State Art Collections
keywords: Animal decoration
materials: Wool; slit tapestry weave, interlock weave, floating wefts, wrapping wefts (contour thread)
tags: slit tapestry weave, interlock weave, floating wefts, wrapping wefts (contour thread)
partner: Dresden State Art Collections, Museum für Völkerkunde Dresden (Ethnological Museum)

ar.name: شكل يمثّل حيواناً ثديّاً.
description:
يشبه هذا الحيوان الثدي فصيلة البقريّات التي ليس لها قرون أو فرس نهر ينقصه ذيل قد قُصّر. كما أنّ الأجزاء السفليّة من القوائم الخلفيّة وإحدى القائمتين الأماميّتين هي ناقصة أيضاً. نلاحظ عند رؤية الحيوان من الواجهةً أنّ معالم الوجه واضحة، إلا أنّها مبسّطة جدّاً، وتقتصر على تجويف مُعَدٌّ للعين وثقب للدلالة على فتحة الأنف وخطّ مقعّر للدلالة على الفم. أمّا عند رؤيته من الخلف، فيبدو شكل الوجه غير واضح على الإطلاق. الرقبة والباقي من الجسم يبدوان شديدي الضخامة.  
يبقى استعمال هذا الحيوان الثدي غير واضح؛ هل استعمل في تزيين واجهات الجدران أو نقوش أخرى قليلة البروز؟ الإجابة شديدة الصعوبة بسبب ندرة القطع المماثلة في الفنّ الإسلامي، سواء كان ذلك في المشرق أم في المغرب. ومن المؤكّد أنّنا نمتلك تماثيل صغيرة من الصلصال تمثّل جياداً وإبلاً وبغالاً، مصدرها إيران أو سمرقند، غير أنّ وظائف هذه القطع محدّدة تماماً، إذ كانت تستعمل كألعاب أو كقطع تزيينيّة، وتختلف كلّياً عن التماثيل الصغيرة التي وُجدت في القيروان والتي تبقى فريدة في الفنّ الإسلامي.

تمثال حيواني صغير من الجص، يصور ثديا من فصيلة البقريات بدون قرون أو فرس نهر ينقصه الذيل. لم يتم تحديد استعمال هذا الثدي بسبب ندرة القطع المشابهة في الفن الإسلامي؛ والتماثيل القيروانية الصغيرة مختلفة اختلافا تاما.
dates: منتصف القرن الرابع-منتصف القرن الخامس / منتصف القرن العاشر-منتصف القرن الحادي عشر.
keywords: زخرفة تصويريّة؛ جبس منحوت؛ تمثال حيواني.

en.name: Carved figure of a mammal.
description: This mammal looks like a cow with no horns or like a hippopotamus with no tail. The lower part of the two hind legs and of one of the fore-legs is also missing. Face on, the features are quite clear but highly simplified; just rough cavities for the eyes, a hole to indicate the nostrils and a hollowed-out line for the mouth. Seen from the back, the face is totally unrecognisable. The neck and the rest of the body are thick-set. It is unclear what this animal was used for. Could it have decorated the facade of a wall or have been part of a bas-relief? This is very difficult to ascertain because of the rarity of such objects in both Occidental and Oriental Muslim art. We do have clay figures of horses, camels and mules from Iran and Samarkand, but their function is well-defined. They were used as toys or ornaments and are completely different from Kairouanese figures, which are unique in Muslim art.

This animal figure in stucco appears to be a bull with no horns or a hippopotamus with no tail. The purpose of this mammal is unknown, given the rarity of such objects in Islamic art. Kairouanese figurines are entirely different.
keywords: Figurative decoration

es.name: Figuración de mamífero.
description:
Este mamífero se asemeja a un bóvido sin cuernos o a un hipopótamo al que le falta el rabo, que está cortado. El animal carece igualmente de las partes inferiores de las dos patas posteriores y de una de las dos patas anteriores. Vistos de frente, los rasgos de la cara están bien definidos, aunque muy simplificados; se limitan a una cavidad reservada para el ojo, un orificio que insinúa la ventana nasal y un profundo surco que indica la boca. Vista desde la parte posterior, la faz es completamente irreconocible. El cuello y el resto del cuerpo son macizos.  
El uso de este mamífero aún no está claro: ¿servía para decorar fachadas de muros u otros relieves? Es difícil responder a esta pregunta, debido a la escasez de objetos análogos en el arte musulmán, tanto en Oriente como en Occidente. Existen estatuillas de arcilla que representan caballos, camellos o mulos, originarias de Irán o de Samarcanda, pero su función está definida con precisión. Servían como juguetes u objetos decorativos y son completamente diferentes de las estatuillas kairuaníes, consideradas únicas dentro del arte musulmán.

Esta estatuilla animal de estuco parece representar a un bóvido sin cuernos o un hipopótamo sin rabo. Debido a la escasez de objetos análogos en el arte musulmán, el empleo de este mamífero no ha podido determinarse. Las estatuillas kairuaníes son completamente diferentes.
dates: Mediados del siglo IV-mediados del V de la Hégira / X-XI d. C.
keywords: Decoración figurativa

fr.name: Figuration d’un mammifère.
description: Le mammifère ressemble à un bovidé sans cornes ou à un hippopotame auquel il manque la queue, qui est écourtée. Les parties inférieures des deux pattes postérieures et une des deux pattes antérieures sont également manquantes. Vus de face, les traits du visage sont bien clairs mais très simplifiés, se limitant à une cavité ménagée pour l'œil, un trou pour désigner l'orifice du nez et un trait en creux pour indiquer la bouche. Vu de derrière, le visage est complètement méconnaissable. Le cou et le reste du corps sont très massifs. L'usage de ce mammifère est peu clair ; servait-il à décorer des façades de murs ou autres bas-reliefs ? La réponse est extrêmement difficile du fait de la rareté d'objets similaires dans l'art musulman, que ce soit en Orient ou en Occident. Certes, on dispose de figurines en argile représentant des chevaux, des chameaux ou des mulets, provenant d'Iran ou de Samarcande, mais leur fonction est bien déterminée. Ils servaient de jouets ou de bibelots et diffèrent complètement des figurines kairouanaises, qui restent uniques dans l'art musulman.

Figurine animale en stuc, elle évoque un bovidé sans cornes ou un hippopotame sans queue. L'usage de ce mammifère n'a pas pu être déterminé, étant donné la rareté d'objets similaires dans l'art musulman. Les figurines kairouanaises sont complètement différentes.
dates: Milieu IVe-milieu Ve siècle de l’Hégire (milieu Xe-milieu XIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Décoration figurative
partner: Musée des arts islamiques de Kairouan

en.name: Portrait of Mihai Suţu
short_description: Mihai Suţu was the last Greek prince of Moldova. The Sublime Porte imposed Greek rulers in Wallachia and Moldavia (called “Phanariotes” because they came from Fanar, the Greek neighborhood of Istanbul) at the beginning of the 18th century and maintained them until 1821. During this period some modernizing reforms, influenced by the ideology of the Occidental Enlightenment, were introduced in the Romanian countries. The drawing was made by French artist Louis Dupré, who visited Greece, Istanbul, the Balkan Peninsula and the Near East in 1819 –1820. In the summer of 1819 he arrived in Bucharest together with Mihail Şuţu, whom he had met in Istanbul. He painted Şuţu laying on a red divan, wearing Oriental clothes.

en.name: Heraldic panel of Christoph Froschauer
description: In 1530, famous Zurich printer Christoph Froschauer donated a heraldic panel depicting three scenes from the Tell legend of the Old Confederacy: Tell’s apple-shot, Wolfenschiessen in the bath and Gessler’s hat on the pole.

en.name: The Bridge-Dam of al-Battan
description: Throwing itself over across the Medjerda, 2 km downstream from Tbourba, this bridge-dam was built around AH 1101 / AD 1690 by the Bey Mohamed, son of Murad II. It is one of the most commendable works, pierced by 16 arches that stand raised up on an invert that serves as its foundation. Gates closed the arches and raised the water-level to set the press mills in action and to irrigate the river plains. The bey ordered for a summer house to be built next to this bridge.
keywords: Water; hydraulic system; Tunisia.
partner: Ministry of Culture, National Institute of Cultural Heritage

en.name: *Asia. Athalide*
description: In this lithography, Asia is represented as a woman dressed in Turkish style. She is Athalide, the lover of Bayaceto, in a 1762 play by Jean Racine. She wears Circassian clothes. Orientalist painting usually represents Circassian women in the seraglios or harems.
keywords: Turkey; Women; Theatre

en.name: Early 1900s Villas
description:
Traditionally characterized by a rural appearance, this countryside area acquired an elegant and residential charm as several villas started to be built at the beginning of the 20th century. With their outstanding architectural quality, being harmoniously integrated with the wooded surroundings, in a few decades the villas qualified Ariccia as a coveted tourist destination for the Roman bourgeoisie.  
  
The first phase of this transformation involved the area between the area of Borgo Garibaldi in Albano and the Monumental Bridge, with a series of buildings in classic and liberty style.  
  
From the surrounding greenery emerges the white Villa Augusta (also called "Bianca" – white), built in 1910 in neoclassical style with reassembled doors from Villa Torlonia in Rome.  
  
The Villa Le Lieure, now "Hotel Villa Ariccia", preserves the remains of the Temple of Aesculapius and used to host national hero Giuseppe Garibaldi and his family for holiday periods.  
  
The Villino Barbetta was built in neo-Gothic style and Villa Amalia, as well as Villa Volterra, in Art Nouveau style. Moreover, the latter is renowned for its "garden-antiquarium" rich in archaeological finds from the Roman times, and whose belvedere (also called Altana), on which stands the statue of the Lady of the Winds, establishes an ideal dialogue with the Piazza di Corte right across the bridge.  
  
Finally, Villa Macrì was built shortly before the outbreak of the Second World War in 1939 by the then general director of the Ministry of Popular Culture.

it.name: Ville di inizio '900
description:
La comparsa di ville di indubbia qualità architettonica, armoniosamente inserite nel contesto boschivo ai margini dell’abitato, conferì in pochi decenni, a partire dai primi del ‘900, un signorile carattere residenziale ad un contesto abitativo con tradizionale vocazione rurale, qualificando Ariccia come ambita meta turistica della borghesia romana.  
  
Una prima fase di questa trasformazione interessò l’area compresa tra il borgo Garibaldi di Albano e il Ponte Monumentale, con una serie di costruzioni in stile classicheggiante e liberty. Immerse nel verde emergono la Villa Augusta (detta anche “Bianca”), costruita nel 1910 in stile neoclassico con porte rimontate provenienti da Villa Torlonia a Roma.  
  
La Villa Le Lieure, attuale “Hotel Villa Aricia”, che conserva i resti del Tempio di Esculapio e che accolse per periodi di villeggiatura, Garibaldi e la sua famiglia.  
  
Il Villino Barbetta in stile neogotico e la Villa Amalia in stile liberty come la Villa Volterra che spicca sul “giardino-antiquarium” ricco di reperti archeologici dell’Aricia romana, e che con la sua altana su cui sorge la statua della Signora dei Venti, si pone come in dialogo ideale con la Piazza di Corte dall’altra parte del ponte.  
  
La Villa Macrì, infine, fatta costruire poco prima dello scoppio della seconda guerra mondiale nel 1939, dall’allora direttore generale del Ministero della Cultura Popolare.

cs.name: *Křest sv. Augustina*
description:
Obraz zachycuje scénu, kdy sv. Augustin (354–430), jeden z církevních otců a milánský biskup, jehož spisy ovlivňovaly církevní učení jak středověké tak novověké, je zároveň se svým synem Adeodatem křtěn sv. Ambrožem. Pod­stavu křtitelnice tvoří úl, symbol církve a současně atribut sv. Ambrože.  
Ukázkový model pro obraz bočního oltáře v Jevíčku, jehož objednavatelem byl opat augustiniánského kláštera v Brně, má řadu motivů společných s Křtem knížete Bořivoje (Svatopluka?) Josefa Winterhaldera ml. (Slezské zemské muzeum Opava). Týká se to draperie zavěšené v popředí a sloupů, vytvářejících průhled do chrámového prosto­ru, jeho pročlenění a prosvětlování řadou oken. Také hlavní světelný zdroj, v obou obrazech pronikající do scény klenbou a významově zdůrazňující ústřed­ní figurální motiv, je v obou malbách obdobný; u Winterhaldera je však světlo faktorem scénu zcelujícím, zatímco u Havelky tuto roli nehraje. Po­dobnosti se najdou rovněž v komparsu, např. klečící a stojící mužské postavy v popředí.  
Tyto analogie lze vysvětlit bud'to společnou předlohou, nejspíše grafickou, nebo spíše tak, že Havelka přejal podněty od J. Winterhaldera ml. Tomu by nasvědčovala především barevná škála jeho návrhu, ve kterém se uplatňuje stříbřitě bílá a chladně modrá; v ostatním Havelkově díle je tato barevnost neobvyklá.  
Ve sbírkách Jihomoravského muzea ve Znojmě je uložena další verze Ha­velkova Křtu sv. Augustina, poněkud menších rozměrů. Znojemský obraz jí patrně předcházel, neboť je bezprostředněji, volněji malo­vaný a komponovaný do obdélníka, který Havelka na brněnském modelu upravil do tvarové podoby oltářního obrazu.  
Havelkův formální výraz svědčí v některých dílech o tom, že mu nebyla neznámá tvorba F. A. Maulbertsche, případně J. W. Bergla, jehož obrazy mohl poznat ve svém rodném regionu. Příbuznou kompozici nalezneme ale i v díle C. Carloneho nebo F. J. Spieglera (Merdingen).

Sv. Augustin, jeden z církevních otců, je se svým synem Adeodatem křtěn  
sv. Ambrožem. Jde o ukázkový model pro obraz hlavního oltáře v Jevíčku. Havelkův výraz svědčí o tom, že mu nebyla neznámá tvorba F. A. Maulbertsche, případně  
J. W. Bergla, jehož obrazy mohl poznat ve svém rodném regionu.

en.name: *The Baptism of St. Augustine*
description:
The picture depicts the baptism of St. Augustine (354–430), together with his son Adeodat, by St. Ambrosius. Augustine, one of the Church Fathers and Bishop of Milan, influenced Christian doctrine from the Middle Ages to modern times with his writing.  
The base of the font is a beehive, a symbol of the church and an Augustine attribute. This picture was a template for a high altar painting in Jevíčko Church, commissioned by the Abbot of the Augustinian Monastery in Brno. It shares a number of motifs with *The Baptism of Prince Bořivoj* (Svatopluk?) by Josef Winterhalder Jr. (Silesian Provincial Museum, Opava). For example, drapery hangs in the foreground and columns form a vista into the temple space, with segmentation and illumination provided by a row of windows. The main light source in both pictures enters the scene through the vault to accentuate the central figurative motif, and although light is a unifying factor for both artists, for Havelka, it is assigned a different role. There are also similarities in the figurative aspects of both paintings, such as the standing and kneeling male figures in the foreground.  
These analogies may be explained either by a joint model (a print) from which both artists derived their motifs or by the fact that Havelka drew inspiration from J. Winterhalder Jr. The latter speculation is supported by the colour scheme of this design; silver-white and cold blue, colours that are not found in the rest of Havelka's oeuvre.  
The Museum of South Moravia in Znojmo holds another smaller version of Havelka's *Baptism of St. Augustine*. The Znojmo picture probably preceded the Brno design as its style appears more spontaneous and it is composed as a rectangle.  
Some of Havelka's pictures indicate that he was familiar with the work of F. A. Maulbertsch and J. W. Bergl, whose paintings were known in Havelka's native region. Similar compositions can be found in the work of C. Carlone and F. J. Spiegler (Merdingen).

St. Augustine, one of the Church Fathers, together with his son Adeodat, are baptised by St. Ambrosius. This is a template for a high altar piece in Jevíčko Church. Havelka’s style indicates that he was familiar with the work of both F.A. Maulbertsch and J.W. Bergl.
keywords: Modello; attribute; zoomorphic imagery; Christian themes; religious object

ar.name: علبة مجوهرات بتصميم حيوان وأشكال نباتية وهندسية
description: القطعة عبارة عن علبة مجوهرات صغيرة ذات غطاء برونزي جاثمة على أربعة أرجل بيضوية متصلة بجسم الأرجل ذات تزيين محزز وحواف ملفوفة. والغطاء له سطح مسطح ومستطيل مزين بتصاميم هندسية مترابطة / متداخلة ونباتية وهناك رصيعة تشبه الدولاب الصغير في كل زاوية وخمسة أخرى متباعدة بشكل متساوي في السطح المسطح للغطاء والحاقة المشطوفة للغطاء لها تصاميم نباتية وأيضا رصائع ذات خطوط متداخلة. والشريط قرب شفة الغطاء يحتوي سلسلة من الكلاب التي تجري أو الغزلان والتي تقابل جهة اليسار. وطرفي العلبة مزينة بنفس الشكل الذي للسطح العلوي المسطح للغطاء. وكل وجه عريض له عشرة رصائع بشكل الدولاب وكل وجه ضيق له خمس رصائع مركزية وأربعة أنصاف رصائع واحدة على كل حافة من اللوحة.
dates: النصف الأول من القرن الثامن الهجري /النصف الأول من القرن الرابع عشر الميلادي

en.name: Casket with Design of Animal, Vegetal, and Geomettric Motifs
description: A small, lidded bronze casket sitting on four ovular feet attached to legs with incised decoration and scrolled edges. The lid has a flat, rectangular top, decorated with interlocking geometric and vegetal designs. There is a small wheel-like medallion at each corner, and five more equally spaced within the flat top of the lid. The beveled edge of the lid has vegetal designs, as well as medallions of interlocking lines. The register near the lip of the lid contains a series of running dogs or deer, facing left. The sides of the box are decorated in the same manner as the flat top of the lid. Each wide face has ten of the wheel-like medallions, and each narrow face has five central medallions and four half-medallions, one on each edge of the panel.
dates: Hegira First half 8th century / AD first half 14th century
keywords: Casket; Metalwork; Copper; Alloy; Silver; Gold; Inlay; Iran; Asia; Persian
materials: Copper alloy with silver and gold inlay

en.name: Church of San Román
description:
It seems probable that the church already existed in Visigothic times, which would explain the reuse of various capitals belonging to this period in the Mudéjar building. In the years immediately after the conquest of the city in 1085, the church was cited among the so-called “Latin parishes of the Christian cult”. The family of the Illán belonged to it, a lineage connected to the kings of Castile, an ancestor of which had been the *caudillo* or military leader of Alfonso VI. This evidence proves the existence of a church before the year 1221, the date when it was consecrated by don Rodrigo Ximénez de Rada, Archbishop of Toledo, as is recorded in the *Anales Toledanos* (Annals of Toledo).  
Keeping this information in mind, when examining the present building it is easy to distinguish two different architectural projects. One, which coincides with the main part of the nave, must belong to the church when it was in use in the 12th century. The type of horseshoe arch resting on brick pillars with attached columns corresponds to this period – the Visigothic columns and capitals mentioned above – along with the organisation of the upper part of the spans, which are not for the purposes of illumination, but simply lighten the load of the wall. These characteristics coincide with those of the other churches in Toledo from the so-called “first phase” of Toledo Mudéjar, like San Lucas, Santa Eulalia, or San Sebastián. The sanctuary belongs to a later phase of work, which may have coincided with the date of the consecration of the church in 1221. Here, in spite of the remodelling of the interior carried out in 1553 by Alonso de Covarrubias, there are still the remains of the exterior decoration of the primitive apse, with blind arcades following the Castilian model, which became the dominant style from the 13th century, within the “second phase” of Toledo Mudéjar. Also dating from the 13th century are the murals, discovered in 1940, which in all likelihood were painted to unify the old aisles with the new sanctuary.  
Although they are within the Romanesque tradition, certain details hint at the influence of the Islamic tradition, such as the use of imitation voussoirs in white and red on the arches of the nave, the multifoil arches of the windows and the plant motifs of the *ataurique* in the spandrels of the arches.  
The tower, which must have been built at the end of the 13th century or in the early 14th century, is notable for its use of multifoil arches, which rest on small columns of vitrified ceramics, a solution, which although quite rare in Toledo is seen in some other buildings, for instance in the Tower of Santo Tomé.  
Since 1971, the interior of the church has housed the Museum of the Councils of Toledo and Visigothic Culture.

es.name: Iglesia de San Román
description:
Parece probable que la iglesia existiera ya en época visigoda, lo que explicaría la reutilización de varios capiteles de ese estilo en el edificio mudéjar. Ya en los años inmediatos a la conquista de la ciudad en 1085, aparece citada entre las llamadas “parroquias latinas de culto cristiano”. A ella perteneció la familia de los Illán, linaje vinculado a los reyes de Castilla, uno de cuyos antepasados fue caudillo de Alfonso VI. Estos testimonios prueban la existencia de una iglesia anterior al año 1221, fecha en que fue consagrada por el arzobispo de Toledo don Rodrigo Ximénez de Rada, según consta en los Anales Toledanos.  
Teniendo en cuenta estos datos, al examinar el actual edificio resulta fácil distinguir dos proyectos arquitectónicos diferentes. Uno, que coincide con el cuerpo de las naves, debió pertenecer a la iglesia utilizada en el siglo XII. A esa época corresponde el tipo de arcos de herradura que apoyan en pilares de ladrillo con columnas adosadas —las columnas y capiteles citados de época visigoda—, y también la organización en la parte alta de vanos que no tienen la función de iluminar, sino únicamente de aligerar el muro. Estos caracteres coinciden con los de otros templos de Toledo dentro de la llamada “primera fase” del mudéjar toledano, como San Lucas, Santa Eulalia o San Sebastián. A otra obra posterior, que podría coincidir con la fecha de consagración del templo en 1221, corresponde la cabecera, donde, a pesar de la remodelación interior realizada en 1553 por Alonso de Covarrubias, aún se conservan restos de la decoración exterior del ábside primitivo, con arquerías ciegas siguiendo el modelo castellano que se impuso desde el siglo XIII, dentro de la segunda fase del mudéjar toledano. También en la primera mitad del siglo XIII se fechan las pinturas murales descubiertas en 1940, ejecutadas probablemente para unificar las antiguas naves con la nueva cabecera. Aunque se hallan dentro de la tradición románica, ciertos detalles indican la influencia de la decoración islámica, como el uso fingido de dovelas blancas y rojas en los arcos de las naves, los arcos lobulados en las ventanas o los motivos vegetales de *ataurique* en las enjutas de los arcos.  
La torre debió construirse ya a finales del siglo XIII o comienzos del XIV. En ella destaca el uso de arcos lobulados que apoyan en columnillas de cerámica vidriada, solución que, si bien no es frecuente en Toledo, se encuentra también en otros edificios, como la torre de Santo Tomé.  
Desde 1971, en el interior de la iglesia está instalado el Museo de Concilios de Toledo y de la Cultura Visigoda.

en.name: Air France Brochure
description: This folding brochure, illustrated by an artist signing as Mariner, advertised Air France services to the Orient and the Far East for the summer of 1939. On its cover, the route runs from London and Paris to Marseille, divides as it crosses the Mediterranean and meets again in the Levant, before continuing to Baghdad and onwards to India, Southeast Asia and Hong Kong, a journey of eight days and more than 15,000 kilometres. A Dewoitine D-338 airliner, cut open to reveal its passengers, crew and cargo, promises comfort as well as speed. At the European end of the route stands a woman in an evening gown, while at the far eastern end another woman appears in East Asian dress. Inside, timetables, fares, visa regulations and currency tables guide the traveller across a map divided by colonial and mandate rule. Before the summer season was over, the outbreak of the Second World War disrupted this network of long-distance civilian air travel.
keywords: Advertisment; Travel; Flight; Art Deco; Holidays

en.name: Saint Nicholas of Mozhaisk with Scenes from His Life
description: Saint Nicholas, a 4th-century bishop from modern-day Turkey, is one of the most venerated saints in Russia. Stories of Saint Nicholas giving gifts to the needy and protecting children spread far and wide as people traveled or emigrated from Russia to other countries. In this icon, a full-length statue of Saint Nicholas is set in a *kiot* (wooden box). Painted panels with images of Christ and the Mother of God were once affixed to either side. In the center panel, Saint Nicholas originally held a sword in his right hand and a church in his left hand; both are now missing. The doors are illustrated with important scenes from the saint’s life.
keywords: Saints; Religious iconography

en.name: Aleppo Citadel
names: Aleppo Citadel (in three parts: Entrance Block, Palace and Mosque)
description:
In terms of both its height and the greatness of its entrance block, Aleppo Citadel ranks far above all the other urban citadels in Syria and her neighbouring countries. Seen from any angle,  
the entrance block alone is an impressive sight. Linked with the city by means of a ramp supported on seven arches, it rises like a great monolith pierced by numerous arrow slits and machicolated brattices. Its two massive towers hide behind them a U-shaped corridor that would force an attacking army to change direction six times, all the while being exposed to projectiles and hot liquids poured from openings in the vaults above them. Indeed, the strength of the entrance block was reinforced by use of powerful imagery, such as the intertwined dragons at the first gate and the two lion sculptures at the last.  
The Ayyubid palace complex is located on high ground near to the south end of the citadel and is reached by stairs to  
the right of the main ramp. Built initially by al-Zahir Ghazi and rebuilt by his son ‘Aziz Muhammad in the early 6th/13th century, the palace complex measures about 50 m x 40 m. It  
consists of the palace proper, a *hammam* with three chambers, and a warren of guardrooms and arsenals, which are currently under excavation, to the south. The palace entrance is  
on the west side through a monumental portal, which is quite striking in its richness and complexity, combining, as it does, *muqarnas* vaulting, geometric ornamentation and colour.  
Although *muqarnas* portals were fairly commonplace in this period, this one is the tallest and most elaborate example in Aleppo.  
Moving through a vestibule for guards one  
passes through a small courtyard (4.5 m sq) before entering a more spacious courtyard, (about 10 m sq), which forms the centre of the palace. With an octagonal pool in the middle and  
four coaxial *iwans*, the palace resembles other Ayyubid palaces, in particular that seen at Qal‘at Najm (VIII.1.). The northern *iwan*, undoubtedly the most privileged, has the  
remains of a *salsabil* fountain hooded by a *muqarnas* vault. Originally, water would have flowed down a carved marble slab, into a partially open and part-covered channel, and  
emptied into the central pool.  
Perched at the highest point in the citadel, the mosque’s inscription on the portal dates it to 610/1214. Externally, it has a simple and traditional form,  
consisting of a large rectangular block with a central dome and a tall, square minaret. Internally, the mosque is equally traditional, with a rectangular courtyard and a tripartite prayer-hall  
with a dome and a plain, stone *mihrab*. In fact, the mosque is interesting chiefly for its minaret, whose height and square section recall the older minaret of the Great Mosque below.

en.name: Águas Livres Aqueduct
description: The aqueduct has three main parts: the Mãe d'Água reservoirs located near the spring at the beginning of the course in the Carenque valley; the aqueduct and its secondary aqueducts spreading out around the city with a total length of 58.135 km. The system includes arches over the Alcântara valley. These are 941 m in length with an ensemble of 35 arches of which 14 are pointed and 21 are round. The ultimate destination of the Águas Livres aqueduct is the Mãe d'Água reservoir delivering water to the city. The reservoir is a wide, vaulted construction with an approximate capacity of 5,500 m3. The formal structure is perfectly justifiable for a work of this nature, which demands various materials and rational engineering. The incredible height of the rises of the Aqueduct's arches in the Alcântara valley is astonishing. The technical audacity is largely due to the Custódio Vieira's knowledge of engineering. The aqueduct pays homage to Roman models as it is imposingly “imperial” in its monumentality and even in its geographic position. The scarce ornamentation of Mãe d'Água das Amoreiras reservoir is compensated by the scale of the work and imposition of the vast stripped and solemn walls, as if the building was in fact a temple of the waters.

An aqueduct using a classic system of gravity to capture, conduct and distribute water to the city of Lisbon. An open-air structure, it is mainly known for its monumental pointed arches over the Alcântara valley. There are also the underground galleries, the Mãe d'Água reservoir, and other springs dotted throughout its course. The main, oldest spring is located in the municipality of Sintra, which is endowed with adjacent works, canals and fountains.
artist: Portuguese architect and engineer: Manuel da Maia (1677–1766 ); Italian architect: António Canevari (1671–1764); Portuguese architect and engineer: Custódio Vieira (c. 1690–1744?); main contractor: Carlos Mardel (c. 1695–1763); unknown Hungarian architects and engineers. For the fountain: engineer, Miguel Ângelo Blasco (active 1769–1770); architect: Reinaldo Manuel dos Santos [n.d.].
history: At the beginning of João V's reign, the water supply in Lisbon was at a critically low state so in 1723, in an attempt to overcome the problem, Claudio do Amaral (attorney of west Lisbon) proposed that a study should be carried out on the spring at the Belas Águas Livres. He hoped that the study would allow water from the Belas Águas Livres to be channelled via an aqueduct into Lisbon. The king supported this decision and granted the means necessary to fund the aqueduct such as, in 1729, imposing a tax on the sale of certain goods entering the city (meat, wine, straw, olive oil and salt). Work began on the aqueduct in 1731 and, although construction didn't finish until approximately 1799, water was first channelled by the structure to Lisbon in 1744.
keywords: Water architecture, aqueduct, civil architecture, Alcântara valley, Lisbon
tags: Water architecture, aqueduct, civil architecture, Alcântara valley, Lisbon
partner: Institute for the Administration of Architectural and Archaeological Heritage -  IGESPAR

pt.name: *Aqueduto das Águas Livres*
description: O Aqueduto possui três partes constituintes principais: as *mães de água*, no arranque do percurso junto às nascentes, no Vale de Carenque; o aqueduto e a as respectivas ramificações pela cidade com 58,135 quilómetros de extensão, de que faz parte a arcaria sobre o Vale de Alcântara, com 941 m de comprimento e 35 arcos, 14 dos quais ogivais o os restantes de volta inteira; e a *Mãe de Água das Amoreiras*, ponto do chegada da água à cidade, ampla construção abobadada, provida de um depósito com cerca de 5500 m3 de capacidade. No conjunto da grande obra, é evidente a influência estética da Aula dos Paços da Ribeira, da qual Manuel da Maia foi mestre. Caracteriza-se pela simplicidade de meios e pela eficácia de objectivos. A contenção formal era perfeitamente justificável para um empreendimento desta natureza, que exigia uma seriação dos materiais e dos talhes a utilizar com vista a uma maior racionalização de meios. Surpreende pelo arrojo técnico a enorme altura a que sobem as flechas dos arcos do Aqueduto no Vale de Alcântara, sendo de realçar o contributo de Custódio Vieira e do seu saber de engenharia de guindagem. A obra do Aqueduto tornou-se numa afirmação de um “modo de fazer” tradicional, “à portuguesa”. Trata-se de uma gigantesca operação de glorificação do rei e de transformação da cidade. O Aqueduto é, ele próprio, uma alegoria ao “romano”, quer dizer, imponentemente “imperial” na sua monumentalidade e, até, no seu posicionamento geográfico. Na *Mãe de Água das Amoreiras*, a escassa ornamentação é compensada pela escala do empreendimento e pela imposição das vastas paredes despidas e solenes, como se o edifício fosse, de facto, um templo das águas. Aliás, tudo aqui parece provar a intenção de criar um lugar de destaque na topografia monumental da Lisboa joanina, que era modesta, por sinal. Trata-se de um caso de claro empenhamento “barroco” na monumentalização da cidade capital, aliás, clarificada pela poética inscrição joanina do exterior da Casa do Registo (à ilharga da Mãe de Água): *Nayadum, Olisiponensiu Urbana Domus intus Aquae dulces. Anno Domini 1748.*

Aqueduto para captação, condução e distribuição de águas à cidade de Lisboa, segundo o sistema clássico da gravidade. Estrutura a céu aberto e em galeria subterrânea, com “mães de água” ao longo do seu percurso, sendo as principais junto ao manancial de origem. Dotado de obras anexas, ramificações e chafarizes.
artist: Município de Lisboa; rei D. João V.

Arquitecto e engenheiro português Manuel da Maia (1677–1766); arquitecto e engenheiro italiano Antonio Canevari (1681–1764); arquitecto e engenheiro português Custódio Vieira (c.1690–c.1744); arquitecto e engenheiro húngaro Carlos Mardel (c.1695–1763); outros arquitectos e engenheiros húngaros desconhecidos. Fontes: engenheiro Miguel Ângelo Blasco (activo 1769–1770); arquitecto Reinaldo Manuel dos Santos [n.d.].
history: No começo do reinado de D. João V, a situação do abastecimento de água a Lisboa era de quase ruptura. A população acorria aos chafarizes da parte velha da cidade, onde as disputas pela posse da água assumiam grande violência. A água era um bem escasso e dispendioso, sujeito a especulação por parte dos aguadeiros. Para obviar a este estado de coisas, Cláudio do Amaral, procurador de Lisboa Ocidental, propôs, em 1723, o estudo dos mananciais das Águas Livres de Belas com o intuito de promover a sua condução a Lisboa. O rei apoiou esta decisão e conferiu-lhe meios de execução. Logo em 1729 foram lançados impostos sobre alguns géneros que entravam na cidade (carne, vinho, palha, azeite e sal), com a finalidade de reunir a soma necessária para o arranque da edificação do aqueduto que partisse daquelas fontes. Em 1731, iniciaram-se as obras do Aqueduto e, em 1744, chegaram a Lisboa as primeiras águas conduzidas pelo empreendimento, embora as obras só tenham ficado concluídas por volta de 1799.
keywords: Arquitectura da água, aqueduto, arquitectura civil, Vale de Alcântara, água de Lisboa, água.
tags: Arquitectura da água, aqueduto, arquitectura civil, Vale de Alcântara, água de Lisboa, água.

ar.name: صحن
description: صحن المبخرة هذا له قعر مسطح وجدار يميل بشكل طفيف وإطار مسطح مسنن بعض الشيء. والشكل الرئيس في الحلقة المتوسطة يظهر ثلاثة حيوانات متحركة ذات جسم نحيل تمثل كلب صيد (سلوقي) فارسي ولكن لها ذيول قصيرة وآذان طويلة كالتي للأرنب البري. والآذان مشكلة مثل أوراق أو سعف نخل وقد جمعت معا بشكل يشبه مثلث الذي يربط الأرانب البرية ويشكل انطباعا أن كل حيوان مزود بأذنين. وخلفية الحلقة محفورة بلفات نباتية تنتهي ببراعم ثلاثية الفصوص. والحلقة مؤطرة بعصابة مطعمة بالنحاس يليها أخدود مقولب محاط بدائرة مثلمة / محززة أخرى ،والدائرة الأخيرة تعمل كنقطة حدود للهالة المحاطة التي تكوّن حتى 42 قوسا متقاطعا وتستند على تيجان عواميد (عقود) ذات أعمدة أقل ثخانة . والفراغات بين الأعمدة مملوءة بجسم محفور يشبه المسمار الطويل أو الملعقة. وهو ينتمي لتصاميم أكثر تعقيدا لنموذج الهالة التي ترمز لقرص الشمس. الإطار مقسم بواسطة ستة مناطق تزيين /أزرار والأضلاع / الجوانب الأقصر محشورة ومملوءة بنقوش تهنئة. والحلقة مملوءة بتفاصيل حبل زينة محفور بين كل زري تزيين. والدوائر النصفية الأربع المزخرفة بنقوش نافرة موجهة بالاتجاهات الرئيسية الأربعة على عصابة سهمية حول الرصائع وهي ميزة تزيينية للقرن العاشر – الحادي عشر والجدار الخارجي مصمم بنفس الشكل الخراساني أيضا وهنا يوجد طاووس في الشكل يملأ الرصائع والقعر الخارجي مزين يحلقة مركزية وأيضا محفورة بطاووس يسير.
keywords: مشغولة معدنية ، مبخرة
partner: المتحف الجامعي للفن الإسلامي / مجموعة بوميلر

en.name: Dish
description:
This incense dish has a flat bottom, a slightly slanting wall and a somewhat indented flat rim. The main motif in the central roundel of the inner bottom side shows three revolving animals with the wiry body of a Persian greyhound but with a short tail and the long ears of a hare. The ears, structured like palm fronds or leaves, are put together like a triangle connecting the hares and creating the illusion that each animal is equipped with two ears. The background of the roundel is engraved with vegetal scrolls ending in trilobed buds. The roundel is framed with an inlaid copper band followed by a moulded groove surrounded by another incised circle. The last circle serves as boundary point for the enclosing corona that is made up of 42 intersecting arches based on capitals with slender columns. The spaces between the columns are filled with an engraved object resembling a long nail or spoon. It belongs to the more complex designs of the corona pattern that symbolizes the sun disk.  
The rim is divided by six cartouches, the shorter sides inserted, filled with benedictory inscriptions. A roundel filled with a festoon detail is engraved in between each cartouche. The four embossed semicircles pointed in the four cardinal directions on the narrow band around the medallions are a 10th-11th century décor feature. The outside wall is equally designed in the same Khorasanian manner. Here, a peacock in profile fills the medallions. The outside bottom is decorated with a central roundel, also engraved with a walking peacock.
holder: University Museum of Islamic Art | The Bumiller Collection
keywords: Metalwork; incense burner
partner: University Museum of Islamic Art | The Bumiller Collection

en.name: Ker Porter’s box
short_description: In 1814 Ker Porter, British artist and travelller, visited Rich. Together they explored famous sites in Iraq. He mistook the ruins at Aqar Quf for the Tower of Babel. The box contains fragments of a Babylonian mudbrick and bitumen, matching the Biblical description of the Tower.
keywords: Bible; Babel

en.name: Santuario della Beata Vergine di San Luca
description: Starting from the project made by Sacchi, Dotti’s drawings provided an elliptic plan, completed by a high chapel covered by a great dome. Most important Dotti thought of a very ingenious and startling connection of the body of the church and the last section of the portico accompanying the faithful from the city. The main façade is linked to the covered route through a sort of tribune while another one is symmetrically repeated on the other side of the front giving way to the exit. There is also a place for resting after the effort of climbing the hill which opens towards the sky, encouraging meditation and prayer before entering into the sacred space of the church.

Located upon the so called hill ‘della Guardia’ (“of the guard”), in the outskirts of Bologna, the shrine is dedicated to the Virgin, in particular to a miraculous painting of a Madonna with child attributed to St. Luke’s brush. A place of special worship for the Bolognese people, this religious complex is characterised by the harmonious connection between architecture and landscape: the soft bends  seem to be inspired not only by the sinuosity (due to the site orography) of the covered route (a portico) leading to the place but are also in relation with the circular and linear structure of the main building.
artist: Architect: Carlo Francesco Dotti; sculptor: Angelo Gabriello Piò; painter: Vittorio Maria Bigari
history:
In 1680, Cardinal Lazzaro Pallavicino bequest some money to build a new altar for the miraculous painting of the Virgin still preserved in the old church. It was realised in 1696 in the shape of a modern chapel. In this same year, refurbishing work was made enlarging the church, so that when the new chapel was finished (1713) the church appeared too poor and indecorous. The architect G. Paolo Sacchi was charged to design a new building and his project was presented in 1717. Five years later the Swiss Carlo Francesco Dotti, a celebrated master builder, made a new project that was approved and finally built.  
The new shrine was consecrated in 1765.
keywords: Religious architecture; Devotional route; Miraculous images; Devotion; card. Lazzaro Pallavicino; G. Paolo Sacchi; Carlo Francesco Dotti; Angelo Piò; Antonio Borelli; Giovanni Calegari, Vittorio Maria Bigari; Claudio Ferroni; Gian Giacomo Monti; Giovanni Antonio Conti; Francesco Galli Bibiena; Pilgrimage; Fresco; Architectural sculpture
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: Santuario della Beata Vergine  di S. Luca
names: Santuario della Beata Vergine di San Luca
description: Partendo dal progetto di Sacchi, i disegni di Dotti immaginano una pianta ellittica, completata da una enorme cappella maggiore coperta da un agrande cupola. Soprattutto Dotti pensò ad un collegamento molto ingegnoso e sorprendente tra il corpo della chiesa e l'ultima parte del portico che conduce il fedele dalla città. La facciata principale è collegata al cammino coperto da una sorta di tribuna (un'altra, ripetuta simmetricamente sull'altro lato della fronte apre all'uscita), un luogo di riposo dopo lo sforzo di salire il colle, aperto verso il cielo, che incoraggia alla meditazione e alla preghiera prima di entrare nello spazio sacro della chiesa.

Posto sul cosiddetto colle ‘della Guardia’, alla periferia di Bologna, il santuario è dedicato alla Vergine, e precisamente ad una immagine miracolosa raffigurante la  Madonna col Bambino attribuita al pennello di S. Luca. Luogo di speciale devozione per la gente di Bologna, questo complesso religioso è caratterizzato dall'armonioso rapporto tra architettura e paesaggio. Le morbide curve sembrano ispirate non solo alla sinuosità della posizione geografica del portico che conduce al santuario ma anche alla struttura lineare e circolare dell'edificio principale.
artist: Chiesa di Bologna e privati cittadini
Architetto: Carlo Francesco Dotti; scultore: Angelo Gabriello Piò; pittore: Vittorio Maria Bigari
history:
Nel 1680 il Cardinal Lazzaro Pallavicino lasciò una somma di denaro per costruire un nuovo altare per l'immagine miracolosa della Vergine che si trovava nella vecchia chiesa; lo si costruì nel 1696 in forma di cappella in stile moderno. Nello stesso anno vennero intrapresi lavori di ristrutturazione che portarono ad un ampliamento della chiesa, tanto che quando la nuova cappella fu finita (1713) la chiesa apparve troppo povera e inadatta. L'architetto G. Paolo Sacchi ricevette l'incarico di progettare un nuovo edificio e il suo progetto fu presentato nel 1717. Cinque anni dopo lo svizzero Carlo Francesco Dotti, un famoso capomastro, realizzò un progetto nuovo che fu approvato e finalmente realizzato.  
Il nuovo santuario fu consacrato nel 1765.
keywords: Architettura religiosa; Percorso devozionale; Immagini miracolose; Devozione; card. Lazzaro Pallavicino; G. Paolo Sacchi; Carlo Francesco Dotti; Angelo Piò; Antonio Borelli; Giovanni Calegari, Vittorio Maria Bigari; Claudio Ferroni; Gian Giacomo Monti; Giovanni Antonio Conti; Francesco Galli Bibiena; Pellegrinaggio; Affresco; Scultura architettonica

ar.name: لوحة معدنية من الهند
description: هذه اللوحة المعدنية الهندية تصور شاه جانجير الإمبراطور المغولي الرابع ويوجد عليها نقشان يقول الأول :""ضوء نهار البلد سنة 1013"" والثاني نقش ذهبي على الطرف الأيسر العلوي يقول "" مولانا جانجير ، الإمبراطور"" واللوحة مزينة بإطارات صغيرة التي نقشت فيها أبيات من الشعر عن الإمبراطور. وبداية ونهاية الشعر مفقودة مما يعني أن هناك قطع أخرى من نفس النوع تحمل بقية الشعر. ويورد الشعر مناقشة بين الإمبراطور ونائبه.
keywords: مغول ، جانجير ،مشغولة معدنية

en.name: Metal plaque from India
description: This Indian metal plaque depicts Jahangir Shah, the fourth Mughal emperor. It had two inscriptions in Persian: the first reads "Daylight of the country, year 1013” and the second, golden inscription on the upper left side reads "Lord Jahangir, the Emperor." The plate is decorated with small frames in which verses of a poem about the Emperor are inscribed. The beginning and end of the poem are missing, suggesting that there may have been other objects of the same kind bearing the rest of the poem. The poem recounts a discussion between the Emperor and a proxy.
keywords: Mughal; Jahangir; Metalwork

short_description: This series of photographs attests to the existence of African slaves working in domestic roles or in agricultural labour.
