en.name: Bowl
description: Glassmakers from Europe started travelling to the capital of China in the beginning of the 18th century AD. This progress was made possible through means of commercial and diplomatic interactions between China and the West, the latter being significantly represented by Venetian glassmakers from Murano. This alliance provided the Chinese with, on a practical level, novel mirrors, lenses, windowpanes and production skills. But also, in artistic terms, the alliance provided them with Aventurine glass and enamel materials, which would soon enough become their own productions. The Western glassmakers were invited to produce glassware mainly in the Chinese style, often copying ceramic forms. Normally glass was used for small snuff bottles and bowls were rare. Therefore, these types of bowls are esteemed for their beautiful form and colour, presenting signature techniques and shapes of Murano glassmaking.
keywords: Glass; bowl; vessel; Beijing; Qianlong; 18th century; china
partner: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art

cs.name: *Portrét císaře Josefa II. a jeho druhé manželky Marie Josefy Bavorské a knížat Esterházyho, Bathianyho a Liechtenštejna*
names: *Josef II. s manželkou Marií Josefou Bavorskou, nejbližšími dvorskými spolupracovníky a dvorními dámami*
description:
Rozměrné plátno má protějšek v *Portrétu císařovny Marie Terezie se syny pod bustou zesnulého chotě Františka Štěpána Lotrinského a kancléřem Kounic-Rietbergem*. Jde o zobrazení představující rodovou i vladařskou hierarchii. Od smrti svého otce byl Josef II. spoluvladařem Marie Terezie. V pozadí poukazuje na medailon s portrétem Isabely Parmské, první manželky Josefa II. Josef Václav z Liechtenštejna, vpravo za trůnem diskutují dvě neprovdané Josefovy sestry Marie Alžběta a Marie Anna. V popředí s tygří kožešinou stojí František Esterházy a z okraje plátna vyhlíží kníže Karel Josef Batthyány, vrchní hofmistr. Slavnostně majestátní charakter dodává obrazu repusoárové aranžmá draperie se zlatými střapci a posazení figurální skupiny na stupně. Psa v popředí je možné chápat jako symbol lásky a věrnosti. Z krajinného pozadí se vynořuje obelisk završen zeměkoulí, na níž sedí orel, který drží v zobáku stočeného hada zakousnutého do vlastního ocasu, symbol věčnosti. Orel, jako živočich spjatý s Jupiterem, patřil k základním prvkům imperiální ikonografie Karla VI. Odkazuje na ctnosti panovníka. Dalším atributem a symbolem Moudrosti je štít s hlavou Medusy dole na kamenné váze. Skupina puttů krotících lva ve vrcholu vázy vyjadřuje moc lásky a jejího vítězství nad silou.  
Skupinový portrét nebyl zakázkou dvorskou, nýbrž projevem loajality opata premonstrátského kláštera v Louce u Znojma, který ještě netušil, že v osobě Josefa II. oslavuje likvidátora svého konventu. Obrazy pocházejí z letního refektáře kláštera, jenž v celkovém ideovém konceptu jako chrámu Šalamounova byl jedním z klíčových míst. Odpovídal v podstatě dekoru tzv. císařských sálů. Těžiště výzdoby zaujímaly malby Franze Antona Maulbertsche zobrazující založení kláštera a apotheosu premonstrátského řádu. Doplňovala je galerie podporovatelů a představitelů kláštera. Císařské portréty byly umístěny po stranách hlavního vchodu refektáře, jehož výzdoba zanikla se zrušením kláštera r. 1784.

Jde o zobrazení představující rodovou i vladařskou hierarchii formou alegorického portrétu, jež byl součástí náročné výzdoby jednoho z nejvýznamnějších klášterů  
v Podunají, k jehož zániku došlo právě v důsledku reforem Josefa II.
keywords: Portrét; alegorie; decorum; premonstráti; Josef II

en.name: *Portrait of Emperor Joseph II and His Second Wife Marie Josepha of Bavaria and Counts Esterházy, Bathiany and Liechtenstein*
names: *Joseph II with Wife Maria Josepha of Bavaria, Close Courtiers and Ladies-in-Waiting*
description:
A counterpart to this sizeable canvas is the picture *Maria Theresa with Sons Below the Bust of Her Deceased Husband Franz Stephan of Lorraine and Chancellor Kounic-Rietberg*. This painting represents the hierarchy of both the dynasty and the monarchy. After the death of his father, Joseph II ruled side-by-side with Maria Theresa. In the background, Josef Wenzl of Liechtenstein indicates a medallion bearing a portrait of Isabela of Parma, Joseph II's first wife. On the right, behind the throne, Joseph's two unmarried sisters, Marie Elisabeth and Marie Anna, are engaged in conversation. In the foreground stands Franz Esterházy with a tiger skin, while Count Karl Josef Batthyány, High Steward, is located at the edge of the canvas. The festive air is enhanced by the arrangement of a drapery with golden tassels together with the seating of the figures on the steps. The landscape in the background features an obelisk topped with a globe upon which an eagle perches holding in its beak a curled serpent biting its own tail a symbol of eternity. The eagle, a creature associated with Jupiter, was among the attributes of imperial iconography and refers to the sovereign's virtues. Another attribute and a symbol of wisdom is the shield with the head of Medusa at the bottom of the picture, on a stone vase. A group of *putti* taming a lion in the upper section of the vase symbolise the power of love and its victory over physical strength.  
The group portrait was commissioned by the abbot of the Premonstratensian Monastery in Louka near Znojmo as an expression of loyalty. The paintings come from the summer refectory, a key section of the monastery designed as a “Temple of Solomon”. The major decorative components were paintings by Franz Anton Maulbertsch depicting essential elements of the Premonstratensian order. These were accompanied by a series of portraits of monastery supporters and superiors.

The group allegorical portrait of the Habsbourg family was commissioned by the abbot of the Premonstratensian Monastery in Louka near Znojmo – one of the most important monasteries in the Danubian country – as an expression of loyalty. The painting represents the hierarchy of both the dynasty and the monarchy.
keywords: Portrait; allegory; decorum; Premonstratensian; Joseph II; symbolism; zoomorphic imagery; eagle; mithology

en.name: Necklace for horses – Type 2
short_description: This necklace was used on the horses of Ottoman officials and indicated their high status and wealth. The chain consists of alternating silver spheres and amber cubic beads, with a silver cylindrical pendant in the centre.
keywords: Decoration; Silver; Silver chains; Jewells; Precious stones; Beads

ar.name: قنديل مسجد.
description: قنديل مسجد زجاجي مطعم بالمينا، له فتحة متسعة وجسم منخفض على قاعدة منخفضة. لون الزجاج مائل إلى البني مع زخارف بالأزرق والأبيض من المينا، وضربات بالأحمر والأخضر والأصفر والذهبي. تتألف الزخرفة على وجه الحصر تقريباً من نقش بخط الثلث الفخم مع أطواق إضافية من الزخارف الزهرية الغزيرة حول العنق وفوق القاعدة. ويتضمن النقش الآيات 22، 24، 25 من سورة المطففين من القرآن، وعبارة "عز لمولانا السلطان الملك المظفر العالم العادل ركن الدنيا والدين عز نصره" التي تعود إلى السلطان المملوكي ركن الدين بيبرس الثاني الذي حكم لفترة قصيرة فقط في ما بين 704 و709/ 1306 و1310 قبل الإطاحة به وقتله. حكم هذا السلطان مع ضابط آخر لصالح الناصر محمد بن قلاوون الأسير منذ عام 698/ 1299، وبنى مجمعاً جميلاً في القاهرة يحتوي قبراً له ومقراً لإقامة الصوفية في الفترة 704-8/ 1306-9. وعلى الرغم من قيام خلفه بإزالتها مباشرة إلا أن الكتابات على المبنى تذكره على أنه السلطان. ولما كانت الآيات القرآنية على القنديل تشير إلى الحياة الآخرة، فمن المحتمل أنها صنعت ليتم تعليقها ضمن غرفة القبر. وتشابه زخارف القنديل أيضاً الكتابات الموجودة في القرآن الذي أمر بيبرس به للمجمع نفسه مما يسمح بالافتراض بوجود فريق من المصممين عملوا على وضع تصميم موحد للنظام التزييني هناك.

مصباح مسجد، مُصمَّم على الطراز المملوكي، مُزخرف كاملاًبالكتابات، تظهر عليها بعض الآيات القرآنية التي تتحدث عن الحياة الآخرة، ونُقش عليه اسم السلطان ركن الدين بيبرس الثاني، الذي لم يعش طويلاً، على الأغلب فإن المصباح صُنع خصيصاً لقبر السلطان.
keywords: قطعة ذات استخدام ديني.

en.name: Mosque lamp.
description: An enamelled glass mosque lamp with a flaring mouth and squat body standing on a low foot. The glass is brownish, with decoration in blue and white enamelling, and highlights in red, green, yellow and gold. The decoration consists almost exclusively of an inscription in majestic *thuluth* script, with additional bands of exuberant floral decoration around the neck and just above the foot. The inscription includes verses from the Qur'an (83:22, 24–5) and the phrase 'Glory to our lord, the Sultan, al-Malik al-Muzaffar, the learned, the just, Rukn al-Dunya wa'l-Din, may God grant him victory'. This refers to the Mamluk Sultan Rukn al-Din Baybars II, who ruled only for a short period, from AH 708–9 / AD 1309–10, before being overthrown and killed. He did, however, govern with a fellow officer as co-regents for the captive al-Nasir Muhammad Ibn Qala'un, beginning in AH 698 / AD 1299. He also built a fine complex in Cairo, containing his tomb as well as a lodge for Sufis, between AH 704–8 / AD 1306–9. Inscriptions in the building – immediately erased by his successor – referred to him even then as Sultan. Since the Qur'anic inscriptions on this lamp refer to the afterlife, it may have been intended to hang in the tomb chamber. The lamp's decoration is also similar to that found in a large Qur'an that Baybars had commissioned for the same complex, suggesting that there may have been a team of designers consciously working to give a unified look to the decorative programme there.

An enamelled glass lamp of typical Mamluk form, whose decoration is almost exclusively calligraphic. It includes Qur’anic verses and praise of the short-lived Sultan Rukn al-Din Baybars II. The verses refer to the afterlife, implying that the lamp may have been intended for the sultan’s tomb.
keywords: religious object; Mosque interior decoration; calligraphy; inscription; floral decoration

es.name: Lámpara de mezquita
description:
Lámpara de mezquita de vidrio esmaltado con boca abocinada y cuerpo achatado sobre un pie bajo. El vidrio, de color parduzco, está decorado con esmaltes azules y blancos, con partes destacadas en rojo, amarillo y dorado. Los motivos se reducen a una majestuosa inscripción en letra *zuluz* y dos bandas de exuberante decoración floral, una alrededor del cuello y la otra en la parte inferior del cuerpo. La inscripción incluye versos del Corán (sura 83, aleyas 22 y 24–25) y la frase: “Gloria a nuestro señor, el sultán, al-Malik al-Muzaffar, el instruido, el justo, Rukn al-Dunya wa l-Din, que dios le asegure la victoria”. Se refiere al sultán mameluco Rukn al-Din Baybars II, destronado y asesinado después de gobernar durante un corto periodo de tiempo (708-709 / 1309-1310). Sin embargo, había comenzado a gobernar en 698 / 1299 como corregente junto con otro oficial durante el cautiverio del sultán al-Nasir Muhammad Ibn Qalawun. Entre 704 y 708 / 1306-1309 construyó un gran complejo donde se encuentran su tumba y un pabellón para sufíes; las inscripciones de este último, inmediatamente eliminadas por su sucesor, se refieren a él como sultán.  
Las inscripciones coránicas de esta lámpara se refieren a la vida eterna, así que probablemente el objeto estuvo colgado en la cámara funeraria. La decoración es similar a la de un gran Corán que Baybars encargó para el mismo conjunto arquitectónico de El Cairo, lo que sugiere que quizás un equipo de artistas trabajó para crear deliberadamente una decoración única.

Lámpara de forma típicamente mameluca de vidrio esmaltado, con decoración casi exclusivamente caligráfica. Las inscripciones reproducen versículos coránicos y alabanzas al sultán Rukn al-Din Baybars II, que falleció prematuramente. Como sugieren las frases sobre la vida eterna inscritas, fue creada para decorar su tumba.
keywords: objetos religiosos

fr.name: Lampe de mosquée.
description: Lampe de mosquée en verre émaillé à ouverture évasée et corps ramassé, posé sur un pied court. Son verre brunâtre est décoré d'émail bleu et blanc et de rehauts en rouge, vert, jaune et or. Le décor consiste presque exclusivement en une inscription en majestueuse écriture de style *thoulouth* et de bandeaux additionnels à l'étranglement du col et juste au-dessus du pied, ornés d'une décoration florale exubérante. Les inscriptions comprennent des versets du Coran (sourate 83:22, 24-5) et la phrase : “Gloire à notre seigneur, le Sultan, al-Malik al Mudaffar, le savant, le juste, Rukn al-Dunya wa'l-Din, que Dieu lui assure la victoire.” Ce texte se réfère au sultan mamelouk Rukn al-Din Baybars II, qui ne régna que pendant une courte période de 708 à 709 H / 1309 à 1310 J.-C., avant d'être renversé et tué. Il gouverna cependant comme co-régent, avec un autre officier, au nom du sultan captif al-Nasir Muhammad Ibn Qalawun à partir de 698 H (1299 J.-C.). Il édifia également un bel ensemble architectural au Caire, contenant son tombeau ainsi qu'un pavillon pour les soufis, de 704 à 708 H (1306 à 1309 J.-C.). Les inscriptions sur le bâtiment – immédiatement effacées par son successeur – se référaient déjà à lui comme sultan. Comme les inscriptions coraniques de cette lampe évoquent la vie dans l'au-delà, elle a pu être commandée pour être suspendue dans la chambre funéraire. Le décor de la lampe est par ailleurs similaire à celui d'un grand coran que Baybars avait commandé pour le même complexe, ce qui suggère l'existence d'une équipe d'artisans travaillant à donner un aspect unifié au programme décoratif prévu.

Lampe en verre émaillé de forme typiquement mamelouke, dont la décoration presque exclusivement calligraphique inclut des versets du Coran et un éloge de la brève vie du sultan Rukn al-Din Baybars II. Les versets évoquent l'au-delà, ce qui suggère que la lampe a peut-être été fabriquée pour la tombe du sultan.
dates: entre 704 et 709 de l’Hégire / 1306 et 1310 J.-C.
keywords: Objets religieux

en.name: *Maktab al-\`Anbar School, Damascus*
names: First modern secondary school founded by the state in Damascus. Building was originally a private dwelling
short_description: The growth of Damascus urban culture and the changing role of the state were accompanied by important reforms and social changes. One of them was an increased alphabetisation and an improved public education. Attempts were first made by the state to reform schools in 1869 with the passing of an edict on school reform for the whole Ottoman Empire, officially recognizing private and foreign schools while setting out the basic principles of state education. The law now made a distinction between military schools on the one hand, and schools preparing children for a civil service or administrative career on the other hand. An example for the latter is Maktab al-`Anbar school.
holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
partner: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums

en.name: *Jerusalem, al-Haram al-Sharif, Dome of the Rock*
short_description: Joseph-Philibert Girault de Prangey (1804–1892) was a photographer who had, in all probability, worked with Daguerre. Being a wealthy man, he was very well travelled. His photographs, which  remained anonymous for a long time but were among the first photographs to be taken in the Middle East.
keywords: Jerusalem; religious buildings

fr.name: *Jérusalem: esplanade du Temple de Salomon, Dôme du Rocher*
short_description: Joseph-Philibert Girault de Prangey (1804-1892) est un photographe qui a vraisemblablement travaillé avec Daguerre. Bénéficiant d’une fortune personnelle, il a beaucoup voyagé, et ses clichés, longtemps restés dans l’anonymat, sont parmi les premiers réalisés en Orient, comme celui-ci pris à Jérusalem.
keywords: Jérusalem; édifices religieux

ar.name: إبريق.
description: إبريق متوسط الحجم، جسمه شبه كروي وقبضته على شكل حرف S ؛ يستند على قاعدة صغيرة غير مطلية. الإبريق مزخرف بصورة نمطية بأطواق عادية أفقية ومتعرِّجة، ملوَّنة بصباغ أسود على جسم الإناء غير المزجَّج في الأصل، وقد تمَّ طلاؤه لاحقاً بطبقة مزججة. وكانت الرَّقَّة أحد مركزين رئيسيين لإنتاج الخزف في سوريا العصر الأيوبي، بينما كانت الرصافة ثانيهما. ففي الرقة كان هنالك عدد من الورش المصنِّعة للخزف، وقد أنتجت مجموعة كبيرة من الأواني الفخارية؛ منها ذات البريق المعدني، والمفرَّغ في قوالب منقوشة، والمزيَّن برسوم تحت التزجيج.

الزخرف الأسود، تحت اللمعة الفيروزية الشفافة، هو أحد مميزات الخزفيات المصنوعة في الرقة، خلال الفترة الأيوبية. وقد كانت الرقّة أحد مركزي إنتاج رئيسيين في سورية، جنباً إلى جنب مع المركز الثاني، في الرصافة. والمركزان، كلاهما، كانا يقعان في مكانين قريبين من الفرات.
keywords: آنية منزلية؛ زخرفة هندسية؛ ماء.
materials: عجينة بيضاء كوارتزية مزخرفة بلون أسود تحت تزجيج شفاف بلون فيروزي.
tags: عجينة بيضاء كوارتزية مزخرفة بلون أسود تحت تزجيج شفاف بلون فيروزي.

en.name: Jug.
description: A medium-sized jug that has a spherical-shaped body and a small 'S-shaped' handle. The body rests on a small, unglazed, foot. The jug is typically decorated with simple horizontal zigzag bands, painted with black pigment on the body of the unglazed vessel, and then glazed with a transparent turquoise glaze. Raqqa was one of two major pottery-production centres in Ayyubid Syria, the other being Rusafah. Raqqa had a number of pottery workshops, which produced a range of ceramics including lustre-painted, relief-moulded and underglaze painted vessels.

The black decoration under the transparent turquoise glaze is typical of ceramics made in Raqqa during the Ayyubid period. Raqqa was one of two major production centres in Syria, the other being Rusafah. Both were located near the river Euphrates.
keywords: domestic vessels; geometric decoration; water
materials: Fritware; painted with black decoration under a transparent turquoise glaze.
tags: painted with black decoration under a transparent turquoise glaze.

es.name: Jarra.
description: Jarra de tamaño mediano con cuerpo esférico, pequeña asa en forma de “s” y pie estrecho sin vidriar. El cuerpo está decorado con las típicas bandas negras horizontales en zigzag, y luego vidriado en turquesa transparente. Raqqa y Rusafah eran los dos mayores centros productores de alfarería en la Siria Ayubí. En Raqqa había un gran número de talleres que producían varios tipos de cerámica: vasijas de reflejo metálico, moldeadas en relieve y pintadas bajo vidriado.

La decoración en negro bajo vidriado turquesa transparente es típica de las cerámicas realizadas en Raqqa durante el periodo ayyubí. Las ciudades de Raqqa y Rusafah, cercanas ambas al río Éufrates, eran los dos mayores centros productores en la Siria ayyubí.
dates: Siglo VII de la Hégira / XIII d. C.
keywords: vasijas de uso doméstico; decoración geométrica; agua.
materials: Frita o pasta cerámica, pintada en negro bajo vidriado transparente turquesa.
tags: Frita o pasta cerámica, pintada en negro bajo vidriado transparente turquesa.

fr.name: Cruche.
description: Cruche de taille moyenne à corps sphérique et petite poignée en forme de S. Le corps repose sur un court piédouche non vernissé. Ce récipient est typiquement décoré de simples bandeaux horizontaux en zigzags, peints au pigment noir directement sur la poterie non vernissée, avant d'être recouverts d'une glaçure transparente turquoise. Raqqa était l'un des deux grands centres de production de poterie dans la Syrie des Ayyoubides, l'autre étant Rusafa. La ville possédait un certain nombre d'ateliers de potiers produisant divers types de céramiques, dont des récipients à décor lustré, moulés en relief ou peints sous glaçure.

La décoration noire sous glaçure transparente turquoise est typique des céramiques fabriquées à Raqqa durant la période ayyoubide. Raqqa était l’un des deux grands centres de production en Syrie, l’autre étant Rusafa. Tous deux étaient situés près de l’Euphrate.
dates: VIIe siècle de l’Hégire (XIIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: récipients domestiques ; décoration géométrique ; eau
materials: Céramique frittée à décor peint en noir sous glaçure transparente turquoise.
tags: Céramique frittée à décor peint en noir sous glaçure transparente turquoise.

en.name: Mummy board and inner coffin for Nes-pauti-taui
description: An entire set of coffins was made in Thebes for the Amun priest Nes-pauti-taui. The mummy board and both coffin lids bear the same decorative scheme. We see enormous ornamental collars of foliage and flowers. The hands are separately applied and hold the djed-pillar and the Blood of Isis. The faces and wigs are also superimposed.
keywords: Theben; Egypt; Museum of Fine Arts Vienna
materials: Wool covered with linen cartonnage; painted, vanished

en.name: Travel case
short_description: Travelling became a great cultural and social phenomenon with Romanticism. The “Grand Tour” through the countries of the known world, and particularly around the Mediterranean, became a means of developing cultural and social skills. Travel became refined and even a simple journey to the countryside required such accessories as this travel case for meals.
keywords: objects; travel case; silverware

en.name: Portrait of Ahmad Faris al-Shidyaq
short_description: Ahmad Faris al-Shidyaq was born in 1804 in the 'Ashqut (Keserwan) district, and received his primary education in Hadath (Ba'abda), and his secondary education in 'Ayn Warka School. Here, he studied both foreign languages and Arabic literature. He was later converted to Protestantism by American missionaries in the region. He moved to Egypt in 1825, and then to Malta in 1834, where he lived for 14 years. During this period he became the head of the American Printing Press, and started publishing his own books. From Malta, he travelled to London, Paris and Tunis, where he converted to Islam and changed his name to Shaykh Ahmad Faris al-Shidyaq. In 1857, he began publishing his newspaper whilst he continued to edit his books. He died on 20 September 1889, and was buried in Lebanon, in Hazmiyya.
keywords: Missionaries; Newspaper; Press; Publisher

en.name: Qasr al-Kharrana
description:
Qasr al-Kharrana is a relatively well-preserved square building that measures about 36.50 x 35.50 m. It has two storeys of rooms decorated with stucco and arranged around a courtyard with a cistern underneath it. Small rooms are annexed to two rectangular halls (around 13 x 8 m.) on the southern, or frontal, side which are “divided” by the entrance passageway. Two inner stairways are directly opposite the eastern and western sides and lead to the upper storey.  
The *qasr* is built of stone rubble and was once covered with a coat of mortar. The four corners are distinguished by threequarter round towers and a semicircular tower marking the middle of the eastern, western and northern façade. Two quarter-circle towers flank the entry gate in the centre of the southern façade.  
The façades of the structure are further articulated through the use of a herringbone design, diagonally placed bricks that run as a frieze around the upper quarter of the building.  
In spite of Qasr al- Kharrana’s fortress-like appearance, the building was not used for military purposes. The towers and the numerous arrow slits marking the outer façades are ornamental since the former are solid and the arrow slits too high above the floor to serve archers.  
The *qasr* shows Persian influence in the building methods (rubble covered in mortar) and its decoration (of stucco finish). This has led K.A.C. Creswell, the renowned historian of Islamic architecture, to conclude that it was not an Umayyad but a Sassanian or Persian building going back to the Sassanian occupation of the area from 614 to 6/628. The Persians were not known to have carried out any building programmes, however, during their occupation. To the contrary, the idea of simulating a fortified appearance, and the fact that the related structures were non-functional, is characteristic of other Umayyad palaces such as al- Mushatta.  
A graffito found in the *qasr* gives the precise date of 27th *Muharram* 92/24th November 710, which is evidence that the construction was either before or around that date. There has been considerable debate about the exact date and while some have attributed it to the reign of al-Walid I (86/705-96/715), there are other suggestions dating it before 65/685. The latter year favours the argument that the palace is the only pre-Marwanid Umayyad palace known. As for the main function of Qasr al-Kharrana, it has been posited that it was used as a meeting place where Umayyad princes met with local tribal leaders.

es.name: Qasr al-Jarrana
description:
Qasr al-Jarrana es un edificio cuadrado relativamente bien conservado, que mide unos 36,50 x 35,50 m. Posee dos plantas cuyas habitaciones, dispuestas en torno a un patio con una cisterna debajo, están decoradas a base de estuco. Pegadas a los dos salones rectangulares (aprox. 13 x 8 m) del lado meridional o frontal y divididas por el pasadizo de entrada, se encuentran unas pequeñas habitaciones. Dos escaleras interiores, situadas en posiciones directamente opuestas en los lados este y oeste, conducen a la planta superior.  
El *qasr* está construido con mampuestos, y estuvo en otro tiempo revestido con una capa de mortero. Las cuatro esquinas están articuladas por otras tantas torres de tres cuartos de círculo, mientras que tres torres semicirculares señalan respectivamente la mitad de las fachadas este, oeste y norte. Dos torres de cuarto de círculo flanquean a su vez la puerta de entrada, situada en el centro de la fachada meridional. Las fachadas del edificio están articuladas, además, mediante el uso de un aparejo en espinapez, formado por ladrillos colocados diagonalmente que discurren a modo de friso en torno a la franja superior del muro exterior.  
A pesar de la apariencia de fortaleza del Qasr al-Jarrana, el edificio no se utilizaba para propósitos militares. Las torres y las numerosas aspilleras que señalan las fachadas exteriores son puramente ornamentales, ya que las torres son macizas, mientras que las aspilleras están demasiado altas para un arquero.  
El *qasr* muestra influencia persa en los métodos constructivos (mampuestos revestidos de mortero) y en la decoración (enlucido de estuco). Esto ha llevado al prestigioso historiador de la arquitectura islámica K.A.C. Creswell a la conclusión de que no se trata de un edificio omeya sino sasánida o persa, originario de la época de la ocupación sasánida de la zona, entre los años 614 y 6/628. Sin embargo, no se sabe de ningún programa constructivo llevado a cabo por los persas durante este periodo de ocupación. Por el contrario, la idea de simular una fortaleza y el hecho de que las edificaciones asociadas no fueran funcionales son características habituales de otros palacios omeyas, como es el caso de al-Muchatta. Una inscripción hallada en el *qasr* ofrece la fecha exacta del 27 de *Muharram* del año 92/24 de noviembre de 710, clara evidencia de que la construcción se produjo antes o en torno a esta fecha. Aún así, se ha producido bastante debate en torno a la fecha exacta y, mientras unos atribuyen la construcción a la época de Walid I (86/705-96/715), hay quienes sugieren una fecha anterior al 65/685. Esta última fecha favorece el argumento de que el edificio es el único palacio omeya premarwaní que ha llegado hasta nuestros días. En cuanto a la función principal del Qasr al-Jarrana, se ha sugerido que pudo usarse como un lugar de encuentro, donde los príncipes omeyas se reunían con los dirigentes locales.

fr.name: Qasr al Kharrana
description:
Qasr al-Kharrana est relativement bien conservé. Cet édifice carré, d’environ 36,50 m sur 35,50 m, est construit sur deux niveaux où les pièces décorées de stucs se répartissent autour de la cour centrale qui recouvre une citerne souterraine. Sur la façade sud, de part et d’autre du couloir de l’entrée principale, deux grandes salles rectangulaires (environ 13 m sur 8 m) donnent accès à d’autres petites pièces. Deux escaliers intérieurs, disposés symétriquement sur les côtés est et ouest, conduisent à l’étage.  
La construction en moellons était autrefois complètement recouverte d’un enduit de mortier. Les quatre angles sont épaulés par des tours en trois-quarts de cercle, et une tour semi-circulaire est érigée au centre des côtés est, ouest et nord. Deux tours en quart de cercle flanquent la porte d’entrée de la façade sud. Aux trois-quarts de la hauteur des murs, un décor court sur tous les côtés, comme une sorte de frise en motifs à chevrons obtenus par la pose diagonale des briques. Qasr al-Kharrana a une apparence trompeuse de forteresse, car il n’a pas été construit dans un dessein militaire. Les tours, comme les nombreuses meurtrières ménagées sur les façades extérieures, sont purement ornementales: les tours sont pleines et les meurtrières placées beaucoup trop haut pour être utiles à des archers.  
On remarque les influences perses tant dans les techniques de construction (mortier sur moellons) que dans la décoration (finitions en stuc). De ce fait, le grand historien de l’architecture islamique K.A.C. Creswell en a déduit qu’il ne s’agit en réalité pas d’une construction omeyyade mais sassanide ou perse, consécutive à l’occupation sassanide de la région, entre 614 et 6/628. Cependant, il n’est aucunement établi que les Perses avaient commencé à mettre en oeuvre un quelconque programme de constructions au cours de leur occupation. Par contre, le principe de la fortification simulée, avec des aménagements dépourvus de toute fonctionnalité, est une caractéristique commune à d’autres châteaux omeyyades comme al-Mouchatta.  
Le graffiti trouvé dans le *qasr*, qui mentionne précisément la date du 27 *Mouharram* 92/24 novembre 710, apporte la preuve que la construction a forcément précédé ou avoisiné cette date. La datation exacte est très controversée. Les uns la font remonter au règne de Walid Ier (86/705-96/715), d’autres penchent pour une construction antérieure à l’an 65/685. Dans ce cas, la thèse selon laquelle ce palais serait le seul palais omeyyade pré-marwanide connu en serait renforcée. Pour l’interprétation du château et de sa fonction principale, l’hypothèse la plus plausible serait qu’il servait de lieu de rencontre pour les princes omeyyades et les chefs des tribus locales.

ar.name: صفحة من ألبوم مصنوع من أجل جاهانجير
description: هذه اللوحة المرسومة على صفحتين ذات شكل متقن من جانب (اليسار) وتخطيط مؤطر على الصفحة الأخرى (اليمين) والشكل في اليسار يصور مشهد ناصع الألوان يبين ست شخوص بشرية وطائرين. وكل التشكيل يمكن تقسيمه إلى ثلاثة أرضيات. وكل الشخوص البشرية تشغل أمكنة في الأرضية الأمامية ويوجد شاب (الشخص المتوسط الذي يجلس على قاعدة مرتفعة) مبين في وضعية تحمل تساؤل حيث تشير يده اليسرى للأعلى. وهو يرتدي ثوب علوي برتقالي (جاما) ذو نطاق عند الخصر وبنطالا أزرق وحذاءا طويلا وإلى يمينه رجل عجوز يرتدي جاما صفراء فاتحة وقبعة زرقاء مرسوما وهو ينخرط في جدال مع الشاب.ويوجد ثلاثة أشخاص ذكور آخرين يما فيهم رجل منحن ومستند على مضرب ويقف إلى يسار الشاب والشخص المنحني الذي يرتدي ثوبا أصفر وهو محاذ بوقفته بدهشة. والشخص السادس هو عبارة عن أنثى تظهر وهي تختلس النظر سرا لهذا المشهد الدراماتيكي. ويمكن أن يرى وعاء شراب على أرض معشوشبة (مع بعض الأزهار) والأرضية الوسطى للتشكيل تتضمن عمارة قوسية بنية ذات نقش مستطيل وأشجار بعيدة داكنة وجبال والأرضية العليا تحتوي سماء زرقاء ساطعة وطيورا كبيرة ذات تلويحات لونية مخضرة ومزرقة وكل التشكيل محاط بالعديد من الحدود حيث الحد المتوسط الذهبي هو الأكثر بروزا. وهو يتألف من أزهار ونباتات متسلقة التي تزيد من جمال كامل التشكيل. وكل الشكل في الصفحة اليسرى محاط بالتالي بحدود متقنة مكونة من العديد من الحيوانات والطيور وهي تتحرك .وتشمل هذه الأشكال  نمور، أسود ، غزلان ، أرانب ، نسر ..الخ والحد البعيد مليء بالنباتات والأزهار وهذه كلها مرسومة بالذهب مع لمسات لونية والطرف الأيمن من الصفحة يبين تخطيط منقوش قطريا باللغة الفارسية ضمن حدود مزينة والحد الخارجي الواسع فيه مشهد للصيد بواسطة الصقور ووليمة مبينة بالذهب ذات معالجة عظيمة بألوان مختلفة.

en.name: Page from an Album made for Jahangir
description:
This is a two-sided painting with elaborate bordered illustration on one side (verso) and bordered calligraphy on the other (recto). The verso illustration has brilliantly colored scene delineating six human figures and two birds. The whole composition can be divided into three grounds. All the human figures occupy places in the foreground and a youth (central figure sitting on a raised pedestal) is shown in explanatory posture with left hand pointing upwards. He is wearing an orange top (*Jama*) belted on the waist, blue trousers and long boots. On his right an old man wearing a light yellow *jama* and a blue hat is drawn engaged in an argument with the young man. Three other male figures, including a reclining man bent on a club, are standing on the left side of the youth. The reclining man is draped in a yellow top and is juxtaposed in astonishment. The sixth figure, a female attendant, is shown peeping surreptitiously on this dramatic event. A light blue wine vessel can be seen on the grassy (with some flowers) ground.  
The middle ground of the composition is comprised of a brown arched architecture with a rectangular inscription, distant dark trees and mountains. The upper ground holds a bright blue sky and large birds of greenish and bluish hues. The entire composition is surrounded by several borders with the middle golden one being the most prominent. It consists of flowers and creepers which enhance the beauty of the whole composition. The entire verso illustration is then surrounded by an elaborate border consisting of many animals and birds in movement. These figures include leopards, lions, deer, rabbits, eagle etc. The broad border is replete with plants and flowers. These are all drawn in gold with touches of colors.  
The recto side of the page shows diagonally inscribed calligraphy in Persian within decorative borders. Broad outer border has a scene of falcon hunt and feast shown in gold with sublime treatment of different hues.
dates:
Recto calligraphy: Hegira first half 10th century / AD first half 16th century;  
Verso image: Hegira c. 998 / AD c. 1590; album: Hegira c. 1017-1028 / AD c. 1608–19
keywords: Page; Album; Jahangir; Drawing; Watercolor; Gold; Ink; Paper; India; Asia; Pencz; German; watercolour
materials: Ink, opaque watercolor, gold on paper

en.name: Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico 'L. Pigorini' (National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography), Exhibition Room
names: Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico 'L. Pigorini', sala espositiva
short_description: The origins, in terms of scientific activity and conservation, of the Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome, can be traced back to the foundation in 1875 of the “Regio Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico di Roma" (Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography). Initially the museum was located in a wing of the Palazzo del Collegio Romano built in the late 16th century by the Society of Jesus. This rare image represents the old arrangement of one of the rooms of the Roman College, where the collection of antiquities and curiosities gathered by Father Athanasius Kircher was kept after the foundation of the museum. According to the intentions of its founder, Luigi Pigorini, the purpose of this new institution was not only to gather together the remains of Italian prehistoric culture and the "primitive" cultures of other European and non-European peoples in a "central" museum located in the new capital of the Kingdom, but above all to support, promote and participate in research by palethnologists in Italy.

en.name: Palazzo Malvasia
description:
Initial contact began with the architect Alfonso Torreggiani in 1745. The following year, the Count engaged Giovanni Carlo Sicinio Galli Bibiena, son of Francesco and nephew of Ferdinando. The celebrated architects and stage designers worked for the most prestigious European courts. Giovanni Carlo left Bologna for Lisbon shortly after he projected the staircase of the Malvasia Palace.  
On a very small area (about 4x7 meters) the staircase is based on an oval plan. It is characterised by a single flight, which is very sinuous and dynamic, and by the presence of two mythological figures. The first one, representing Sisyphus is located on the right where the flight turns. The second figure, representing Athena, stands in a niche in the wall with two heraldic dragons at her sides. The statues are the works of the sculptor Filippo Scandellari, aided by Giovan Battista Canepa.  
The ceiling shows a particular solution, typical of Bolognese baroque architecture. Containing a ‘sfondato' or “chamber of light” (a space with windows not visible by the visitors), often painted, as in this case, and opened in its central part.

Very original in its shape, the staircase realised in the residence of the Malvasia family is one of the most representative creations of Bolognese late baroque architecture. It was designed by a member of the famous dynasty of theatrical architects and stage designers, Giovanni Carlo Sicinio Galli Bibiena; thanks to his ability in those fields the work is intended to astonish and involve the visitors, inviting them to start climbing the stairs and reaching the apartment of count Cesare Alberto.
artist: Architect: Giovanni Carlo Sicinio Galli Bibiena; sculptor: Filippo Scandellari; aid sculptor: Giovan Battista Canepa
history: Acquired in 1535, Count Malvasia restored a palace originally made for the Fantuzzi family located in Strada Maggiore. The restoration kept the original portico and built a new façade for the upper floors. Important work was intended to renew the interiors of the palace, made – or begun – around the mid eighteenth-century. From 1756 Count Cesare Alberto Malvasia, a member of the Bolognese Senate, was a patron to the work. He lived in this palace until 1761, when he moved to another residence projected and built under his supervision. The new palace was in a new style, inspired by Italian and Bolognese sixteenth-century architecture. The palace of Strada Maggiore was sold to Filippo Savini in 1771.
keywords: Residential architecture; Monumental staircase; Late baroque architecture, Bibiena; Malvasia; Alfonso Torreggiani; *Sisyphus*; Filippo Scandellari; Giovan Battista Canepa; *Athena*; Architectural sculpture
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: Palazzo Malvasia
description:
Dopo un primo contatto con l'architetto Alfonso Torreggiani nel 1745, il conte ingaggiò l'anno dopo Giovanni Carlo Sicinio Galli Bibiena, figlio di Francesco e nipote di Ferdinando, i famosi architetti e scenografi che avevano lavorato per le più prestigiose corti europee. Anche Giovanni Carlo, poco tempo dopo aver progettato la scala di Palazzo Malvasia, lasciò Bologna per Lisbona.  
Su un'area molto piccola (circa 4x7 metri) la scala si sviluppa su una pianta ovale; è caratterizzata da una sola rampa, molto sinuosa e dinamica, e dalla presenza di due figure mitologiche: la prima, che rappresenta Sisifo, si trova a destra della voltata della scala, mentre la seconda, che rappresenta Atena, sta in una nicchia scavata nel muro, con due draghi araldici ai lati. Le statue furono eseguita dalla scultore Filippo Scandellari con l'aiuto di Giovan Battista Canepa.  
Il soffitto mostra una soluzione particolare, tipica dell'architettura barocca bolognese: il cosiddetto 'sfondato' che consiste nel porre una “camera di luce” (uno spazio con finestre invisibili ai visitatori), spesso dipinta, come in questo caso, e aperta al centro.

Molto originale nella forma, la scalinata realizzata nella residenza della famiglia Malvasia è una della più interessanti creazioni dell'architettura bolognese tardo barocca. Fu disegnata da Giovanni Carlo Sicinio Galli Bibiena, membro della celebre famiglia di architetti di teatri e scenografi; grazie alla sua abilità in questo campo l'opera è fatta per stupire e coinvolgere il visitatore, invitandolo a salire le scale, raggiungendo l'appartamento del conte Cesare Alberto.
artist: Architetto: Giovanni Carlo Sicinio Galli Bibiena; scultore: Filippo Scandellari; aiuto scultore: Giovan Battista Canepa
history: Dopo aver acquistato nel 1535 un palazzo originariamente costruito per la famiglia Fantuzzi e posto in Strada Maggiore, i Malvasia lo restaurarono mantenendo il vecchio portico e costruendo una facciata nuova per i piani superiori. Importanti lavori, intesi a rinnovare l'interno del palazzo vennero intrapresi, o almeno iniziati, attorno alla metà del XVIII secolo. Furono commissionati dal conte Cesare Alberto, dal 1756 membro del Senato  Bolognese, in occasione delle sue nozze con Ginevra Gozzadini, nel 1745. Cesare visse in questo palazzo fino al 1761, quando si trasferì in un'altra residenza progettata e costruita sotto la sua supervisione in un nuovo stile, ispirato all'architettura italiana a bolognese del XVI secolo. Il palazzo di Strada Maggiore fu allora venduto a Filippo Savini, nel 1771.
keywords: Architettura residenziale; Scalone monumentale; Architettura tardo barocca, Bibiena; Malvasia; Alfonso Torreggiani; *Sisifo*; Filippo Scandellari; Giovan Battista Canepa; *Atena*; Scultura architettonica

en.name: *Portrait of the Beneficiary Faustino das Neves*
description:
Strongly influenced by her father, Baltazar Gomes Figueira, and by painters such as Francisco Zurbarán, Juan de Roelas and Daniel Seghers, Josefa de Ayala worked in a small provincial centre outside Lisbon. Away from the court, and in a place where the medieval lifestyle was preserved, she related to the politics opposed to the Spanish Habsburg dynasty, supporting the Restoration cause of the Royal House of Braganza. The social life of this micro-society revolved around social gatherings and meetings in convents and noble residences. The noblemen – members of the Municipal Senate – religious orders, brotherhood and charitable institutions with whom she fraternized, were well-read and had no economic restrictions. In their homes were many works of art some of which were commissioned from local provincial artists.  
From as early as the 17th century, Josefa had several biographies written about her. Costa Meesen (1696) referred to her “cleanliness and aptitude” upon imitating “things from nature”. Writer Damião Froes Perym (1736) also praises her “skill, beauty, honesty and charm” and her moral virtues. In the 19th century, José Silvestre Seabra and Almeida Garrett made reference to *Portrait of the Beneficiary Faustino das Neves*, considering it the genre which best revealed the sensitive side of Josefa d'Óbidos. The piece got lost in time and in 1957 it was identified by Reis-Santos as the work of Josefa d'Óbidos.  
The artist perfectly captures the psychology of this distinguished man from Óbidos. His dark clothing and his vigorous look contrast with the luminosity of the white and beige of his face, accentuating the Counter-Reformation features of the piece. The male figure, accompanied by an angel announcing his death, is purposely decentralised relative to the axis of the composition. This is a peculiarity which enhances the formal skills of Josefa de Ayala thus allowing her to be included within the ranks of the best 17th-century Portuguese painters.

Josefa de Ayala skilfully conveys the psychology through the glance, gesture and pose of this distinguished man from the town of Óbidos. His dark clothing and vigorous look contrast with the luminosity provided by the white and beige tones of his face. The figure is accompanied by an angel announcing his death.
artist: Josefa de Ayala e Cabrera (Josefa d'Óbidos)
Workshop of Josefa de Ayala e Cabrera; regional 17th-century naturalist painting

pt.name: *Retrato do Beneficiado Faustino das Neves*
description:
Josefa de Ayala foi considerada, logo a partir do século XVII, o protótipo da cultura seiscentista nacional, sendo a sua obra muito valorizada no contexto mecenático da época e disputada pelas colecções aristocráticas. Nascida em Sevilha, viveu a maior parte da sua vida em Óbidos, povoação que cumpria os requisitos de corte de aldeia, pela sua nobreza activa e desafogada, defensora da causa de Bragança contra o domínio espanhol, pelas confrarias laicas e o senado municipal, pelas tertúlias literárias e as residências com obras de arte, para além da importância do seu património histórico.  
A sua obra revela uma forte influência de seu pai, Baltazar Gomes Figueira (1604 – 1674), *bodegonista* notável, de nível peninsular, e igualmente de Francisco Zurbaran (1598 -1664). Neste retrato do Beneficiado Faustino das Neves, Josefa d'Óbidos faz a apologia da figura e da vida deste seu contemporâneo. Com efeito, o retratado terá sido um personagem influente da sociedade de Óbidos, amigo da família Figueira e especialmente de Josefa. Sacerdote, letrado, com fortuna pessoal, foi Beneficiado em S. Tiago, irmão da Confraria das Almas da Igreja de Santa Maria, de Óbidos, irmão com cargos em várias mesas administrativas e provedor da Santa Casa da Misericórdia local, a quem legou todos os seus bens, após a sua morte, em 1689.  
Nesta composição mergulhada numa subtil atmosfera de claro-escuro, cuja luz mortiça esbate os contornos das duas figuras, distingue-se nitidamente o anjo, na metade esquerda da composição, que segura o punho de Faustino das Neves e lhe segreda a promessa de salvação, apontando para o clarão de luz redentora que representa o céu e rasga a escuridão em que ambos estão envoltos. Na outra metade, o retratado, sereno, de porte severo e vestes escuras, segura os Evangelhos na mão esquerda, como fundamento da sua vida. A forma como Josefa de Ayala logrou representar este personagem maduro, austero de costumes e digno representante do sistema contra-reformista, permite-nos considerar esta obra como um exemplo notável da retratística portuguesa do século XVII.

Neste exemplo notável da retratística seiscentista, utilizando com mestria a técnica do claro-escuro, Josefa d’Óbidos faz a apologia do Beneficiado Faustino das Neves, membro destacado da sociedade obidense, representando-o com trajes negros, empunhando a Bíblia, a quem um anjo anuncia a morte próxima, numa atmosfera contra-reformista.
artist: Josefa de Ayala e Cabrera (Josefa d'Óbidos)
Atelier de Josefa de Ayala e Cabrera; pintura naturalista regional do séc. XVII.

en.name: Bridal headdress (*Tepelak* – tas)
short_description: Jewellery worn on the head included diverse types of metal articles which served to support the hat or scarf and also had an apotropaic function in addition to their decorative one. Especially noteworthy head-pieces were *tepelaks*. These are headdresses of round form, sometimes slightly concave, abundantly adorned with chains, smaller or larger silver coins and with *trepkas* (tiny ornaments in diverse forms – round, leaf-shaped, rectangular, heart-shaped, etc.). *Tepelaks* used to be worn everywhere in Macedonia, particularly in the Kumanovo, Skopje, Gostivar and Gevgelija regions, as well as within Vlachs. This piece of bridal *tepelak-tas* was made by application of filigree technique. It is abundantly decorated with coins suspended on tiny chains.
keywords: Head-dress; tepelak; coin; coinage; currency; numismatics; tughra; marriage; wedding; fashion; costume

en.name: São Miguel Arcanjo (Parish Church)
names: São Miguel Arcanjo (Vila Franca do Campo Parish Church)
description: The Parish Church dates back to the time of D. Manuel I, though it has the appearance of a traditional mid-15th-century Gothic building. The main portal is in the form of a *canopied arch* ending in a foliate rosette, and there are four small columns on either side that continue into the *archivolts*. The capitals form a foliate ring and have highly developed abacuses. The complex bases are in the Flamboyant Gothic style.

ar.name: نزل قوزة (الشرنقة).
description:
أسس السلطان بايزيد الثاني نزل قوزة (المعنى الحرفي لكلمة قوزة هو شرنقة الحرير) كوقف ديني لتمويل تكيته في استنبول. ويتألف النزل من فناء مساحته التقريبية 45.90 x37.50 متراً، تحيط به غرف من طابقين إضافة إلى إسطبل من دور واحد يقع إلى جوار الجانب الشرقي. ويُرى على الجدران الخارجية أنساق مفردة من الحجر المربع المنحوت تتناوب مع أنساق مزدوجة من الطوب. وتحت النسق المزدوج المزخرف بأنياب كلب يوجد طوق من أعمال الطوب على شكل سلسلة مزدوجة تحيط بالجدران الأربعة للمبنى. وتتخذ نوافذ الغرف في الطابق السفلي شكل فتحات صغيرة، بينما نوافذ الطابق العلوي مستطيلة الشكل.  
  
يبدي المدخل الواقع في منتصف الجدار الشمالي، وكذلك الغرف المحيطة به، بروزاً إلى خارج الجدار. أما إيوان المدخل الذي تغطيه أقبية فهو بارتفاع طابقين، شأنه شأن الغرف المحيطة به، والمفتوحة على الإيوان عبر عقد في المنسوب السفلي.  
  
يوجد في وسط الفناء مبنى لمسجد ذي ثمانية أضلاع تعلوه قبة، ويرتكز على ثمان دعامات حجرية تتصل ببعضها البعض بواسطة عقود. ويمكن الدخول إلى المسجد عبر درج من الرخام.  
  
وهنالك 50 غرفة في الطابق الأرضي للنزل؛ حيث يغطي الغرف الواقعة في الزوايا أقبية قائمة الزوايا ذات ألواح، بينما يغطي باقي الغرف أقبية برميلية متعامدة مع الفناء. وثمة أروقة أمام الغرف وفي الجهات الأربع للفناء. وهذه الأروقة، المحمولة على أعمدة مربعة، تغطيها أقبية برميلية مبنية بشكل موازٍ للفناء. وقد تمَّ تحويل إحدى غرف الجهة الشرقية للنزل إلى مدخل للإسطبل. يوجد في الطابق الثاني 54 غرفة بما فيها تلك الواقعة على جانبي المدخل. ويغطي الغرف المحيطة بالمدخل، وكذلك تلك الموجودة في الزوايا، أقبية قائمة الزوايا، بينما جميع الغرف الأخرى مغطاة بأقبية برميلية، ويوجد في كل غرفة موقد. أما رواق الطابق العلوي فمسقوف بسلسلة من القباب تنتصب على أعمدة مربعة. وهذا الرواق، الذي كان مصنوعاً من الخشب حتى وقت قريب، أُعيد بناؤه في شكله الحالي من قبل 'جمعية محبي آثار بورسة'.  
  
مخطط الإسطبل غير منتظم؛ ويتألف عموماً من سلسلتين من المجازات رتبت على شكل حرف 'U' حول ثلاث جهات من الفناء. يغطي هذه المجازات أقبية برميلية.  
  
بالإضافة إلى الرسم المتكرر في السلسلة المزدوجة للزخرفة المحيطة بالجدران الخارجية للنزل، هنالك زخرفة تزين واجهة المدخل. ثمة نمط من الرسوم اللولبية تبدأ على ارتفاع 100 سم عن أرض المدخل وتحيط بفجوته الرئيسية والواجهة. كما يوجد في المسطحات المثلثية للعقود رسوم هندسية نجمية خماسية الزوايا وأشكال عديدة متشابكة مكوَّنة من بلاطات تركوازية منزَّلة داخل أخاديد محفورة في الحجارة. كذلك هناك سلسلة عريضة لشكل متكرر مصنوع من قوالب الصلصال المشوي يطوق الجوانب الثلاثة لجدار المدخل.  
  
ما زال النزل مستخدماً بوصفه سوقاً حتى اليوم.
keywords: أعمال الطوب؛ بايزيد الثاني؛ بلاطات؛ بورسة؛ تجارة الحرير؛ زخرفة هندسية؛ فن عثماني؛ نزل.

en.name: Koza Han.
description:
Koza Han, *koza* meaning literally 'silk cocoon', was founded by Sultan Bayezid II as a *waqf* (or pious foundation) to fund his *imaret* in Istanbul. The *han* (inn) consists of a courtyard measuring approximately 45.90 m x 37.50 m with two stories of rooms around its perimeter as well as a single-storey stable adjoining the eastern side. On the outer walls, single rows of ashlar alternate with double rows of brick. Below the double row of dog-tooth ornament, a band of brickwork in a double-chain pattern winds round the four walls of the building. The windows of the rooms on the lower level are slits (embrasures), while those on the upper floor are rectangular.  
The portal in the middle of the north wall and the rooms flanking it project outward from the wall. The portal *iwan* has panelled square vaults and is two-stories high. The rooms to either side are also two-stories high open onto the *iwan* through an arch on the lower level.  
In the centre of the courtyard is an octagonal kiosk-*masjid* supported on eight stone pillars connected to each other by arches. Beneath the mosque is an octagonal fountain with an additional pillar in its centre. The *masjid* is accessed by a marble stairway and is covered with a dome.  
There are 50 ground-floor rooms in the *han*. Those at the corners have panelled square vaults, while the others have barrel vaults oriented perpendicular to the courtyard. There are porticoes in front of the rooms and on the four sides of the courtyard. The porticoes, carried on square pillars, are covered with barrel vaults arranged parallel to the courtyard. One of the rooms on the east side of the *han* has been converted into the stable entrance. On the second floor, there are 54 rooms including the rooms on either side of the portal. The rooms flanking the portal and those in the corners are covered with square vaults while all the rest are covered with barrel-vaults. There is a fireplace in each room. The portico on the upper storey is covered by a series of domes supported on square pillars. Made of wood until recently, the portico was rebuilt in its current form by the 'Bursa Monument Lovers' Association'.  
The stable does not have a regular plan. In general it consists of two series of aisles arranged as a 'U' on three sides of the courtyard. The aisles are covered with barrel-vaults.  
In addition to the brickwork double-chain motif running around the outer walls of the *han* there is also decoration on the portal façade. A moulding in the form of a spiral begins about 100 cm from the floor of the portal and winds around the main niche and façade. In the spandrels of the arches are geometric designs with five-pointed stars and various interlacing motifs made up of turquoise tiles set into grooves carved in the ashlar. In addition, a large chain motif, made of mouldings of baked clay, winds round three sides of the portal wall.  
The *han* is still used today as a market.

The caravanserais built at a distance of a day's journey in the Anatolian Seljuq period were superseded by the *han*s (inns) built in the cities in the Ottoman period. These *han*s were sometimes named after the marchandise traded in them, such as Copper Han, Iron Han, Rice Han and Silk Han. Koza means silk cocoon and this *han* served the silk cocoon trade, and still serves as a market.
keywords: Han; trade; tilework; brickwork; geometric decoration; Bursa; Ottoman architecture; Bayezid II; silk trade.

es.name: Han (caravasar) Koza.
description:
El *han* Koza (*koza* significa, literalmente, 'capullo de seda') fue fundado por el sultán Bayezid II como *waqf* con el objetivo de financiar su *imaret* de Estambul. Consta de un patio que mide 45,90 × 37,50 m, rodeado por dos plantas de habitaciones y un establo de un solo nivel adyacente a la cara este. En los muros externos, una hilera sencilla de piedras sin labrar se alterna con hileras dobles de ladrillo con adornos de diente de perro. Debajo de ellas se aprecia una banda de ladrillos de doble cadena que recorre los cuatro muros del edificio. Las ventanas de las habitaciones del nivel inferior tienen forma de saeteras y las del nivel superior son rectangulares.  
El portal situado en medio del muro norte y las salas que lo flanquean sobresalen del muro. El *iwan* de entrada, de dos alturas, está coronado por bóvedas cuadradas recubiertas de paneles. Las habitaciones de los lados también ocupan dos plantas y dan al *iwan* a través de un arco del nivel inferior.  
En el centro del patio hay un kiosco-*masyid* octogonal que descansa sobre ocho pilares de piedra unidos por arcos. Bajo él hay una fuente octogonal con un pilar adicional en el centro. Al, *masyid*, que está cubierto por una cúpula, se sube por una escalera de mármol.  
La planta baja del *han* tiene 50 habitaciones. Las de las esquinas están cubiertas por bóvedas cuadradas con paneles y las demás tienen bóvedas de cañón perpendiculares al patio. Frente a las habitaciones hay pórticos, al igual que en los cuatro lados del patio. Estos pórticos, que reposan sobre pilares cuadrados, están cubiertos por bóvedas de cañón dispuestas en paralelo al patio. Una de las habitaciones de la cara este del *han* se ha convertido en la entrada de las caballerizas. En la segunda planta hay 54 habitaciones, incluidas las que están a los lados del portal, las cuales, al igual que las de las esquinas, presentan bóvedas cuadradas; las demás están cubiertas por bóvedas de cañón. Todas las habitaciones disponen de chimenea. El pórtico del piso superior está cubierto por una serie de cúpulas sustentadas sobre pilares cuadrados. Este pórtico era de madera, pero la Asociación Amigos de los Monumentos de Bursa lo modificó recientemente y le dio su forma actual.  
El establo es de planta irregular. A grandes trazos, consta de dos series de naves cubiertas por bóvedas de cañón dispuestas en forma de U en tres laterales del patio.  
La fachada presenta elementos decorativos, aparte del enladrillado con motivos de doble cadena que rodea los muros externos del *han*. A un metro aproximadamente del suelo comienza una moldura trenzada que rodea el nicho principal y la fachada. En las enjutas de los arcos se aprecian adornos geométricos con estrellas de cinco puntas y diversos motivos entrelazados compuestos en azulejos de color turquesa colocados en hendiduras talladas en la piedra. Además, una gran cadena moldeada en arcilla cocida rodea tres laterales del muro del portal.  
Este *han* funciona aún como mercado.

Los caravasares construidos a una distancia de una jornada durante el periodo selyuqí de Anatolia fueron reemplazados por los *han* ('hospederías') de las ciudades en el periodo otomano. Estos *han* a veces llevaban el nombre de los productos que se vendían en ellos, como el *han* del Cobre, el del Hierro, el del Arroz o el de la Seda. *Koza* significa 'capullo de seda', a cuyo comercio se dedicaba este *han*. Hoy en día sigue funcionando como mercado.
dates: 25 de *du l-qada* de 896 de la Hégira / 29 septiembre de 1491.
keywords: Han; comercio; azulejería; enladrillado; decoración geométrica; Bursa; arquitectura otomana; Bayezid II; comercio de seda.

fr.name: Han Koza.
description:
Han Koza (*koza* signifie littéralement “cocon de soie”) a été fondé par le sultan Bayézid II en tant que *waqf* (fondation pieuse) pour financer son *imaret* d'Istanbul. Le *han* (auberge) consiste en une cour d'environ 46 x 37,50 m entourée de deux niveaux de pièces et d'une écurie sur un seul niveau côté est. Sur les murs extérieurs, les rangées de pierres taillées alternent avec une double rangée de briques. Tout le long des quatre murs du bâtiment court un bandeau de briques à motif de double chaîne sous une double rangée d'ornements en dents-de-scie. Les fenêtres des pièces du niveau inférieur sont de simples embrasures hautes et étroites, celles du niveau supérieur de forme rectangulaire.  
Le portail du milieu du mur nord et les salles qui le flanquent sont en saillie par rapport au mur. L'*iwan* d'entrée, de deux niveaux de hauteur, est couvert de voûtes plates à arêtes. Les pièces figurant de chaque côté sont également hautes de deux niveaux et ouvrent sur l'*iwan* par un arc au niveau inférieur.  
Au centre de la cour se dresse un kiosque-*masjid* octogonal soutenu par huit piliers de pierre réunis par des arcs. Sous la mosquée se trouve une fontaine octogonale comportant un pilier central. On accède au *masjid* couvert d'une coupole par un escalier de marbre.  
Le rez-de-chaussée du *han* compte 50 pièces. Les pièces d'angles sont couvertes de voûtes plates à arêtes, les autres de voûtes en berceau orientées perpendiculairement à la cour. Elles sont précédées d'un portique à voûtes en berceau disposées parallèlement à la cour ; le portique court sur les quatre côtés de la cour et repose sur des piliers carrés. L'une des pièces à l'est a été transformée en entrée pour les écuries. L'étage compte 54 pièces, dont celles qui flanquent le portail et qui, comme les pièces d'angles, sont à voûtes d'arêtes, les autres étant à voûtes en berceau. On trouve une cheminée dans chaque pièce. Le portique de l'étage est couvert par une succession de coupoles reposant chacune sur quatre piliers. En bois jusqu'à récemment, ce portique a été reconstruit sous sa forme actuelle par l'Association des amis des monuments de Bursa.  
Les écuries ne présentent pas de plan régulier, mais consistent en deux séries de nefs disposées en “U” sur trois côtés de la cour et surmontées de voûtes en berceau.  
En dehors du décor à double chaîne en brique qui court sur les murs extérieurs, on remarque également celui de la façade du portail. Une moulure en spirale qui part de 1 m du sol environ tourne autour de la niche principale et de la façade. Dans les écoinçons des arches, des motifs géométriques d'étoiles à cinq branches et divers motifs d'entrelacs en carreaux de céramique émaillée turquoise ont été insérés dans des gorges creusées dans la pierre de taille. Par ailleurs, une importante moulure en terre cuite à motif de chaîne court sur les trois côtés du mur du portail.

Les caravansérails construits à une journée de voyage de Bursa dans l’Anatolie Seldjoukide furent supplantés par les *han* (auberges) construits dans les villes durant la période ottomane. Ces *han* portaient parfois le nom des marchandises vendues dans leurs murs, comme *han* de l’argent, *han* du fer, *han* du riz et *han* de la soie. Koza signifie “cocon de soie” ; ce *han* servait à ce négoce, et sert encore aujourd’hui de marché.
keywords: han ; commerce ; carrelage ; travail de brique ; décoration géométrique ; Bursa ; architecture ottomane ; Bayézid II ; commerce de la soie

tr.name: Koza Hanı.
description:
II. Bayezid tarafından, İstanbul'daki imaretine gelir getirmesi amacıyla inşa ettirilen Koza Hanı, yaklaşık 45.90 x 37.50 metre ölçülerindeki bir avlunun çevresinde iki kat halinde sıralanan odalar ile doğu cephesine bitişik, tek katlı ahırdan oluşmaktadır. Dış duvarlar, dönüşümlü olarak yerleştirilmiş bir sıra kesme taş, iki sıra tuğla ile kaplanmıştır. çatı seviyesindeki iki sıra kirpi saçağın altında, tuğladan bir çift zencirek şeridinin yapının dört cephesini de dolaştığı görülmektedir. Alt kat odalarının pencereleri mazgal şekilli; üst kat odalarının pencereleri ise, dikdörtgen şekillidir.  
  
Kuzey cephesinin ortasındaki taçkapı, iki yanındaki birer mekanla birlikte cepheden dışa taşıntı yapmaktadır. Ortada yer alan, üzeri aynalı manastır tonozu ile örtülü taçkapı eyvanı iki kat boyunca yükselmektedir. Taçkapının iki yanındaki mekanlar iki katlıdır. Alt kat mekanları birer kemerle taçkapı eyvanına açılırlar.  
  
Avlunun ortasında, birbirlerine kemerlerle bağlanmış kesme taştan sekiz desteğin taşıdığı sekizgen planlı mescid yer almaktadır. Mescidin altındaki sekizgen alan şadırvan olarak değerlendirilmiş ve bunun ortasına bir destek daha inşa edilmiştir. Mermer merdivenler ile çıkılan mescid bir kubbe ile örtülüdür.  
  
Hanın zemin katında 50 oda vardır. Köşe odaları aynalı manastır tonozu ile, diğer odalar ise, avluya dik uzanan beşik tonozla örtülüdür. Odaların önünde, avlunun dört kenarına da inşa edilmiş revaklar vardır. Kare şekilli payelerle taşınan revakların üzeri, avluya paralel beşik tonozla örtülüdür. Doğu kanadındaki odalardan birisi, hanın ahırına geçilen bir mekan olarak düzenlenmiştir. İkinci katta, taçkapının iki yanındaki mekanlarla birlikte 54 oda vardır. Taçkapının iki yanında mekanlar ve köşe odaları manastır tonozuyla, diğer odalar beşik tonozla örtülüdür. Her iki katın odalarında birer ocak bulunmaktadır. Kubbelerle örtülü üst kat revakı da, kare şekilli payelerle taşınmaktadır. Yakın zamana kadar ahşap olan üst kat revakı, “Bursa Eski Eserleri Sevenler Derneği” tarafından bugünkü şekilde inşa ettirilmiştir.  
  
Ahırın düzgün bir planı yoktur. Genel olarak bir avlunun üç kenarına “U” şeklinde yerleştirilmiş iki sıra sahından oluşmaktadır. Sahınların üzeri beşik tonoz ile örtülüdür.  
  
Hanın dış cephe duvarlarını dolanan, tuğla ile yapılmış bir çift zencirek şeridinden başka taçkapı cephesinde de süslemeler bulunmaktadır. Taçkapı zemininin yaklaşık 100 cm yukarısından başlayan burmalı kaytan silme taçkapı ana nişini ve cephesini çevrelemektedir. Kemer köşeliklerinde, kesme taşlar üzerine açılmış oyuklara yerleştirilmiş firuze renkli çini parçalarıyla beş kollu yıldızlar ve değişik geçmeler şeklinde geometrik süslemeler oluşturulmuştur. Ayrıca, pişmiş topraktan silmelerle yapılmış iri bir zencirek motifi taçkapı cephesinin üç kenarını dolanmaktadır.  
  
Han, günümüzde de çarşı olarak kullanılmaktadır.

Anadolu Selçukluları zamanında inşa edilmiş menzil hanlarının yerine Osmanlılar zamanında şehir içi hanları önem kazanmıştır. Bu hanların bazen, içinde ticareti yapılan malın cinsine göre Bakır Han, Demir Han, Pirinç Hanı ve İpek Hanı gibi adlarla adlandırıldıkları görülmektedir. Koza Hanı da ipek kozası ticaretinin yapıldığı bir handır. Yapı, bu özelliğini günümüzde de devam ettirmektedir.
keywords: Bursa; Han; Osmanlı mimarisi; Ticaret; Çini; Tuğla süsleme; geometrik bezeme; II. Bayezid; Pulad Şah Oğlu Abdülali

en.name: *Bouquet of flowers abat-jours*
description: Two lampshades in lost-wax moulded clear glass with a light amber patina. The decoration is in the form of a bouquet of poppies, daisies, hydrangeas and clematis.

en.name: Castle of Calatubo
description:
The castle stands on a majestic rock, dominating the landscape consisting of a broad valley cultivated with vines, facing the sea and isolated by the low hills, which decline gently towards the gulf of Castellamare. The motorway passes nearby the rocky prominence, and has affected the views and the original countryside aspect in which Calatubo played a dominant role. Al-Idrisi does not lose the opportunity to describe it: “*Calatubo is a valid fortress and large village \[provided\] with vast territories, good for sowing and very productive. It is situated roughly four miles from the sea; it has a harbour where much wheat is loaded equally with other grains*” (tr.Amari, 1880-1881). The fortress of Calatubo served for centuries as the centre of harvests and sorting of agricultural products of the whole western side of the Val di Mazara, being provided with its own natural port of call. The settlement of Alcamo was closely linked to this, originating as an agricultural and commercial centre in the place of an ancient station placed along the Roman consular road that led from Palermo to Trapani. Calatubo, near to the valley of the homonymous torrent, was known in the times of the Arabs as *Qal‘at Awib* and during the Norman period as *Calatub* (diploma of 1093) and as *Calathubi* (diploma of 1110). The castle, built entirely of local grey calcareous stone in the opus incertum technique, developed at two levels round two courtyards following the irregular borders of the ground on which it lay. Access to the stronghold was obtained by passing across a slightly sloping flight of steps the raised sides of which are still marked by blocks of square stone. There were intervals which interrupted the irregularly shaped wall with two square towers placed as safeguards at the front of the entrance, while two other small 18th-century towers rose on a rocky spur  
overlooking one of the courtyards, below which was the cistern adjacent to a vast system of canalisation. The lowest level of the buildings contained farms and warehouses, the stables and places destined for housing, the level above ending with a small church covered with cross vaults, erected on the upper part of the rock. The castle, under private ownership now, is in a state of abandon and without a roof.

es.name: Castillo de Calatubo
description: El Castillo se alza sobre un peñón majestuoso que domina el paisaje de un amplio valle cultivado de vides, asomado al mar y aislado entre las bajas colinas que se van degradando suavemente hacia el golfo de Castellammare. La autopista, que pasa cerca del saliente rocoso, ha modificado las vistas y el aspecto paisajístico original del que Calatubo constituía un elemento dominante. Al-Idrisi no deja de describirlo: “Calatubo es válida fortaleza y pueblo grande, de territorio vasto, bueno para la siembra y muy productivo. Está situado a cuatro millas más o menos del mar; tiene un puerto donde se viene a cargar mucho trigo al par que otros cereales” (trad. original al italiano de M. Amari, 1880-81). La fortaleza de Calatubo desempeñó durante siglos la función de centro de recogida y de clasificación de las producciones agrícolas de toda la vertiente occidental del Val di Mazara, estando provista de un puerto marítimo natural propio. A ella estaba estrechamente unido el asentamiento de Alcamo, nacido como centro agrícola y comercial en el lugar de una estación en la carretera consular de Palermo a Trapani. Calatubo, próximo al valle del torrente homónimo, se conocía en la época árabe como Qal‘at Awib y en la época del condado normando como Calatub (diploma de 1093) y como Calathubi (diploma de 1110). El Castillo, enteramente edificado en piedra calcárea local gris en *opus incertum*, está organizado en torno a dos patios, siguiendo los bordes regulares de la elevación sobre la que se alza. El acceso a la plaza se hacía por una escalinata en leve pendiente, cuyos peldaños están marcados ahora por bloques de piedra escuadrada. La muralla, de trazado irregular, estaba interrumpida por dos torres cuadradas para vigilar el frente de la entrada, mientras que otras dos pequeñas torres (del siglo XVIII) se alzaban sobre un espolón rocoso y daban a uno de los patios, debajo del cual estaba la cisterna unida a un gran sistema de canalizaciones. El piso más bajo de los cuerpos de fábrica albergaba las masadas y los almacenes, las cuadras y los lugares destinados a vivienda; el superior terminaba con una iglesita cubierta por bóvedas de crucería, erigida en la parte más alta de la roca. Actualmente, el Castillo, propiedad de un particular, está en estado de abandono y sin cubiertas.

en.name: *Capture of Christ*
description:
The canvas came to the Borghese collection due to the life annuity agreed in 1787 by Marcantonio Borghese with the sculptor Bartolomeo Cavaceppi, who gave a number of different pieces from his collection.  
The painting shows notable similarities to the *Capture of Christ* painted by Caravaggio (Dublin, National Gallery of Ireland), handling the same subject in a more balanced and composed manner. Bright armour that illuminates the scene contrasts with the central figure of Christ, dressed in red with his gaze lifted to the sky and his hands together, the only figure who is facing the viewer.  
The composition appears orchestrated with rhythm, suggesting a drama that is more theatrical than profound. The work shows the influence of the Caravaggesque language used by Bartolomeo Manfredi, focusing on a substantial simplification of the dramatic, artistic and moral implications of Merisi's painting. The Caravaggesque inventions thus became easier to spread and, reproduced in different contexts, they quickly became elements of “typical” painting, which in turn gave rise to the phenomenon of “Caravaggism”.  
This method, described as *Manfrediana methodus*, became widespread in Rome in the first decades of the 17th century, in particular among the ever-present colony of northern artists who came to new and prestigious commissions. Van Baburen, who worked with David de Haen on the decoration of a chapel in the Church of San Pietro in Montorio in Rome, was particularly able to mediate between the Caravaggesque lesson and the Baroque style of Rubens' work.
The Dutch painter arrived in Rome around 1617 and assimilated the *chiaroscuro* of Caravaggio's style. He had an important role in establishing Utrecht as a stronghold of the Caravaggesque style.
keywords: Dutch painting; Utrecht school; Caravaggio; chiaroscuro; theatre; movement; Rubens

it.name: *Cattura di Cristo*
description: La tela è pervenuta nella collezione Borghese attraverso il vitalizio stipulato nel 1787 da Marcantonio Borghese con lo scultore Bartolomeo Cavaceppi, che cedette diverse opere della sua collezione. Il dipinto presenta notevoli attinenze con la *Cattura di Cristo* dipinta da Caravaggio (Dublino, National Gallery of Ireland), di cui elabora il medesimo soggetto in chiave più equilibrata e composta. Alle lucide armature che illuminano la scena con i loro bagliori, si contrappone la figura centrale del Cristo dalla rossa veste, lo sguardo alzato al cielo e le mani intrecciate, unico tra i personaggi ad essere rivolto verso lo spettatore. La composizione appare costruita e orchestrata in modo cadenzato, così da suggerire una drammaticità più teatrale che profonda. L'opera risente dell'elaborazione del linguaggio caravaggesco operata da Bartolomeo Manfredi, indirizzato verso una sostanziale semplificazione delle drammatiche implicazioni di ordine artistico e morale proprie della pittura del Merisi. Le invenzioni caravaggesche diventavano così di più facile divulgazione e, riprodotte in differenti contesti, erano pronte a trasformarsi in elementi di una pittura “di genere”, che avrebbe dato luogo al fenomeno del cosiddetto “caravaggismo”. Questo metodo, definito appunto “Manfrediana methodus”, trovò larga diffusione a Roma nei primi decenni del XVII secolo, in particolare presso la consistente colonia di artisti nordici che vi soggiornava alla ricerca di nuove e prestigiose committenze. Van Baburen, in particolare, che lavorò con David de Haen alla decorazione di una cappella della chiesa di San Pietro in Montorio a Roma, seppe mediare la lezione caravaggesca con lo stile barocco proprio delle opere di Rubens.
Il pittore tedesco arrivò a Roma nel 1612 e si avvicinò allo stile chiaroscurale di Caravaggio. Ebbe un ruolo importante a Utrecht nel fondare una roccaforte dello stile caravaggesco.
keywords: Pittura olandese; scuola di Utrecht; Caravaggio; chiaroscuro; teatro; movimento; Rubens

en.name: Rug *l'ahmal n'ibouli*
description: Traditionally, Ait Ouaouzguite Berber rugs were flat-woven in natural white and brown wool with twining applied in the horizontal bands. In this rug, borders and horizontal bands are woven in knotted-pile technique in a palette of orange, red and yellow that is a result of the weavers’ exposure to urban weavings, Rabat carpets in particular. The tribe’s location on the trans-Atlas and trans-Saharan trade routes – through which goods moved from the Atlantic coast to Timbuktu (Mali) – made this cultural influence possible. These mixed knotted pile and flatwoven rugs were made long and narrow to conform to the room sizes typical of village architecture.
place: Morocco, High Atlas Mountains, the Berber, Ait Ouaouzguite tribe
keywords: Wool

en.name: Convent of São Francisco
names: Chapel of João Carneiro, Church of the Convent of São Francisco
description:
"The Church of the Convent of São Francisco is one of the oldest of Portuguese Early Gothic buildings, but its original structure is covered by magnificent carved gilded woodwork dating from the Baroque to the Rococo. In the midst is a small but highly important Manueline work, an architectural jewel: the chapel of the schoolmaster of Braga Cathedral, João Carneiro, also known as the Chapel of Redress.  
According to an inscribed stone, it was founded canonically in 1500, with one of João’s brother’s acting as the executor of his will. This highly influential family gave Portuguese politics a number of important figures at the time of the Discoveries, such as António Carneiro, who was the confidential scribe to D. João II and donatory of the Island of Príncipe. He was also Secretary of State to D. Manuel I, as was Pêro de Alcáçova Carneiro, who was also later Secretary of State to D. João III. Together with their brother Francisco Carneiro, they were responsible for overseeing trade with India.  
Stylistically speaking, the architecture of the church can be attributed to the circle of Diogo de Castilho, who, in about 1526, settled in the city of Oporto after marrying the daughter of a rich Basque iron merchant. He lived in Rua das Flores and only returned definitively to Coimbra in about 1535. The Biscayan master produced a solid and elegant structure, even though not in line with the latest trends.  
The painting on the high altar in oil on wood, representing the Baptism of Christ, now swathed in Baroque carved gilded woodwork, dates from the same period, c.1530. The master and his helpers, active in Entre Douro e Minho and Galicia, produced a series of works that were greatly influenced by Late Gothic work from the Flemish workshops in Ghent and Bruges. The donor of the painting, João Carneiro, is represented on the left, set back from the main scene as the river water is sprinkled onto the head of the Messiah." master produced a solid and elegant structure, even though not in line with the latest trends.
