tr.name: Kapı Kanatları ve Tokmağı.
description:
Cizre Ulu Cami'ye ait çift kanatlı kapının ahşap iskeleti, tunç plakalarla kaplanmış; pirinç çubuk ve levhalardan oluşan süsleme, demir çivilerle kapı iskeletine çakılmıştır. Kapının kenarını, yuvarlak başlı çivilerle tutturulmuş dörtlü yonca yaprağı motifli bir bordür dolanır. Kapı kanatları üzerinde her kanatta alt alta sıralanmış ve merkezinde on iki kollu bir yıldızın yer aldığı üç madalyon yer almaktadır. Bunların aralarına gelecek şekilde ise kanatlar kapanınca tamamlanan iki tüm ve iki yarım madalyon yerleştirilmiştir. On iki köşeli yıldızlardan oluşan madalyon ve geometrik motiflerin arasında kalan boşluklar, ajur (delik işi) tekniğinde rumi-palmet motifli plakalarla doldurulmuştur. Bu motiflerin zemininde eskiden kırmızı ve mavi renklerin kullanılmış olduğu ve böylece motiflerin daha belirginleşmesinin sağlandığı, kalan izlerden anlaşılmaktadır. Kapının iki dış kenarında görülen yarım ve çeyrek madalyonlar, bu geometrik düzenin adeta sonsuz bir biçimde uzayıp gittiğini göstermektedir. Kapı kanatlarının ortasına yakın bölümünde, tokmak takılacak iki bölüm vardır. Birbirlerine ortada yer alan bir aslan kafasıyla bağlanmış iki ejderin oluşturduğu tunç kapı tokmakları, kapı kanatlarına bu deliklerden geçerek sabitlenmiştir. Tokmak dökümle yapılmış olup üzeri kazıma tekniği ile süslenmiştir. Tokmağın ejderleri sivri kulaklı, badem gözlü ve kanatlıdır. Yılan pullarıyla kaplı gövdeleri helezon şeklinde düğümlenip, birbirleriyle bağlanan kuyruklarının uçları da kartal başlarıyla betimlenir.  
  
Kapının üstünde yer alan bronz döküm kabartma yazılmış sülüs hatlı kitabenin harflerinin bir kısmı eksik olduğundan tam olarak okunamamaktadır. çözümlenebilen bölümünde “Bizim büyüğümüz Ebul Kasım Mahmud Sencer Şah'a Allah kuvvet versin” yazmaktadır.  
  
Adı geçen Atabek, Cizre Atabeki olup, 1208-1241 yılları arasında hüküm süren Mahmud Sencer Şah olmalıdır.

Anıtsal camilerin görkemli kapıları, aynı zamanda cennetin kapılarını da simgelerler. Kapı üzerinde hükümdar adına yer verilmesi, sonsuzluğu simgeleyen geometrik bezemeler ve kapı tokmaklarındaki ejder ve aslan figürleri, Tanrı'nın ilahi kudreti yanında hükümdarın gücünün de ifadesidir.
keywords: Figürlü bezeme; Geometrik bezeme; bitkisel bezeme; tunç; ajur
materials: Kanatlar: ahşap (ceviz ve kavak), maden (tunç ve pirinç), ajur (delik işi) tekniği.
tags: Kanatlar: ahşap (ceviz ve kavak), maden (tunç ve pirinç), ajur (delik işi) tekniği.

en.name: Hush Khrayef
description:
The *hush* literally means the courtyard of the house, but vernacular language, using a current metonymy, uses it to refer to the whole house, saving the word *dar*, a commonly used term, to refer solely to the room. Situated in one of the historic centres of the town of Gabs, the old *manzel*, al-Menzel al-Qadim, which is characterised by its dense and tightly-knit urban layout, the Hush Khrayef was most probably built at the beginning of the 19th century. Although it resembles local houses in the traditional style that possess a semi-rural, oasian character, particularly in terms of its base made of large second-hand bonded stone, it is distinct for its elegance, its more elaborate architecture, and its relatively expensive construction materials. It also belongs to an Arabic-Mediterranean tradition: large residences with a central courtyard, designed to house extended patriarchal families.  
The entrance of Hush Khrayef was once certainly defended by a covered passageway, a *sabat*; witness the arches that flank the doorway, which are still visible. The doorway is enhanced by a freestone frame, of local *kadhal stone*, and features a unique door with its own gate. The hallway leads to a vast central courtyard, surrounded by a circular gallery featuring lightly curbed and horseshoe arches supported on columns cut from limestone, and Hafsid-type capitals. The amplitude of this patio, the size of which was quite common for this oasis region despite the tightness of the urban web, leads one to suppose that such a space must have served for activities following on from agricultural productivity, such as the drying of henna or of palm foliage used for making woven baskets, hats and fans.  
The central courtyard is as much a well of light acting as a light source as it is a thermic regulator. It also acts as a distributive link between the other spaces in the house. The bedrooms and living rooms open out, through double doors framed by freestone, on each of the three south, north and east sides. The main room possesses, just like those of the grand houses of the *medina*s of Tunis and of Sfax, a central recess, a privileged area, flanked by two side rooms.  
We know, thanks to two sale contracts spread over several dates, that the system of shared ownership shook and transformed the original architecture of this grand home, through dividing up the living space in order to create a sort of *wikala*, where rooms are let individually. Restoration work undertaken by the State allowed it to return to its original form, whilst at the same time building up new spaces to fit in with the new use for the *hush* as a centre for cultural activities.  
The service rooms on the west side formerly consisted of a kitchen, a store room or larder, latrines and shops; two shops opened out directly onto the street. Today, this whole section, which had completely crumbled, has been rebuilt as a vast exhibition hall.  
The roofing of the Hush Khrayef buildings takes the form of a terrace with ceilings made of palm or ordinary wood, combining local construction techniques with techniques known elsewhere in Tunisia. The Gabesian method consists first of attaching a number of joists made of palm stems which are cleaved onto the tie-rods of the walls, then a plank of plaited reeds or palm shafts (on top would go a bed of sand) and the whole lot would be covered by lime mortar. Renovation work has lead to the replacement of the palm wood with imported wood; nevertheless, several examples of this technique are still visible in some places where preservation was possible.  
Through its configuration, and the materials and techniques of construction used, the Hush Khrayef is a study of traditional architecture in which common Tunisian elements are mixed with elements from other countries that belong to the same cultural mentality.

es.name: Huch Jrayef
description:
El *huch* designa literalmente el patio de una casa, pero la lengua vernácula, con una usual metonimia, lo atribuye a la casa entera, reservando entonces la palabra *dar*, que es el término corrientemente utilizado, para designar la habitación. Situado en uno de los núcleos históricos de la ciudad de Gabes, en el antiguo Menzel (*el-menzel el-qadim*) que se caracteriza por un tejido urbano denso y cerrado, el Huch Jrayef fue edificado al parecer a principios del siglo pasado. Aunque es muy parecido a las viviendas tradicionales locales de los oasis semirrurales, sobre todo por sus basamentos de gruesos bloques de piedra reutilizada, se distingue especialmente por su elegancia, su elaborada arquitectura y sus materiales de construcción relativamente ricos. Se inscribe también en la tradición arabo-mediterránea de grandes moradas con patio central, concebidas para albergar a familias patriarcales extensas.  
La entrada del *huch* Jrayef debía estar ciertamente protegida por un paso cubierto (*sabat*), como testimonia el nacimiento de arcos aún visibles que flanquean la puerta. Esta aparece realzada por un marco de piedra tallada, en *kadhal* local, con un único batiente provisto de un portillón. El vestíbulo da acceso a un amplio patio central rodeado por una galería circular con arcos ligeramente quebrados y de medio punto, soportados por columnas talladas en la piedra caliza, así como por capiteles de tipo hafsí.  
La amplitud del patio, de dimensiones bastante corrientes en esta región de los oasis, a pesar de estar situado en un entramado urbano bastante cerrado, permite pensar que tal espacio debió de servir para algunas actividades agrícolas, como el secado de la alheña o de los pétalos de las palmas destinados al trenzado de los grandes cestos, sombreros o abanicos.  
El patio central, además de ser foco de luz, es un regulador térmico. Representa igualmente la zona de distribución de los diferentes espacios. Sobre los tres lados —sur, norte y este— se abren unas puertas con dos batientes, enmarcadas con sillares, que dan a las habitaciones. La habitación principal consiste, como en las grandes moradas de las medinas de Túnez y Sfax, en un hundimiento central, espacio privilegiado flanqueado por otras dos pequeñas habitaciones laterales.  
Gracias a algunos contratos de venta, de varias fechas, sabemos que el sistema de copropiedad fue cambiando la arquitectura original de esta gran morada, provocando la división del espacio habitable para hacer una especie de *wukala* o alquiler de habitaciones. Los trabajos de restauración emprendidos por el Estado han permitido restituirle su forma original disponiendo nuevos espacios compatibles con la reutilización del patio (*huch*) para actividades culturales.  
Los servicios de la parte oeste estaban formados por una cocina, una despensa, unas letrinas, unos almacenes, etc. Dos almacenes se abrían directamente sobre la calle. Hoy en día toda esta parte, totalmente socavada, está organizada como una amplia sala de exposiciones.  
La cubierta de los edificios del *huch* Jrayef está hecha a base de terrazas de techos de madera de palmera o de madera ordinaria, mezclando las técnicas locales de construcción con otras técnicas conocidas en Túnez. El método de Gabes consiste en disponer un conjunto de vigas de tallos largos de palmera sobre el engranaje de los muros; luego aparece un entablado de esteras de cañas o palos de palmeras; por encima, un lecho de arena y mortero de cal cubre el conjunto. Los trabajos de reestructuración han permitido reemplazar la madera de palmera, cuyo apresto se ha perdido, por madera importada; de todas formas han podido conservarse algunos testimonios de esta técnica en algunas zonas.  
Por su morfología, sus técnicas y sus materiales de construcción, el *huch* Jrayef es un conjunto en el que se integra la arquitectura tradicional, donde se mezclan los elementos locales con otros comunes a todo Túnez y otros países de la misma área cultural.

fr.name: Houche Khraïef
description:
Le *houche* désigne littéralement la cour de la maison, mais la langue vernaculaire, usant d’une métonymie courante, l’attribue à la demeure entière, réservant le mot *dar*, terme communément utilisé, à la chambre. Situé dans un des noyaux historiques de la ville de Gabès, le vieux *manzal*, el-Menzel el-Qadim, caractérisé par son tissu urbain dense et serré, le Houche Khraïef a été vraisemblablement édifié au début du siècle dernier. Quoique se rapprochant des habitations traditionnelles locales à caractère oasien semi-rural, surtout par ses soubassements en gros appareil de réemploi, il s’en distingue par son élégance, son architecture plus élaborée, et ses matériaux de construction relativement riches. Il s’inscrit aussi dans une tradition arabo-méditerranéenne: celle des grandes demeures à cour centrale, conçues pour abriter des familles de type patriarcal élargi.  
L’entrée du Houche Khraïef était certainement protégée par un passage couvert, *sabat*; en témoigne la naissance d’arcs encore visibles qui en flanquent la porte. Celleci est rehaussée d’un encadrement en pierre de taille, le *kadhal* local, et comporte un vantail unique pourvu d’un portillon. Le vestibule donne accès à une vaste cour centrale, entourée d’une galerie circulaire à arcs légèrement brisés et outrepassés, supportés par des colonnes taillées dans le calcaire, et des chapiteaux de type hafside. L’ampleur de ce patio aux dimensions assez courantes dans cette région oasienne, en dépit du maillage urbain serré, laisse penser qu’un tel espace a dû servir à des tâches qui prolongent les activités agricoles comme le séchage du henné ou des folioles de palmes destinées au tressage des couffins, chapeaux et éventails.  
La cour centrale est aussi bien un puits de lumière qu’un régulateur thermique. Elle représente aussi un espace de distribution entre les différents espaces. Sur les trois côtés sud, nord et est s’ouvrent par des portes à deux vantaux, encadrées de pierre de taille, les pièces d’habitation. La chambre principale comporte, comme dans les grandes demeures des médinas de Tunis et de Sfax, un défoncement central, espace privilégie, flanqué de deux chambrettes latérales.  
On sait grâce aux contrats de vente, échelonnés sur plusieurs dates, que le système de copropriété a bouleversé l’architecture originelle de cette grande demeure, entraînant le morcellement de l’espace habitable, pour en faire une sorte d’*oukala* louée à la pièce. Les travaux de restauration entrepris par l’Etat ont permis de restituer la forme première tout en aménageant de nouveaux espaces compatibles à la nouvelle affectation du *houche* à des activités culturelles.  
Les services sur le côté ouest étaient auparavant formés d’une cuisine, une chambre à provisions, des latrines, des magasins...; deux magasins ouvraient directement sur la rue. Aujourd’hui, toute cette partie, totalement effondrée, est réaménagée en une vaste salle d’exposition.  
La couverture des bâtiments du Houche Khraïef est en terrasse avec des plafonds en bois de palmier ou en bois ordinaire, mêlant les techniques locales de construction aux techniques connues ailleurs en Tunisie. La méthode gabésienne consiste à disposer un ensemble de solives en stipes de palmier refendus sur les chaînages des murs, puis un plancher de nattes en roseaux ou en hampes de palmes; par-dessus, un lit de sable et un mortier de chaux viennent couvrir le tout. Les travaux de réfection ont permis de remplacer le bois de palmier par du bois importé; toutefois, on a pu conserver par endroits quelques témoins de cette technique.  
De par sa configuration, ses techniques et les matériaux de construction utilisés, le Houche Khraïef est un condensé de l’architecture traditionnelle où se mêlent des éléments communs à la Tunisie et à d’autres pays qui appartiennent à la même aire culturelle.

en.name: Meatball
description: It is an arrangement created by the glass by the free-breaking technique. The work depicts an imagined glass making process, in which sand is placed into the top of two old mincer machines with the output of what seems like molton glass protruding from the ends.
keywords: Glass; Installation; Comtemporary
materials: Glass, sand; free sizing technique, hot glass editing
tags: free sizing technique, hot glass editing

ar.name: زجاجة كروية.
description:
زجاجة كروية ذات سطح سميك، مصنوعة من زجاج أصفر رمادي ولها فتحة صغيرة للصب. والزخرفة العميقة والمصقولة تشمل جسم الزجاجة بكامله. وتتألف هذه الزخرفة من إفريز رئيسي تتناوب فيه رصيعات تحمل صوراً لطاووس مع أخرى تحمل زخرفة نباتية. وهناك أفاريز أخرى أقل عرضاً تزين جسم الزجاجة بكامله. ويبدو أن السدادة المخصصة لإغلاق فتحة الزجاجة الصغيرة القصيرة قد فقدت.  
إن الزخرفة المتقنة الموجودة على هذه الزجاجة، وأسلوب الزخرفة، وأشكال الطاووس، تذكر إلى حد بعيد بالأوعية الكوارتزية النفيسة التي كانت تصنع في مصر في العهد الفاطمي، والتي وصلت إلى أوروبا بعد توزع الكنوز الفاطمية. لذلك فمن الممكن أن تكون هذه الزجاجة الكروية قد صنعت في معمل في مصر على يد عاملين ذوي خبرة بالأشغال الكوارتزية وزخرفتها. أما نوعية هذه الزجاجة فتدل على أن من طلب تصنيعها لابد أن يكون من أصحاب البلاد. ويشابه شكلها أوعية الخزف الكروية المعروفة بالأوعية " الكروية المخروطية ". لم يعرف شيء عن الاستخدام الأصلي لهذه الزجاجة، ولكن أغلب الظن أنها كانت تستخدم لحفظ شيء نفيس.

هذه القارورة الفريدة المصنوعة من الزجاج السميك، مُزيَّنة بإفريز محفور عميقاً، تتناوب فيه مثلثات ذوات أشكال زخرفية، مع عدد من الحيوانات والميداليات. اشتهرت مصر الفاطمية بصناعة الزجاج، ولاسيما بالأواني المصنوعة من الكوارتز التي كانت تحظى بتقدير كبير في أوروبا، حيث بقيت قطع كثيرة منها في الخَزْنات.
keywords: زجاج؛ زجاج من مصر؛ منقوش؛ مصقول؛ عهد فاطمي؛ مصر؛ زخرفة حيوانية؛ زخرفة مباتية.
partner: متحف الفن الإسلامي في متحف بيرغامون ، المتاحف الحكومية

de.name: Kugelflasche.
description: Kugelförmige Flasche aus dickwandigem , graugelbem Glas mit kurzer Ausgußöffnung. Der Körper wird vollkommen von tief eingeschnittenem und geschliffenem Dekor verziert. Er besteht aus einem Hauptfries, in dem mit Pfauen und mit Pflanzenmotiven versehene Medaillons abwechseln. Schmalere Nebenfriese zieren den Körper. Der zum Verschließen der kleinen kurzen Öffnung notwendige Stöpsel scheint zu fehlen. Der sorgfältige herausgeschliffene Dekor dieser Flasche und die Stilisierung sowohl der Pfauen als auch das Ornament zeigen eine Parallele zu den kostbaren Bergkristallgefäßen, die in fatimidischer Zeit in Ägypten entstanden und die nach Auflösung des fatimidischen Schatzes nach Europa gelangten. Es ist daher möglich, dass die Kugelflasche in Ägypten in einer Werkstatt entstand, in der eine Kenntnis der Bergkristallarbeiten und ihres Dekors vorhanden war. Die Qualität der Flasche spricht für einen höfischen Auftraggeber. Die Form erinnert an kugelige Keramikgefässe, die als „sphero-conical vessels“ bekannt sind. Über die ursprüngliche Verwendung gibt es keinerlei Hinweise, aber es dürfte sich um einen kostbaren Inhalt gehandelt haben, der in dieser Kugelflasche aufbewahrt wurde.

Diese einzigartige Flasche ist mit einem tief eingeritzten Fries versehen, in dem Dreiecke mit ornamentalen Mustern sich mit Vögeln in Medaillons abwechseln. Das fatimidische Ägypten war berühmt für sein Glas und insbesondere seine Bergkristall-Gefäße, die in Europa hoch angesehen waren, wo viele dieser Objekte in Schatzkammern erhalten blieben.
keywords: Glas; Glas mit Schnitt- und Schliffdekor; Glas auch Ägypten;  Ägypten; Fatimiden
partner: Museum für Islamische Kunst, Pergamon Museum

en.name: Spherical bottle.
description:
A spherical bottle made of thick, grey-yellow glass with a short opening. Its body is completely covered with decoration that has been cut and deeply engraved into its surface. The decoration consists of a main frieze in which medallions with peacocks and with plant-motifs alternate. Minor side friezes adorn the body. The bottle’s stopper, with which its short opening would have been closed, appears to be missing.  
The bottle’s carefully incised patterns, along with the stylisation of the peacocks and of the ornamentation, find a parallel in the exceptional rock-crystal receptacles that were made in Egypt during the Fatimid era, and which were brought over to Europe after the dissolution of Fatimid treasures. It is therefore possible that this spherical bottle was made by a workshop in Egypt that possessed the knowledge of how to work with, and decorate, rock-crystal. The bottle’s quality suggests that the person who commissioned its making was a member of the court. Its form is similar to that of spherical ceramic vessels known as a ‘sphero-conical vessels’. There is no available information regarding its past use, but, given its workmanship, it must have contained something equally precious.

This unique bottle of thick glass is adorned with a deeply cut frieze in which triangles with ornamental patterns alternate with birds in medallions. Fatimid Egypt was famous for its glass and especially rock-crystal vessels, which were highly esteemed in Europe where many survived in treasuries.
holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum
keywords: Glass; incision; vegetal decoration; animal decoration; Egypt; Fatimid; bird; carving; sumptuary art; rock-crystal
partner: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums

es.name: Frasco con cuerpo globular.
description:
Frasco globular de vidrio grueso color amarillo grisáceo, con boca estrecha y totalmente cubierto de decoración grabada. Esta decoración consiste en una gran franja en que alternan medallones, pavos reales y plantas, y dos franjas menores. No se conserva el tapón que cerraría el frasco.  
El pensado diseño grabado, junto con la estilización de los pavos reales y el resto de motivos decorativos, permite establecer un paralelismo con recipientes de cristal de roca del Egipto fatimí traídos a Europa tras la dispersión de los tesoros fatimíes. Es posible, pues, que este frasco globular se hiciera en alguno de los talleres egipcios que trabajaban el cristal de roca. Su calidad sugiere que se trató de un encargo de algún miembro de la corte.  
Su forma recuerda a un tipo de vasijas de cerámica denominadas “esferocónicas”.  
No hay información acerca de su función, pero, dado el cuidado con que está fabricado, su contenido debía de ser valioso.

Excepcional frasco de vidrio grueso adornado con una ancha franja de grabado profundo en que alternan motivos triangular con aves y medallones.  
El Egipto fatimí fue famoso por sus recipientes de vidrio y, especialmente, de cristal de roca, muy apreciados en Europa, en cuyos tesoros se conservaban numerosos ejemplos.
holder: Museo de Arte Islámico del Museo Pergamon
dates: Siglo V de la Hégira / XI d. C.
keywords: vidrio; tallado; decoración vegetal; decoración animal; incisión; Egipto; fatimí
partner: Museo de Arte Islámico en el Museo de Pérgamo, Museos Estatales

fr.name: Fiole à panse globulaire.
description:
Fiole à panse globulaire en verre épais d'une couleur gris-jaune présentant un goulot court. Le corps de la fiole est entièrement orné d'un décor taillé en profondeur et poli. Ce décor est constitué d'une frise principale de médaillons où alternent des paons et un motif végétal, ainsi que de frises plus étroites. Il ne semble pas y avoir de bouchon pour fermer le col, de dimensions réduites.  
La précision de la taille, la stylisation des paons et des ornements rapprochent cette fiole des précieux récipients en cristal de roche qui furent produits en Égypte à l'époque fatimide et arrivèrent en Europe après la dispersion du trésor fatimide. Il est par conséquent possible qu'elle ait été fabriquée en Égypte dans un atelier ayant une connaissance de la technique du cristal de roche et de son décor. L'objet étant d'une très grande qualité, le commanditaire devait faire partie de la cour. La forme rappelle les céramiques sphériques connues sous le nom de “sphero-conical vessels”. Il n'existe pas d'indications concernant l'utilisation primitive de cette fiole, mais elle contenait vraisemblablement un liquide précieux.

Cette bouteille unique en verre épais est ornée d'une frise taillée en profondeur dans laquelle des triangles à motifs ornementaux alternent avec des oiseaux dans des médaillons. L'Égypte fatimide était réputée pour sa verrerie, et particulièrement ses récipients en cristal de roche, qui étaient hautement estimés en Europe, où nombre d'entre eux sont conservés dans des trésors.
dates: Ve siècle de l’Hégire (XIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: verre ; décor taillé ; décor végétal; décor animal; Égypte ; fatimide
partner: Musée d’art islamique du Pergamon Museum (Museum für Islamische Kunst)

en.name: Gourd Growing
description:
This type of gourd, grown in Hit, Anbar Governorate, Iraq, is among a number of varieties of calabash or "bottle gourd" of different shapes and sizes that were historically used as multipurpose vessels, including water bottles and containers for agricultural produce including beer and wine, milk and other dairy products, honey or grains. Cut segments of these gourds could also be used to make kitchen utensils such as ladles and bowls. They have been cultivated in Africa, Asia, Europe, and the Americas for thousands of years for similar purposes.  
  
While the same gourds can be harvested young for consumption as a vegetable, if grown as containers or utensils they are left to grow for longer and harvested when mature. After harvesting, they are dried for several months until the outer shell becomes hard. The dried gourds are usually cut at the top to make an opening through which the seeds are removed and contents added for storage.
holder: Open Museum Initiative for Water Culture
keywords: gourd; calabash; container; vessel; utensil.
partner: Open Museum Initiative for Water Cultures

de.name: Huldigungssaal und Bibliothek
description:
Über der Haupteinfahrt befindet sich der Huldigungssaal, der von Joseph Amonte ausgemalt wurde. Die Wände und die Decke sind vollständig mit Fresken bedeckt. Das Gesamtprogramm orientiert sich an den Malereien im Festsaal von Schloss Troja in Prag. Die illusionistische Architekturmalerei folgt den Zeichnungen in Andrea Pozzos Vorlagenbuch *Perspectiva pictorum et architectorum*.  
Ein wenig westwärts befindet sich, durch ein Stiegenhaus getrennt und ein Stockwerk höher, die Bibliothek. Im Prunksaal stehen Buchregale vor marmorierten Wänden. Sie sind durch dazwischenstehende marmorierte Säulen voneinander getrennt. Die Decke ist in drei Teile geteilt, die Fresken stammen ebenfalls von Joseph Amonte. Die Themen sind theologisch – in der Mitte findet man eine Darstellung von Christus und Moses, die von Bildern in Medaillons umgeben ist. Auf ihnen sind Jesuiten-Märtyrer, Papst Benedikt XIV mit zwei Kardinälen und Fürsterzbischof Sigmund III von Salzburg mit einem Bischof und einem Abt dargestellt. Letzteres ist ein interessantes Detail, da es sich auf eine zeitgenössische Begebenheit bezieht. Der Fürsterzbischof von Salzburg wurde in demselben Jahr gewählt, als Amonte die Decke malte. Aber was hatte das mit einem Stift in der Steiermark zu tun? Steiermark befand sich kirchenpolitisch vom Mittelalter bis Ende des 18. Jahrhunderts unter der bischöflichen Herrschaft Salzburgs.
dates: Ab dem Jahr 1720 Bau des Nordflügels; 1740 Fresken in der Huldigungshalle; um 1753 Prunksaal der Bibliothek und Deckenfresken
place: In Nordflügel (über der Einfahrt) und westlich davon, durch ein Stiegenhaus getrennt
artist: Architektur: Bau und Barockisierung des Nordflügels: wahrscheinlich Johann Georg Stengg Huldigungssaal und Bibliothek Fresken: Joseph Amonte

en.name: Homage Hall and Library
description:
Above the main entrance there is the two storey Homage Hall. It was decorated by Joseph Amonte. Walls and ceiling are completely covered with fresco paintings. The overall scheme was inspired by the paintings in the festival hall of the Troja palace in Prague. The illusionistic architecture follows the drawings in Andrea Pozzo´s manual *Perspectiva pictorum et architectorum.*  
A bit westward – separated by a staircase and one floor higher – there is the library. In the state room there are bookshelves in front of marbled walls. They are separated by marbled columns from each other. The ceiling is divided into three parts and was painted by Joseph Amonte. The topics are theological – Christ and Moses are represented in the centre, they are surrounded by paintings in medallions representing Jesuit martyrs, Pope Benedict XIV with two cardinals and the Prince Archbishop Sigmund III of Salzburg with a bishop and an abbot. The latter is the most interesting detail of the painting as it relates to a contemporary occasion. The Prince Archbishop of Salzburg was elected in the very year when Amonte painted the ceiling. And what had he to do with an abbey in Styria? Styria had been since the Middle Ages until the end of the 18th century under the ecclesio-political rule of the Salzburg bishopric.
dates: From the year 1720: construction North wing; 1740: fresco paintings in the Homage Hall; around 1753: state hall of the library and fresco paintings on the ceiling
place: In the North wing (above the entrance) and in the West of it, both separated by a staircase
artist: Architecture: construction and baroquization of the North wing: probably Johann Georg Stengg Homage Hall and library fresco paintings: Joseph Amonte

en.name: Ouled Majid Mosque
description:
Ouled Majid is one of the townships or *qsur*s of the Taqyus agglomeration that al-Idrissi, a chronicler living in the 6th/12th century, spoke of. It has actually been abandoned in favour of a new town built alongside the tarmac road. The historic township is located north of the oasis. It still has houses that have nearly kept their entirety, with their palm tree-trunk roofs, their gates and doors, and even with their water supply which has never ceased to run indoors.  
The mosque, situated to the north-east of this agglomeration, is in architectural terms one of the most important in the state of Tozeur, although it is not structurally different from the other mosques in the Jrid, which have all been inspired by the Bled al-Hadar Mosque. It differs from the other mosques in terms of the shallowness of its courtyard and the portico, which limits itself to one side only. The tendency for shortening the courtyard between the minaret and the prayer hall would be adopted by a number of later mosques, which means that the Ouled Majid Mosque became a prototype, just like Bled al-Hadar before it.  
The Ouled Majid Mosque consists of a prayer hall and a courtyard, endowed on its northern side with a double portico. A minaret stands in the middle of this side.  
The minaret, situated at the centre of this northern side, is the oldest of all the minarets in the Jrid. It is worthy for having preserved the form of the minaret of the Bled al-Hadar Mosque, which disappeared but which we know of thanks to the detailed description left to us by Ibn Shabat. This square-based minaret has a trunk over 2 m. high, built of freestone. The body of the construction is of brick. Its lantern, *jamur*, which on each side features a twin-arch, is topped by four fluted domes. The flutes are regular in two of these domes, and streaked (striated) on the other two. The four-domed lantern, a design specific to the Jrid, is unique in the Muslim world.

es.name: Mezquita Ulad Mayid
description:
Ulad Mayid es uno de los pueblos, *ksur*, de la aglomeración de Taqyus, que el-Idrisi, cronista del siglo VI/XII, mencionaba. Actualmente ha sido abandonado, trasladándose en cierto modo a un emplazamiento más cercano al borde de la carretera asfaltada. La población histórica se encuentra al Norte del oasis. Conserva todavía las viviendas casi enteras con sus techos de troncos de palmeras, sus puertas e incluso el agua, que nunca ha dejado de correr en su interior.  
No se diferecia de las otras mezquitas más que por la débil profundidad de su patio, cuyo pórtico se limita a un solo lado. La tendencia a estrechar el patio entre el alminar y la sala de oración será seguida por numerosas mezquitas posteriores, lo que prueba que la mezquita de Ulad Mayid se ha convertido en un prototipo, como lo fue la mezquita Bled el-Hadhar.  
La mezquita de Ulad Mayid comprende una sala de oración y un patio provisto, por su lado norte, de un doble pórtico. En medio de ese lado se sitúa el alminar.  
El alminar es el más antiguo del Yerid y está situado en el centro de la parte norte del edificio. Tiene el mérito de conservar la forma del alminar de la mezquita del Bled el-Hadhar, que ha desaparecido, pero que conocemos gracias a la minuciosa descripción que nos ha dejado Ibn Chabat. Este alminar de base cuadrada presenta un tronco de más de 2 m, construido en sillar. El resto del cuerpo es de ladrillo. Su lucernaria (*yamur*), que lleva a cada lado una arcada geminada, está coronada por cuatro cúpulas acanaladas. Estos canales son regulares en dos de sus cúpulas y estriados en otras dos. La lucernaria de cuatro cúpulas, específica de la arquitectura del Yerid, es única en el mundo musulmán.

fr.name: Mosquée Ouled Majid
description:
Ouled Majid est l’une des bourgades, ksour de l’agglomération de Taqyus qu’el-Idrissi, chroniqueur du VIe/XIIe siècle a signalé. Elle est actuellement abandonnée pour un nouveau village établi au bord de la route goudronnée. La bourgade historique se trouve au nord de l’oasis. Elle garde encore des maisons presque entières, avec leur couverture en tronc de palmiers, leurs portes et même l’eau qui n’a jamais cessé de couler à l’intérieur.  
La mosquée, située au nord-est de cette agglomération, est sur le plan architectural l’une des plus importantes du gouvernorat de Tozeur, quoiqu’elle ne s’écarte pas structurellement des mosquées du Jérid, toutes inspirées de la mosquée de Bled el-Hadhar. Elle ne diffère des autres mosquées que par la faible profondeur de sa cour, dont le portique se limite à un seul côté. La tendance à rétrécir la cour entre le minaret et la salle de prière sera suivie par de nombreuses mosquées postérieures, ce qui prouve que la mosquée d’Ouled Majid est devenue un prototype, comme ce fut le cas, avant elle, de la mosquée de Bled el-Hadhar.  
La mosquée d’Ouled Majid comprend une salle de prière et une cour dotée, à son côté nord, d’un portique double. Au milieu de ce côté se dresse le minaret.  
Le minaret, situé au milieu du côté nord est le plus ancien de tous les minarets du Jérid. Il a le mérite de nous conserver la forme du minaret de la mosquée de Bled el-Hadhar, qui a disparu, mais que nous connaissons grâce à la minutieuse description que nous a laissée Ibn Chabat. Ce minaret à base carrée présente un tronc élevé à plus de 2 m construit en pierre de taille. Le reste du corps est en briques. Son lanternon, *jamour*, que porte sur chaque côté une arcade géminée, est coiffé de quatre coupoles cannelées. Les cannelures sont régulières dans deux de ces coupoles, striées sur les deux autres. Le lanternon à quatre coupoles, spécifique au Jérid, est unique dans le monde musulman.

ar.name: شكل ناقة
description: إن فخار ظفار Dhofar هو مثل المنطقة نفسها متميز تماما عن بقية البلاد من حيث الشكل والصانع والتقنية. وإن الفخار الظفاري يمكن تقسيمه بشكل واسع إلى قطع صلالة Salalah وقطع جمعت من قرى ساحلية في طاقة ومربط Taqah and Mirbat. والاختلافات الأساسية الملحوظة هي في نوع الصلصال المستخدم والأشكال المصورة. وإن هذه الناقة المصنوعة من الطين البسيط تم صنعها في قرى ساحلية في ظفار والتي تشبه الأشكال التي كانت تصنع قبل الإسلام. ولكن صانعي الفخار المحدثين لا يعطوا لا أهمية روحية ولا  دينية لاستخدامهم للأشكال القديمة. وإضافة لاستخدامها كقطع تزيينية فإن الأهمية الروحية و الدينية قد تلاشت منذ أمد قديم في الماضي.
dates: القرن الرابع عشر الهجري / القرن العشرين الميلادي
keywords: شكل ، ناقة ، طين فخاري / نضيج أو محروق ، ظفار
tags: شكل ، ناقة ، طين فخاري / نضيج أو محروق ، ظفار

en.name: Camel figurine
description: The pottery of Dhofar is, like the region itself, quite distinct from the rest of the country in terms of form, producer and technique. Dhofari pottery can be broadly divided between Salalah ware and the combined ware of the coastal villages of Taqah and Mirbat. The key differences noted are the type of clay used and the featured stylistic forms. The simple terracotta camel figures made in the coastal villages of Dhofar bear a resemblance to pre-Islamic forms. However, modern potters attach neither spiritual nor religious significance to their use of ancient forms. Beyond their use as decorative objects, spiritual and religious significance has long since been lost in time.
keywords: Figurine; Camel; Terracota; Dhofar

en.name: Church of Nossa Senhora da Conceição Velha
names: Portal of the Church of Conceição Velha
description:
The Church of Conceição Velha was granted to the Knights of the Order of Christ, who enlarged and enriched it to such an extent in the 16th century, that it became one of the most remarkable in Lisbon. The earthquake of 1755 left little standing other than the fine portal built shortly after 1518, so it is probable that some of the artists who had worked on the Mosteiro dos Jerónimos had a hand in it, under the direction of João de Castilho.  
The portal is composed of a central arch with two finely sculpted *archivolts* defining a *tympanum* and central pillar divided by a sculpted pillar. Two typically Manueline pillars with niches and *baldachins* depicting the Annunciation, flank the doorway. The fine sculpture of Nossa Senhora da Misericórdia shelters under her mantle, on one side representatives of the clergy, including a pope, cardinal and bishops, while on the other side are a king, queen and members of the nobility. This is clearly the work of a sculptor of the very highest quality, who remains unknown, but who certainly proved capable of representing the most essential elements of his theme by placing under the protection of the Virgin’s robe different social classes: on the one hand, ecclesiastic representatives, for instance a pope, a cardinal and various bishops; on the other hand, the emperor, kings and other members of the aristocracy.

cs.name: Kaple sv. Anny
description:
Kaple byla dokončena ještě před zahájením stavby nového kostela. Vystupuje  
z jinak hladké fasády východního křídla konventu a přiléhá k sakristii. R. 1639 zde byla zřízena krypta, kde je pochován také stavebník kláštera, probošt Plocar. Klenby i stěny kaple pokrývají iluzivní malby. Erby se vztahují k mateřskému klášteru v Brně-Zábrdovicích. Bohatě řezané retabulum z r. 1702 s obrazem Boha otce v nástavci rámuje gotickou sochu sv. Anny Samotřetí.

en.name: Chapel of St. Anne
description: The chapel protrudes from the otherwise smooth façade of the east wing of the monastery, adjoining the sacristy. In 1639 a crypt was built there to contain the tomb of Provost Plocar who commissioned the construction of the monastery. The chapel vaults and walls are covered with illusionary painting. The coats of arms are associated with the “mother” monastery in Brno-Zábrdovice. The richly carved retable from 1702, holding an image of God the Father, frames a Gothic statue of St. Anne.

en.name: The Beirut water factory
short_description: Located in the suburb of Dbayeh, this factory provided the daily water supply for all of Beirut. The company was founded in 1873 and the factory was first opened in 1896. The water was taken from the Nahr al-Kalb river and distributed across a large water network.
keywords: Water; Economy

ar.name: تشكيل  حيواني لقرن أيل
description: هذه المنحوتة النادرة ربما استخدمت أثناء التتويج الملكي. وهي تعمل كثقل موازن على قماش ربط لحمل سيف أو قمع لوضع البارود. وقد أنتجت خلال العصر المغولي والحيوانات ذات العيون المطعمة بالذهب محفورة على سطحها. والحيوانات في الوسط المحفورة هي من القطط والدببة أو nilgais (ثيران زرقاء).وهذا القرن هو مثال بارز للطراز الهندو- إسلامي للتمثيل التزييني. والأشكال الحيوانية ذات الطراز الخاص ربما مستمدة من تصاميم الكتب.
dates: القرن الحادي عشر الهجري / القرن السابع  عشر الميلادي
keywords: مغولي ، قرن

en.name: Staghorn animal composite
description: This rare stag horn sculpture would have been used during royal processions. It acted as a counterweight on the lace fabric used to carry a sword or a powder horn. It was produced during the Mughal period. Animals with gold-inlaid eyes are carved on its surface. The animals in the centre carving are felines, bears or *nilgais* (blue bulls). This horn is an outstanding example of the Indo-Islamic style of figurative representation. The stylised animal motifs are probably derived from book designs.
keywords: Mughal; horn

en.name: Bottle
description: With its clean lines and simple designs, this bottle has an almost minimalist aesthetic. Due to the complete weathering in numerous shining colours on a silvery ground, the wheel-cut details are difficult to see. The decoration on its perfectly shaped globular body consists of a simple band around the shoulder. Its circular footring was made by folding. On the pushed-in base is a pontil mark. Its long, cylindrical neck has four main horizontal bands of faceting between four plain minor bands. The uppermost minor band is next to the bottle’s rim. Some of the main bands have a type of diagonal faceting also noticeable on the geometrical relief-cut bottle in the Aga Khan Museum Collection. Like its relief-cut counterpart, this bottle was likely produced in Iran between the 9th and 10th centuries. However, bottles of a related shape are found well into the 11th century in this region.
materials: Glass, colourless, polychrome weathering; free-blown, wheel-cut, tooled, worked on the pontil
tags: free-blown, wheel-cut, tooled, worked on the pontil

en.name: Jédeida Bridge
description: The Jdeida Bridge, completed in 406/1016, was built under the order of Yussef Dey. 116 m. in length and 6 m. wide, it numbers seven equally sized arches supported on quite a high floor built along the entire length of the river, in such a way that the water keeps cascading down as it flows along. Following the Second World War, this bridge was partly torn down and carried away by the water; now only three arches remain, whilst the others have been replaced by a metal construction. A certain Shelebi, son of Yussef Dey, ordered for a summer residence to be built next to this bridge, whose charm and beauty was boasted about in the literature of the day.

es.name: Puente de Yedeida
description: El puente de Yedeida, terminado en 406/1610, se edificó bajo las órdenes de Yusuf Dey. Tiene unos 116 m de largo y 6m de ancho, y cuenta con siete arcos iguales dispuestos sobre un fondo bastante alto construido a lo largo de la ribera, de forma que el agua se diversifica en cascadas. Después de la II Guerra Mundial, este puente fue parcialmente arrastrado por las aguas y sólo quedan tres arcos. Los demás han sido reemplazados por una construcción metálica. Cerca de este puente, un tal Chelebi, hijo de Yusuf Dey, hizo construir una residencia de recreo, cuyo encanto y belleza fueron ampliamente alabados en la literatura de la época.

fr.name: Pont de Jédeida
description: Le pont de Jédeida, qui fut achevé en 406/1016, a été édifié sur ordre de Youssef Dey. Long de 116 m et large de 6 m, il compte sept arches égales établies sur un radier assez haut, construit sur toute la longueur de la rivière, de façon que l’eau y soit déversée en cascades. Après la Seconde Guerre mondiale, ce pont a été partiellement emporté par les eaux; il ne resta plus que trois arches, les autres ayant été remplacés par un édifice métallique. À côté de ce pont, un certain Chélébi, fils de Youssef Dey, fit bâtir une résidence de plaisance dont le charme et la beauté étaient largement vantés par la littérature de l’époque.

en.name: A battle between Algerian ships and ships of the Naples Royal Navy, which chased the Algerian ships and ultimately destroyed them by firing cannon shots on 17 May 1792
names: *Espressione di una caccia intrapresa a due Sciabecchi Algerini dalla Fragata di Sua Maestà Napoletana denominata Sirena, a dì 17 maggio 1792, nelle acque comprese fra le isole d’Jeres ed il Capo Tagliato, quale termina per distruggerli e sommergerli a colpi di Cannone nella spiaggia denominata Cavallara*
short_description: In the 18th century the Kingdom of Naples and the Regency of Algiers were among the countries that competed for the control of trading routes in the Mediterranean and that participated in privateering. Only in 1856, by the Declaration of Paris, did Great Britain and most of other major European countries (with the exception of Spain) declare privateering illegal. By the time, Algeria had already become a French colony. The French military occupation of Algeria had in fact started in 1830.

en.name: Dhow collection
short_description: The National Museum of Qatar holds, in its collection, a fleet comprising of 14 dhows. The growing collection includes a variety of traditional dhows, with several models dating to the early 20th century, as well as more recent replicas of traditional vessels. Originating from Oman, Bahrayn, India and Qatar, among other places traditional dhows represented include *jalbut* (small to medium sized), *shuw\`i* (medium sized, once used for fishing and coastal trade), *sanbuq* (largest type in the Arabian Gulf today) and *baglah* (traditional, deep-sea dhows once used for the long – haul transport of goods.)
keywords: Boat; ship; dhow; pearling; fishing; trade; transportation

en.name: Siamese diplomatic service
short_description: in 1861, Mongkut, the King of Siam, sent a diplomatic service to Paris, not in order to create an alliance, but to preserve their independence by sending messages of good will to various European sovereigns. Napoléon III organised a lavish reception at the Palais Fontainebleau, recalling the Siamese reception which Louis XIV received in 1684. This photo reveals the importance of the Siamese delegation (three ambassadors and ten attachés in their military dress) accompanied by the Abbot Larnaudie, interpreter for the Siamese court.
keywords: Diplomacy; colonies; Siam; France

fr.name: Ambassade Siamoise
short_description: En 1861, Mongkut, le roi de Siam, envoie à Paris une ambassade, non par désir d’allégeance mais par volonté de conserver son indépendance en donnant des messages de bonne volonté aux différents souverains européens. Napoléon III organise une réception somptueuse au palais de Fontainebleau, afin de rappeler l’ambassade siamoise reçue par Louis XIV en 1684. Sur cette photographie, on voit l’importance de cette délégation siamoise (3 ambassadeurs et 10 attachés d’ambassade, dans leurs costumes d’apparat), accompagnée par l’abbé Larnaudie, interprète à la cour de Siam.
keywords: Diplomatie; colonies; Siam; France

ar.name: مسجد ومدرسة الأمير صرغتمش.
description:
يحتوي هذا المبنى على مسجد ومدرسة وضريح. وقد خصصت المدرسة لتدريس المذهب الحنفي - أحد المذاهب السنية الأربعة - وأصبحت معقلاً لعلماء الحنفية وخاصة الفرس منهم، إذ يذكر المؤرخون تقرب صرغتمش من العلماء العجم وإجلاله لهم إجلالاً زائداً.  
  
الواجهة الرئيسية للمبنى هي واجهته الشمالية الغربية التي تطل على الشارع. تعلو قبة الضريح الطرف الجنوبي من الواجهة، وقد بنيت هذه القبة على غرار القباب السمرقندية، فهي بصليّة مطوّلة ذات رقبة طويلة وبنيت من الطوب وتتكون من قبة خارجية وأخرى داخلية. وتشتمل هذه الواجهة على المدخل، وهو عبارة عن جدار غائر يتوّجه عقد وقد سقف بنصف قبة في أسفلها مقرنصات ذات دلايات. ويشبه هذا المدخل مدخل المدرسة الطشتمرية (بنيت عام 782 هـ / 1381 م) في مدينة القدس. وتقع على يسار المدخل مئذنة رشيقة بارتفاع 40 م بنيت من الحجر. وتتكون هذه المئذنة من ثلاثة طوابق تتوّجها قمة منقوشة. ويزخرف الطابق الثاني المثمن كسوة من الحجر الأحمر والأبيض تحتوي على زخارف هندسية تتكون من خطوط متعرجة تأخذ شكل سلسلة متصلة من الرقم "7". وقد امتازت مآذن هذه الفترة باستخدام هذا الأسلوب الزخرفي الذي نجده مثلاً في مئذنة كل من جامع وخانقاه الأمير شيخو الواقعين بالقرب من هذا المبنى.  
  
ويتبع تصميم المبنى تخطيط المدارس المتعامدة أو ذات المسقط الأفقي صليبي الشكل، إذ يتكون المسقط الأفقي للمبنى من أربعة إيونات منظمة حول صحن مكشوف تتوسطه فسقية. ويشتمل إيوان القبلة (الإيوان الجنوبي الشرقي) على عناصر معمارية وزخرفية مميزة. هناك قبة ذات رقبة طويلة تغطي الجزء الأوسط من الإيوان. وهي تشبه تلك التي تغطي الضريح، ولكنها أقل منها ارتفاعاً، وكانت أقدم قبة مقامة فوق محراب مدرسة في مصر. وقد هدمت وأعيد بناؤها عام 1940 م طبقاً لشكلها الأصلي القديم. ويوجد على الحوائط الواقعة على جانبي المحراب بقايا إزار (وزرة) مكون من ألواح رخامية تحتوي على رنك الأمير صرغتمش وألقابه، كما يوجد لوح آخر يحتوي على زخارف مورقة وعناقيد وأوراق عنب. وقد نقل إلى متحف الفن الإسلامي في القاهرة تسعة ألواح من أزر حوائط إيوان القبلة.  
  
ويظهر في المبنى تأثيرات فارسية واضحة تتمثل في أشكال القباب، وفي زخارف أزر حوائط إيوان القبلة. هذا، إضافة إلى اهتمام المنشئ بالفرس وإكرامهم، مما يحمل على الظن أن مهندس المبنى كان فارسياً.

تقع بجوار جامع أحمد بن طولون، وقد أُنشئت على موقع كان ضمن مدينة "القطائع"، وتضم مسجداً ومدرسةً وضريحاً. وقد خُصِّصت لتدريس المذهب الحنفي. وتتميّز بقبتها البصلية، ذات الرقبة الطويلة، التي تعلو الضريح. وفي المبنى تأثيرات فارسية، في شكل القبة وزخارف إيوان القبلة.
artist: الأمير سيف الدين صرغتمش الناصري (توفي عام 759 هـ / 1358 م)، وهو أحد مماليك السلطان الناصر محمد بن قلاوون.
keywords: زخرفة نباتية؛ زخرفة هندسية؛ ضريح؛ عمارة جنائزية؛ عمارة دينية؛ مئذنة؛ مدرسة؛ مقرنص.
partner: Ministry of Culture,Supreme Council of Antiquities

en.name: Mosque and Madrasa of Amir Sarghatmish.
description:
This building contains a mosque, *madrasa* and a mausoleum. The *madrasa* was designated to teach the Hanafi School of *fiqh* – one of the four *Sunni* schools – and became a refuge for Hanafi Ulama, especially the Persians among them. Historians mention, in fact, that the patron, Amir Sarghatmish, was very close to Persian scholars and revered them to the point of excess.  
The principle (northwestern) façade of the building overlooks the street. A dome tops the mausoleum on the southern end of the façade. This dome was built in the manner of Samarkand (Persian) domes, as it is of an elongated bulbous shape, with a high drum, built from brick. It is composed of an outer shell and an inner one. The southern façade is composed of a portal within a recess, which is crowned by an arch, and topped by a semi-circular domed ceiling, below which are *muqarnas*. This entrance is reminiscent of the portal into Madrasa al-Tashtamuriyya (built AH 782 / AD 1381) in the city of Jerusalem. On the left of the entrance is a slender minaret built of stone whose height measures 40 m, and which consists of three stories crowned by a carved dome. The second, octagonal, storey is decorated with an inlaid casing of red and white stone that is arranged in a geometric pattern made up of zigzag lines that assume the form of a linked chain of V-shaped letters. Minarets of this period are distinguishable by this particular decorative style, a further example of which may be seen in the minarets of the Mosque and the Khanqah of Amir Shaykhu which are located close to this building.  
The design of the building follows the plan of cruciform, or cross-shaped, *madrasa*s. The floor-plan consists of four *iwan*s, arranged around an open courtyard, in the middle of which is a fountain. The *qibla iwan* (southeastern) is composed of singular architectural ornamental components. There is a dome with a high drum that covers the central section of the *iwan* and which, although it is lower, resembles the dome of the mausoleum. The dome in the *qibla iwan* is older than that in the mausoleum and is said to be the oldest dome on top of a *madrasa mihrab* extant in Egypt. It collapsed and was restored in 1940 to its original form. On the walls on the two sides of the *mihrab*, there are still remnants of revetment composed of marble panels containing the blazon and titles of the Amir Sarghatmish. There is another panel that contains leafy decoration and clusters of grapes and vine leaves. Nine panels of wall revetment from the *qibla iwan* were transferred to the Museum of Islamic Art in Cairo.  
There are clear Persian influences in the building, exemplified in the shapes of the domes, the decoration on the wall revetment of the *qibla iwan*, and of course the known interest of the building's sponsor in Persian arts and culture, along with his high regard for Persian people. These observations allow the assumption that the architect of this building was a Persian.

This monument is situated beside Ibn Tulun Mosque. The site once stood within the Tulunid city of Qata'i. The building comprises a mosque, a mausoleum and a *madrasa* to teach the Hanafi school of jurisprudence. Persian influences are evident in the mausoleum dome, which is bulb-shaped with a long neck, and in the ornamental components of the *qibla iwan*.
artist: The Mamluk Amir Sayf al-Din Sarghatmish al-Nasiri (d. AH 759 / AD 1358) sponsored the building; he was in the service of Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun.
keywords: Vegetal decoration; geometric decoration; mausoleum; funerary architecture; religious architecture; minaret; madrasa; muqarnas.
partner: Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities, Supreme Council of Antiquities

es.name: Mezquita y madrasa del Emir Sargatmish.
description:
Este conjunto arquitectónico dispone de una mezquita, una madrasa y un mausoleo. La madrasa estuvo destinada a la enseñanza de la escuela hanafí de jurisprudencia sunní y sirvió como refugio para los ulemas, sobre todo persas. Según cuentan los historiadores, el patrocinador tenía un estrecho vínculo con los eruditos persas y los veneraba exageradamente.  
La fachada principal está en el lado noroccidental y da a la calle. El mausoleo, que queda en el extremo sur de la fachada, está cubierto por una cúpula construida al estilo de Samarkanda (Persia), en forma de bulbo alargado y con un tambor alto de ladrillo; tiene una estructura exterior y otra interior. La fachada sur consta de un portal rehundido cubierto por una semicúpula sobre mocárabes. La entrada recuerda al portal de la madrasa al-Tushtumuriya (construida en 782 / 1381) de la ciudad de Jerusalén. A la izquierda de la entrada se eleva un esbelto alminar de piedra que alcanza los 40 m de altura y está compuesto por tres niveles coronados por una cúpula tallada. El segundo novel, de planta octogonal, está decorado con un revestimiento con incrustaciones de piedras rojas y negras dispuestas en zigzag que conforman una cadena con eslabones en forma de V. Los alminares de este periodo se distinguen por su peculiar estilo decorativo, como puede apreciarse en los de la mezquita y la *janqa* del Emir Shayju, cercanos a este edificio.  
El diseño del complejo sigue la estructura de las madrasas cruciformes. Consta de cuatro *iwan* alrededor de un patio con una fuente en el centro. El *iwan* de la *qibla* (sureste) está compuesto por singulares elementos arquitectónicos decorativos. La parte central del está cubierta por una cúpula de tambor alto que se parece a la cúpula del mausoleo, aunque esta es más baja. Es más antigua que la del mausoleo y, según se dice, es la cúpula de *mihrab* de madrasa más antigua que se conserva en Egipto. Se derrumbó y en 1940 se restauró a su forma original. En los muros laterales del *mihrab* se conservan vestigios de un revestimiento de mármol con el blasón y los títulos del emir Sargatmish. Hay otro panel de mármol decorado con hojas, racimos de uvas y parras. En el Museo de Arte Islámico de El Cairo se conservan nueve paneles provenientes del revestimiento del *iwan* de la *qibla*.  
El edificio muestra claras influencias persas, evidentes en las formas de las cúpulas y la decoración del revestimiento del muro de la *qibla*. El patrocinador del complejo era un amante de las artes y la cultura persas, y tenía un elevado concepto de los persas. Por tanto, cabe suponer que el arquitecto del edificio fuera persa.

Se halla junto a la mezquita de Ibn Tulun. El emplazamiento perteneció, en su día, a la ciudad tuluní de Qatai. El monumento posee una mezquita, un mausoleo y una madrasa donde se impartía la escuela hanafí de jurisprudencia. La cúpula del mausoleo tiene forma de bulbo y un tambor alto. La decoración de la cúpula y el *iwan* de la *qibla* presentan claras influencias persas.\]
artist: El emir mameluco Sayf al-Din Sargatmish al-Nasiri (m. 759 / 1358), que estaba al servicio del sultán al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun.
keywords: decoración vegetal; decoración geométrica; mausoleo; arquitectura funeraria; arquitectura religiosa; minarete; madrasa; muqarnas.
partner: Ministry of Culture,Supreme Council of Antiquities

fr.name: Mosquée et madrasa de l'émir Sarghatmich.
description:
L'ensemble regroupe une mosquée, une *madrasa* et un mausolée. La *madrasa* avait pour fonction l'enseignement du dogme hanafite de jurisprudence, l'une des quatre écoles sunnites, et devint un refuge pour les oulémas hanafites, dont un certain nombre étaient perses. L'émir était très proche de ces érudits et les révérait tout particulièrement.  
La façade principale (nord-ouest) du complexe donne sur la rue. Une coupole en brique surmonte le mausolée à son extrémité sud. En forme de bulbe étiré reposant sur un important tambour, elle est du style des dômes de Samarkand (Perse), et se compose en fait de deux coupoles superposées. La façade sud présente un portail en renfoncement couronné par un arc et surmonté d'une demi-coupole soulignée de *mouqarnas*. Cette entrée rappelle le portail de la *madrasa* al-Tochtomoriya (782 H / 1381 J.-C.) à Jérusalem. à sa gauche s'élève sur trois niveaux un fin minaret en pierre de 40 m de haut, couronné par un fleuron bulbiforme. Le second niveau de forme octogonale présente un appareillage de pierres blanches et rouges disposées en zigzag créant un effet de chaîne en V. Les minarets de cette période se distinguent par ce style particulier, comme ceux des toutes proches mosquée et *khanqa* de l'émir Cheikhu.  
Le plan du bâtiment est celui des *madrasa* cruciformes. Il se compose donc de quatre *iwan* autour d'une cour ouverte occupée en son centre par une fontaine. L'*iwan* de *qibla* (sud-est) fait appel à des éléments architecturaux décoratifs singuliers. Une coupole à important tambour recouvre la partie centrale de l'*iwan*. Plus basse que celle du mausolée, elle est du même style, mais serait la plus ancienne coupole de *madrasa* existant en égypte. Elle s'est effondrée et été reconstruite sous sa forme d'origine en 1940. Sur les murs des deux côtés du *mihrab* figurent encore quelques vestiges d'un revêtement composé de panneaux de marbre contenant le blason et les titres de l'émir Sarghatmich. Un autre panneau présente un décor de feuillages et de grappes de raisin et feuilles de vigne. Neuf panneaux de cet *iwan* de *qibla* ont été transférés au Musée des arts islamiques du Caire.  
Ce bâtiment témoigne d'influences perses, particulièrement évidentes dans la forme des coupoles, le décor de murs de l'*iwan* de *qibla*. Elles s'expliquent par l'intérêt connu de son commanditaire pour les arts et la culture perses. On peut imaginer que l'architecte était d'origine perse.

Ce monument est situé à côté de la mosquée Ibn Touloun. Le site était autrefois englobé à l'intérieur de la cité toulounide de Qata'i. L'édifice comprend une mosquée, un mausolée et une *madrasa* pour enseigner le rite hanafite de jurisprudence. Les influences persanes sont évidentes dans le dôme du mausolée, en forme de bulbe étiré à longue flèche, et dans les composants ornementaux de l'*iwan* du mur *qibla*.
artist: C’est l'émir mamelouk Sayf al-Din Sarghatmich al-Nasiri (m. 759 H /1 358 J.-C.), au service du sultan al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun, qui fit construire ce bâtiment.
keywords: décoration végétale ; décoration géométrique ; mausolées ; architecture funéraire ; architecture religieuse ; minarets ; madrasa ; mouqarnas
partner: Ministry of Culture,Supreme Council of Antiquities

en.name: *Paulines at Prayer*
description:
Their hands clasped in prayer, the Pauline brothers kneel on a paved balustraded terrace in a garden in front of a row of vases on pedestals with flowers in them, with palm trees behind them arranged in shortened perspective. The perspective of the composition, based on two intersecting linear scenes, shows the vision of the patron of the Paulines and St Paul the Hermit in a cave on the lawn. The vision of the Patron of the Paulines depicts the Virgin Mary, St. John the Baptist and the *Agnus Dei* with His leg curved around a flag with a cross.  
The use of perspective, accentuated by the row of classical pedestals, evokes an earlier style. The foreshortening decreases the depth of the scene and emphasises the initial pair of brothers and the first pedestal, which brings them closer to the front of the painting. The morphology and typology of the Pauline brother figures, St Paul the Hermit and the ornamental motifs on the vases together with the flowers in them, suggest a date of around 1740, being elements of the Baroque style. The work is in the style of the lay brother and painter, Ivan Ranger. Ranger, regarded as one of Croatia's greatest Baroque painters is most famous for his frescoes, which he painted in enormous numbers. Ranger was already a trained artist when he arrived at the Lepoglava monastery from Tyrol. The Pauline Order accommodated a number of lay brothers in their monasteries, comprising painters, sculptors, cabinet-makers and other masters of the arts and crafts. They produced works for the interiors of churches and monasteries in the monastery workshops.  
Lepoglava was the largest and most important Pauline monastery in Croatia. It was the main centre for educational and cultural learning, with a Latin grammar school and was the first Academy awarded the right to confer doctorates. The Paulines, together with the Jesuits, played a key role in promoting Baroque art and culture in Croatia.

The altarpiece, depicting the Pauline brothers in a garden praying in front of flower vases, is probably the work of the lay brother and painter Ivan Ranger, a trained artist who came from Tyrol. Ranger – who joined the Pauline Order in Lepoglava and remained there until he died – is regarded as one of Croatia’s greatest Baroque painters. He is especially famous for his frescoes, which decorate many Pauline interiors as well as other churches and monasteries. The Lepoglava monastery was the main centre of the Pauline Order. It had a grammar school and was the first Academy awarded the right to confer doctorates. Together with the Jesuits, the Paulines played a key role in advancing Baroque art and culture in Croatia.
holder: Diocese Museum of the Zagreb Archdiocese
place: Made in the painting workshop of the Pauline monastery, Lepoglava
artist: Painting workshop of the Pauline monastery, Lepoglava
keywords: Altarpiece; antependium; Pauline; Jesuit; workshop; Counter-Reformation; garden; education; religious schools; teaching

en.name: Madrasat Abu al-Fida
names: Madrasat Abu Al-Fida also known as Madrasat Al-Dabbagha
description:
This *madrasa*, built at the northern edge of the water reservoir, has well-preserved walls, up to 8 m high. Its tall minaret and the many projections and rejections of its outer walls make it an outstanding building in this part of the city. Although access to the *madrasa* is through the oblong side, the southern wall facing the reservoir has to be considered the main façade. At the base of the building, a row of rectangular openings flows into a canal running towards the west, which once provided the citadel and possibly other structures in the city with water from the reservoir. Accentuation of the protruding, middle, part of the wall is by two large windows at ground-floor level and a row of three smaller windows under the edge of the roof. In the middle of the wall surface, an inscription on a light-coloured limestone slab stands out from the dark-basalt wall. Three layers of various *spolia* – basalt, limestone, and fluted limestone – add to its peculiarity. The inscription mentions that al-Salih Isma‘il commissioned the *madrasa* and that the Sultan’s commander, Amir Shams al-Din Sunqur, donated the funds to build it in 622/1225–6. The *madrasa* followed in the *Hanafi* rite.  
The core of the building is an axial four-*iwans* structure. Accentuation of the longitudinal axis  
of 19 m is by way of the oversized 9 m-long south *iwan* with a prayer-niche that served as a mosque. Two side rooms belong to the original layout although they give the impression of  
a later addition. Traditional transverse arches support the flat-stone roof of the prayer *iwan* proper, whereas the small room to the east of it, and the two side *iwans* in the  
courtyard, are roofed with pointed barrel-vaults, unrecorded in any other religious building in Bosra and evidently inspired by the interiors of the recently erected towers of the citadel. The  
square mausoleum at the southeastern corner of the building was added at a later stage in 630/1232–3 as a final resting place for its patron. The mausoleum’s dome, which rests on an  
octagonal tambour, follows the example of other mausoleums, built profusely in Damascus and in other Syrian cities from the 6th/12th century, another reference to the imperial architectural  
tradition of the capital.  
Here also, the minaret on the mausoleum roof is a later addition. The upper floor is provided with twin arcaded windows on each side of the wall, apparently it too copied the minaret of Jami‘ al-‘Umari.

en.name: Fortifications
description:
From the Manueline period onwards, the importance of the Azores grew, due to a similar increase in the number of voyages to the Far East, Spain, America and Brazil. This led to the construction of fortifications: the Forte de São João on Monte Brasil, on one side, and the Forte de São Sebastião, at Porto das Pipas, on the other side, to protect the ports, population, and the fleets that guarded the seas. The vessels laden with merchandise were a tempting prize for pirates and privateers, who also sought logistical support and provisions in the Islands of the Azores before launching their attacks. In 1542, a plan was put forward to erect some settlements walls and bulwarks, but it was several years before these became effective, despite the warnings that Bartolomeu Ferraz made to D. João III in the following year, about the need to fortify the islands against French pirates.  
Later the Purveyor to the fleets took on the task of preparing the most suitable terrain both in Angra and Ponta Delgada, and construction of the Fortress of São Brás was underway by 1551.  
The engineer and architect, Isidoro de Almeida, designed the forts, assisted by Manuel Álvares. When French corsairs attacked Madeira, an expedition of highly qualified fortification experts was sent to the islands to provide advice. Pompeo Arditi and Tommazo Benedetto de Pesaro were in São Miguel in the spring of 1567 and then went on to the Islands of Terceira, São Jorge, Faial and Santa Maria.  
A general plan for the defence of the islands was put forward by Pedro de Maeda in 1577, and then another in 1592, by João de Vilhena. Although these constructions are outside the time frame fixed for this exhibition, it is nonetheless undeniable that they are the direct result of the navigations and maritime discoveries that are of particular interest to us here.  
The Court never ceased dreaming up new and more powerful forts. By 1590, elaborate projects had been drawn up as part of an overall plan by D. António de la Puebla, which was then carried out by João de Vilhena. The Italian fortification expert, Tiburzio Spanochi, designed the Fortaleza de São Filipe on Morro Brasil, in Angra, which took decades to build, only being completed in 1643. As this was the Restoration period, and Philip of Spain no longer ruled the fort, it was, therefore, named São João (St John), after the new Portuguese king, D. João IV.

en.name: Sunflowers frame
description:
From an inventory of the properties of Vincenzo Bargellini, these pendant frames made in 1750 were originally made for holding mirrors, today they hold pictures. They were shown at an exhibition in Bologna in 1935 on Bolognese eighteenth-century art. At that time the frame was still holding a mirror.  
No mention is made of these frames in Vincenzo Bargellini's letters to Venice to commission furniture. Therefore, it is believed they were made in Bologna by local craftsmen following Roman and Venetian models.  
The high quality of the work is evident in the rich and naturalistic decoration. The sunflowers are an allusion to a particular destination.  
A frame similar to this pair is held in the Pinacoteca Nazionale di Bologna; the evolution of this same style can be recognised in the frames made for the pictures by Marcantonio Franceschini exhibited in this same museum, made especially for the paintings in 1710–1711.

The extraordinary vivacity of this mirror frame testifies at a very early stage (1699) the great skill and the refined taste of Bolognese baroque carvers, who were looking at Rome and Venice for up to date ideas.  
The frame is dated and signed (JACINTO MONTEILTH FECIT1699). Unfortunately, there are no other occurrences of the carver’s name in objects or documents in Bologna. The style of the frame is similar to one in the Pinacoteca Nazionale of Bologna.
holder: Museo di Arte Industriale e Galleria Davia Bargellini
keywords: Frame; Bolognese carver; Monteilth; Sunflower; Floral decoration; Pendant; Woodwork; furnishing; wood; carving

it.name: Cornice con girasoli
description:
La cornice costituisce una coppia con quella che contiene il quadro con l'inv. 1924/77. Da un inventario dei beni di Vincenzo Bargellini compilato nel 1750 risulta che queste due opere erano delle specchiere, come suggerisce anche la presenza dei girasoli nel ricchissimo intaglio. Proprio con uno specchio la cornice in oggetto fu esposta alla *Mostra del Settecento bolognese*, tenutasi in Palazzo Comunale nel 1935.  
Poiché le cornici non compaiono nella corrispondenza che Bargellini inviava a Venezia per commissionare mobili, è verosimile pensare che siano opere precoci che testimoniano l'attività degli intagliatori barocchi bolognesi, probabilmente guidati dai modelli romani, ma soprattutto veneziani.  
La qualità dell'opera è ben evidente dalla ricchezza dell'ornato vegetale, che conserva un andamento naturalistico anche nell'elaborato intrecciarsi dei racemi.  
A queste cornici si può accostare un'altra conservata alla Pinacoteca Nazionale di Bologna; l'evoluzione di questo gruppo può essere riconosciuta nelle cornici delle opere di Marcantonio Franceschini, anch'esse conservate al Museo Davia Bargellini, la cui realizzazione coeva alle pitture è documentata negli anni 1710–1711.

La straordinaria esuberanza di questa cornice per specchio documenta, a date molto precoci (1699), la grande abilità ed il raffinato gusto barocco degli intagliatori bolognesi, aggiornati sulle novità romane e veneziane.
holder: Museo di Arte Industriale e Galleria Davia Bargellini
keywords: cornice; intagliatore bolognese; 1699; Girasole; Decorazione Floreale; Pendant; Intaglio in legno

ar.name: قطعة نقدية محفور عليها نقش الشهادة
description: نقش على هذه العملات نقش الشهادتين التي تقرأ  "" لا إله إلا الله محمد رسول الله"" إن القطع النقدية مثل تلك المعروضة هنا غالبا تستخدم لنقل هذه الرسالة. وفي القرون قبل الإسلام، 200 قبل الميلاد – 651 ميلادي فإن العديد من الحكّام والأسر الحاكمة والسلطات أصدرت قطعا نقدية التي كان يتم تداولها في عُمان والخليج العربي. والقطع النقدية التي صنعت في عُمان في الفترة 133-906 هجري / 751-1500 ميلادي أظهرت وسائل التعبير عن السلطة والمكانة والاستقلال. وإن الحكّام المحليين أصدروا عملتهم الخاصة اعتبارا من 174 هجري / 791 ميلادي. إن أتباع الإباضية (وهم فرقة إسلامية) أسسوا إمامات (وهي نظم حكم فريدة من نوعها تستند لانتخاب شخص يعرف بعلمه وتقواه) في عُمان وذلك في العام 132 هجري/749 ميلادي. والأئمة الإباضية أصدروا قطعهم النقدية الفضية الخاصة. وقد وجدت العديد من هذه القطع النقدية في المناطق التي استكشفت في عام 1422 هجري/ 2002 ميلادي في ولاية بهلاء.  تحمل القطع النقدية اسم  مصنع صك العملة "" عُمان"" وأسماء الحكام الإباضيين "" الخليل بن شاذان"" و"" رشيد بن  سعيد "" .إن الوجيهيين هم أسرة حاكمة محلية قادها يوسف ابن وجيه وهو حاكم سابق من البوسعيد  الذين حكموا عُمان والذين سيطروا على المناطق الساحلية الشمالية من عُمان خلال القرن الرابع الهجري / العاشر الميلادي وقاموا بإنشاء مدينة صحارفي مركز رئيسي من مراكز التجارة الدولية و قاموا بإنتاج عملتهم الخاصة.والقطع النقدية التي أصدرت من قبل الوجيهيين ،المشابهة لما هو مبين هنا ، حافظت على النقش العائد للعباسيين  المعياري مع إضافة اسم الحاكم المحلي أسفل النقش في الجهة المعاكسة.إن العديد من السلالات الحاكمة الإسلامية استمرت في إصدار العملات في وبجوار شبه الجزيرة العربية حيث كانت عملات اليمن وهرمز شائعة في شبه جزيرة عُمان اعتبارا من العام 493 هجري/ 1100 ميلادي وبعد عام 493 هجري/ 1100 ميلادي فإن العملات الذهبية الأيوبية من اليمن و الدنانير الفاطمية من مصر كانت تستخدم بانتظام في موانئ عُمان. والتجارة في جنوب شبه الجزيرة العربية تركزت في ميناء عدن اليمني ومن هناك فإن العديد من الدنانير الأيوبية وجدت طريقها لعُمان. وفي أثناء ذلك فإن ملوك هرمز (فيما يعرف اليوم بعُمان وإيران) تنافسوا على التجارة على طول ساحل إيران. وإن القطع النقدية الذهبية والفضية الهرمزية الصغيرة أصبحت العملة الأكثر أهمية في عُمان خلال هذه الفترة.

en.name: Coin Inscribed with Declaration of Faith
description:
The Declaration of Faith is one of the five pillars of Islam and provides a foundation for all other Islamic beliefs and practices. In translation, it usually reads, "There is no God but Allah and Muhammed is His Messenger".’ This message was often conveyed on coins such as the one shown in this exhibit.  
  
In the centuries before the arrival of Islam, 200 BC-651AD, many rulers, dynasties and powers issued coins that circulated in Oman and the Arabian Gulf. Coins made in Oman 133-906 AH / 751 - 1500 AD also demonstrated a means of displaying power, status and independence. Local rulers issued their own currency from as early as 174 AH / 791 AD.  
  
Followers of Ibadism (a branch of Islam) established an Imamate (a unique governing system based on electing a person known for his knowledge and piety) in Oman in 132 AH / 749 AD. The Ibadi imams issued their own silver coins, many of which were found in a hoard discovered in 1422 AH / 2002 AD in the Wilayet of Buhla. The coins carry the mint name "Uman", and the names of the Ibadi rulers " al-khalil bin Shadhan" and " Rashid bin Said".  
  
The Wajihids, a local dynasty led by Yusuf bin Wajih, a former Abbasaid governor based in Oman, took control of the northern coastal regions of Oman during the 4th century AH / 10 century AD, developing the town of Sohar into a major centre of international commerce and producing their own currency. Coins issued by the Wajihids kept the standard Abbasid inscription, with the name of their local governor added below the inscription on the reverse.  
  
Trade in southern Arabia centred on the Yemen port of Aden, from where many Ayyubid dinars made their way to Oman. Meanwhile, the kings of Hormuz (in modern- day Oman and Iran) competed for trade along the coast of Iran. Small gold and silver Hormuzi coins became the most important currency in Oman during this period.
artist: Issued by Nasr bin Ahmed Samani
keywords: Coins; Currency; Numismatics; Abbasid; Hurmuz

en.name: Carpet
description: Carpets, with designs of yellow geometric split-leaf (*rumi*) lattice on a red ground, are among the most popular classical Anatolian carpets. Carpets with this design are called “Lotto” or “Lotto-style” carpets from their appearance in a well-known altarpiece by the 16th century northern Italian painter Lorenzo Lotto. The earliest examples of Lotto-style carpets use what is called the “calligraphic” kufesque border with clearly denoted “letter finials” recalling *kufic* script. Later examples such as this one, probably from the late 16thor early 17th century, show a wide variety of borders based on repeating multi-lobed cartouches or elongated medallions. Most of the early Lotto-style carpets were woven in large sizes such as this exceptionally well preserved example.
holder: The George Washington University Museum and The Textile Museum
keywords: Geometric patterns; wool; kufic script
materials: Wool (warp, weft, and pile); knotted pile carpet; symmetrical knot
partner: The George Washington University Museum and The Textile Museum
